title: Economies of Scale
body: To the Editor: I believe that your reviewer missed the point of the Topo USA map on CD-ROM ("Magic Carpets for Armchair Explorations," Sept. 30). To a serious map devotee like myself (a geologist), having a detailed topographic map of the entire country on one CD for an affordable price is a miracle. Do you have any idea of the volume, weight and cost of the paper maps that this program replaces? The absence of buildings in the 3-D view is a gap that only city-mouse game players would notice. The 3-D view itself is really an instructional device to show the uninitiated how topographic contour lines on a 2-D surface depict 3-D surfaces.  MARC EDWARDS Houston, Oct. 6, 1999  http://www.nytimes.com

title: Escaping From Web Traps
body: To the Editor: While surfing your Internet site, I read the article about traps for Web surfers, describing several practices for leading the unsuspecting browser to advertisements, including "duplicitous banner advertisements that can be designed by graphics professionals to resemble ominous computer messages" -- banners that have been formatted to look like warning boxes but that contain embedded links to connect the viewer to another site. The insinuation that these practices are underhanded aside, I suppose that even The newyork Times must use all possible tools to fill its coffers: The advertising banner at the bottom of the page was a Windowslike alert box reading "Warning: Your tank is on empty."  REBECCA SIMONS newyork City, Oct. 7, 1999   http://www.nytimes.com

title:
METRO BUSINESS;
Fast-Growing Company
body: VoCall Communications Corporation, a provider of prepaid calling cards and Internet telephone service, was ranked as the second-fastest-growing telecommunications company in the nation by Inc. magazine. The magazine also ranked VoCall, in Mountainside, N.J., as the 17th fastest-growing private company in America. From 1994 to 1998, VoCall's revenues increased 6,400 percent, from $750,000 to $47 million. The company, begun in 1990, said it introduced the first prepaid phone card in 1992. It was also a pioneer of prepaid Internet telephony, the technology that allows Internet users to connect to traditional telephones or fax machines. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Microsoft Sued By Priceline
body: Priceline.com, which lets consumers bid on the Internet for plane tickets and hotel rooms, said today that it had filed a suit against the Microsoft Corporation, contending that Microsoft's new hotel service violates a Priceline patent. Priceline.com, based in Stamford, said it filed the suit in Federal District Court in Connecticut against Microsoft and its Expedia.com Web site. Last month, Microsoft began a service on Expedia that lets consumers name their price for hotel rooms. The suit also says that Microsoft violated the Connecticut Unfair Trade Practices Act. Priceline.com said it provided Microsoft with confidential information about its business while the two companies discussed a possible joint venture earlier this year. Priceline.com has three patents for its "name your own price" business, and 17 more are pending. The shares of Priceline.com fell $3.6875, to $72.25; those of Microsoft fell $1.50, to $91.0625. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Another Way to Get on Line Without Buying a Computer
body: Trying to get on the Internet without using a computer seems to be the current Holy Grail. The latest device to join the parade is the I-Opener from Netpliance. The I-Opener is a kind of portable Web TV. The unit does not need to be attached to a television. It is portable so it can be easily moved to any room with power and a telephone jack. It has a built-in 10-inch color L.C.D. screen. And it comes with a keyboard. But it does not receive television signals. "Our goal was to make getting on the Internet as simple as possible," said Kent Savage, president and chief executive of Netpliance, based in Austin, Tex., during last week's Internet World trade show in newyork. The I-Opener has joined the trend of providing a colorful array of choices to match your decor -- black, silver, blue, green and yellow. There are several pricing plans. For example, it is $199 to purchase with a two-year commitment, or $299 with a one-year commitment, for Internet service at $19.95 per month. For $399, you get unlimited email and some free limited Web services, including news headlines, sports and weather.   STEPHEN C. MILLER http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo

title:
NEWS WATCH;
I.B.M.'s Palette of Colors Shows a Big Expansion
body: It has been a long time since I.B.M. stopped requiring employees to wear dark suits and white shirts, but it is still something of a shock to see Big Blue producing computers in hues that include Mars red metallic, terra green metallic, eclipse blue metallic, lunar gray metallic, Sirius red, Andromeda green and Polaris blue. But those are the actual color options for I.B.M.'s new Thinkpad i-series 1400 portable computers, which were introduced this week. The 1400-series portables come in a traditional I.B.M. black case, but they have snap-on covers in what I.B.M. calls seven "bright but classy" colors. The covers cost $29.95 each. One can imagine using the black Thinkpad Monday through Thursday, then adding Mars red or Polaris blue for dress-down Fridays. In another design innovation, the new Thinkpad 1460 and 1480 models ($2,199 to $2,399) also have an illuminated keyboard that makes it easy to type in a dark meeting room or on an airplane at night.   PETER H. LEWIS http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Internet Users Step Into the World of van Gogh
body: Have you ever been so entranced by a painting that you wished you could enter its world of light, color, texture and artistic imagination? The Intel Corporation, the giant computer chip maker, is inviting Internet users to do just that -- virtually, at least. The company's free art gallery Web site (www.artmuseum.net) allows users to "enter" two of van Gogh's most famous canvases: "The Yellow House" and "The Bedroom." Using three-dimensional, computer-generated environments that are based on the paintings, viewers can look under van Gogh's bed, or study the paintings on his walls or even walk across the street from the house on Place Lamartine in Arles and see it as the artist may have seen it (and imagined it) as he walked home. "This is not just some technology stunt," said Ralph Bond, Intel's consumer education manager. "From an educational point of view, it is very compelling, especially for younger people."   MICHEL MARRIOTT http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo: Artmuseum.net offers a computer-generated, worm's-eye view, above, of van Gogh's "Bedroom," inset.

title: Corrections
body: An article in Circuits on Thursday about the ways that some Web site designers trick Web surfers referred incorrectly to one method of avoiding certain tricks. Programming created with Javascript can be avoided by disabling Javascript, not Java, through the user's Web browser. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEW YORKERS & CO.;
On Line All the Time, With Delivery to Match
body: As the holiday shopping season approaches, a new on-line store is preparing to offer free delivery of products including CD's, books, video games, snack foods and gift certificates from spas. The Web site, www.urbanfetch.com, which will begin providing the service on Friday, will deliver 24 hours a day to all of Manhattan and Brooklyn Heights in an hour or less by uniformed couriers. People without access to the Web may call (212) 981-3500 for the same service. The company plans to make its service available in six other cities from London to Seattle next year.   AARON DONOVAN http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
24/7 MEDIA SHARES RISE ON SPECULATION OF TAKEOVER
body: Shares of 24/7 Media Inc. rose 17 percent amid speculation that the Internet advertising company was in talks to be acquired by a larger rival, Doubleclick Inc. The newyork-based company's shares rose $6.875, to $47.375. Doubleclick rose $4.75 a share, to $136.625. In July, Doubleclick's chairman, Kevin J. O'Connor, said the company was seeking to buy more Internet advertising companies to expand ad sales that were now on more than 1,300 Web sites. 24/7 would be a good fit because it would add 150 Web sites to broaden Doubleclick's customer base and fend off rivals. Doubleclick is in talks to buy 24/7 Media for about $1.5 billion, the Silicon Alley Reporter Web site said. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MACROMEDIA TO BUY MAKER OF WEB-COMMERCE SOFTWARE
body: Macromedia Inc., a provider of tools for building Web sites, said yesterday that it was acquiring the closely held Andromedia Inc., a maker of electronic commerce software for the Internet. Macromedia said it would issue about five million shares of stock and $5 million in cash, worth about $280 million based on Wednesday's stock price. The stock fell $3.53125, to $51.4375. Andromedia, based in San Francisco, makes software that analyzes data about Web site visitors. It also allows Web sites to be customized based on data about the user. Macromedia, based in San Francisco, makes Dreamweaver software and the Shockwave player, a media playback device for Web content. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Ebay in Dispute With Listing Site
body: Ina developing dispute over Internet auction listings, the Web site Auctionwatch.com said this week that it would continue to provide lists of items for sale on the site of Ebay Inc., which has been trying to stop the practice. Auctionwatch.com is one of a handful of Web sites calling themselves auction aggregators, which allow visitors to search for items on many auction sites from a single search page. The site submits a visitor's query to the auction search functions of sites like Amazon.com, Yahoo and MSN, then compiles the results. Ebay began demanding several months ago that auction aggregators no longer list items for sale on Ebay. Kevin Pursglove, a spokesman for Ebay, said the company had contacted five or six aggregators, all of whom had stopped the practice. Auctionwatch.com, based in San Bruno, Calif., introduced its universal search function on Sept. 25. On Monday, the company said it would not comply with Ebay's demand. "From the time we've launched, we've had a tremendous response from consumers," said Rodrigo Sales, co-founder and chief executive of Auctionwatch.com. "We feel there's a real need here." http://www.nytimes.com

title: Yahoo's Revenue And Profit Rise
body: Yahoo Inc., the No. 1 Internet directory, said today that its third-quarter revenue more than doubled as both its audience and advertising sales rose. Yahoo reported net income of $14.9 million, or 5 cents a share, compared with $4.25 million, or 1 cent a share, a year earlier. Earnings a share, excluding costs from its acquisition of Broadcast.com, came to 14 cents a share, higher than the 9 cents a share forecast by analysts -- and even above the "whisper number" of 12 cents a share. Revenue rose to $155.1 million from $66.3 million a year earlier. Yahoo reported its earnings after the close of unitedstates trading. After hours, its shares rose as much as $7.25 on Nasdaq. During the regular session, Yahoo gained $2.4375, to close at $175.75. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
INTEL PAYING $500 MILLION FOR INTERNET EQUIPMENT MAKER
body: The Intel Corporation agreed yesterday to acquire Ipivot Inc. for about $500 million in cash as part of a move to use Ipivot's Internet traffic equipment to extend Intel's network equipment business. Intel, the world's leading maker of computer chips, also operates a networking business; it said the acquisition would help customers manage the huge volumes of Internet traffic generated by the rapid growth of electronic commerce. Ipivot, which is based in Poway, Calif., designs and manufactures Internet commerce equipment that can complement Intel's network equipment expertise in switches, routers and servers. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
INTERNET SERVICES COMPANY IN DEAL TO ACQUIRE TESSERA
body: IXL Enterprises, an Internet services company, agreed yesterday to acquire Tessera Enterprise Systems for $120 million. IXL, which is based in Atlanta, said the purchase of Tessera -- a provider of customer-relationship management systems based in Boston -- would give it advanced data warehousing and data-mining technologies. The acquisition will be the first in more than a year for IXL, which has more than 1,700 employees and 20 offices in five countries. The company posted revenue of $126.3 million in the last 12 months. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
INTRAWARE BUYING 2 CONCERNS TO WIDEN ON-LINE SERVICES
body: Intraware Inc., which helps its corporate customers research and purchase software over the Internet, agreed yesterday to acquire the closely held Bitsource Inc. and Internet Image Inc. for about $48 million to expand its on-line services. Intraware will pay $11 million in cash and stock for Bitsource, which has about 28 employees, and $37 million in cash and stock for Internet Image, based in Fremont, Calif. The addition of Bitsource, based in Sunnyvale, Calif., will enable Intraware's clients to manage their software licenses on line, while Internet Image will enable customers to distribute upgraded software to their computers. Intraware shares fell $1.5625, to $24.3125. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
PALM TO PALM COMBAT
body: Psion P.L.C. of Britain said it would introduce a new hand-held electronic organizer this month, offering Internet access through a mobile phone or wireless modem and linked to a free Internet-service provider. Psion is Europe's biggest palmtop producer but has not dented the supremacy of the 3Com Corporation's Palm series in the unitedstates. The company said its new product, the Revo, would sell for around $500. Alan Cowell http://www.nytimes.com

title: Siemens-Clarent Deal
body: The Clarent Corporation, a small maker of equipment that transmits telephone calls using Internet technology, plans to announce today that Siemens of Germany, one of the world's biggest makers of telecommunications gear, has agreed to incorporate Clarent's technology into its products. The deal appears set to give Clarent a boost against competitors like Lucent Technologies Inc. and the 3Com Corporation. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
Sept. 26-Oct. 2;
Amazon.com Opens Its Doors
body: Looking for more cash, Amazon.com opened its popular Web site to any interested merchant. Like most Internet retailers, Amazon loses lots of money. But by selling access to its 12 million customers, the retailer gains a new revenue stream without the costs associated with a warehouse of products. Merchants will pay $9.95 a month to be listed on the site. If they choose to have Amazon process credit card purchases, they will pay 4.75 percent of the total sale. LESLIE KAUFMAN  http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
INTERNET AD AGENCY ISSOLD FOR $690 MILLION
body: CMGI Inc. agreed yesterday to buy the Flycast Communications Corporation, an Internet advertising agency, for about $690 million in stock, CGMI's third acquisition of an advertising company in two weeks as it takes on the on-line marketing leader Doubleclick Inc. CMGI, an Internet venture capital company, will exchange 0.4738 share, worth $47.53, for each Flycast share. CMGI, which is based in Andover, Mass., and owns stakes in the Internet search services Yahoo Inc. and Lycos Inc., invests in start-up companies with the goal of taking them public or selling them. Shares of Flycast, based in San Francisco, surged 20 percent, climbing $7.50 each, to $45.50, in Nasdaq trading, while CMGI gained $2.1875 a share, to $102.50. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
Metro Business;
Internet Provider Expands
body: BiznessOnline.com, an Internet service provider based in Wall, N.J., has agreed to purchase a Connecticut-based competitor, NECAnet. NECAnet is a high-speed Internet access provider with 4,200 customers in Connecticut, Maine, Rhode Island and New Hampshire. It is expected to generate $1.2 million in revenue this year. The acquisition, for an undisclosed amount, will increase BiznessOnline's customer base to more than 30,000, the company said. http://www.nytimes.com

title: NEWS WATCH
body: So you want to check your email, but a computer isn't handy. Why not just pick up a telephone and have it read to you? A free service called Mytalk.com permits users to do just that. More than 100,000 people have signed up for the service (www.mytalk.com), which carries ads, since it began this summer, said Kevin Wray, director of Web strategy and programs for General Magic, the company that runs the service.  http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Dell Markets Desktops For Lovers of Web Music
body: Another hardware company has heeded the siren call of MP3. Reporting that nearly three-quarters of its customers say they're mad for downloading music files, Dell Computer has begun tailoring models of its Dimension computer for such buyers. The new Dimension systems, which start around $1,700 and climb from there as processor speeds and monitor and hard disk sizes go up, come bundled with Diamond's Rio 500 Walkman-size MP3 player. Since sound is of the essence, the company has beefed up the system with higher-quality speakers and a deeper-boom subwoofer so huge that a very small rock band could practically perform on top of it. Software by Musicmatch.com enables users to fill up the hard disk with gigabytes of tunes recorded from source material like CD's and cassettes or with music downloaded from the Web. The portable Rio 500 player comes with 64 megabytes of memory. By adding an additional 32 megabytes, the company says, the device can play downloaded music for more than two hours before it's time to run back to the desktop for a refill.   JOE HUTSKO http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo

title: Cheaper by the Web
body: To the Editor: The article "Untangling the Grocery Web" (Sept. 22) disparages on-line grocers. I beg to differ. I am a regular customer of netgrocer.com and have found prices there consistently cheaper than in Manhattan for diapers and cat food -- the two major bulk items I buy. There is no tax since it is in New Jersey, and I get my deliveries in two days.  SHIRLEY YONG newyork http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CMGI SHARES RISE AFTER BETTER-THAN-EXPECTED EARNINGS
body: Shares of CMGI Inc. rose more than 5 percent yesterday after the company, an investor in Internet ventures, posted better-than-expected quarterly earnings. CMGI gained $4.8125 a share, to $97.9375, as more than 10.2 million shares were traded. In a conference call after its earnings were released late on Monday, CMGI's chairman and chief executive, David Wetherell, said that the company expected vastly increased revenue in the fiscal year that began Aug. 1 as its portfolio of Web companies begins to generate significant revenues. The company, based in Andover, Mass., also said it planned to spin off its Altavista Internet portal, which it bought earlier this year from the Compaq Computer Corporation. CMGI plans to file documents for an initial public offering after the current quarter ends. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MURDOCH'S YOUNGEST SON IS NAMED TO AN INTERNET POST
body: The News Corporation has named James Murdoch, youngest son of its chairman, Rupert Murdoch, executive vice president in charge of a new worldwide Internet unit. Since 1997, James Murdoch, 26, has run News America Digital, a newyork-based unit that operates the company's Internet businesses in the unitedstates, mainly the World Wide Web sites for the Fox News and Fox Sports cable channels. Mr. Murdoch will also continue to oversee the News Corporation's music operations, which include a hip-hop label he started with some high-school friends and later sold to his father's company. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Intel Online Begins Web Hosting Service
body: The Intel Corporation started a subsidiary today that will operate corporate computing systems over the Internet. Intel plans to invest more than $1 billion in the new business, Intel Online Services Inc., which opened at a site near Intel's headquarters in Santa Clara, Calif. Intel said its initial customers included the e-Citi unit of Citigroup, Excite@Home Shopping Service, and NEC. Intel also said it was working with Web development companies including iXL Enterprises Inc., PricewaterhouseCoopers, Proxicom, Razorfish, US Interactive, and Uunet on the new venture. The on-line service, first announced by Intel in April, is the company's entry in the fast-growing market for so-called Web hosting. Such companies typically house and maintain a corporation's server computers at a remote site. By offering regular software updates, duplicate power sources and backup capabilities, Web hosts give their customers greater reliability and predictable costs for their operations. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Internet Issue Up 525% in Debut
body: Shares of Foundry Networks Inc., a three-year-old designer of devices to manage Internet traffic, rose more than sixfold yesterday in their first day of trading, the second-sharpest rise ever for a new stock. Analysts had predicted a scorching debut. The company is in a market that has been lucrative for investors and, unlike most new Internet businesses, is already profitable. Even so, the gains were stunning, giving the company a market capitalization of $8.7 billion. Foundry's shares closed at $156.25, up $131.25 from the offering price of $25. Slightly more than 5 million shares were offered, and trading volume topped 12 million on Nasdaq. The shares peaked at $166.56 in midafternoon. The only initial offering to have outpaced that 525 percent gain was the one of theglobe.com, with those shares jumping 606 percent from a $9 opening to $63.50 on its first day of trading last November. Foundry's arrival was more impressive to some analysts because its initial price was relatively high, with the price set at $25 by the underwriter, Deutsche Bank Alex. Brown. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
FREESERVE SHARES SLIDE
body: Shares of Britain's largest Internet access company, Freeserve P.L.C., slid 7 percent after it reported quarterly finances that were weaker than expected. Freeserve, which pioneered the subscription-free Internet sector, said losses widened to £5.23 million, or $8.61 million, in the first quarter of the year as expenses increased. But the company had a strong gain in subscribers, jumping 19 percent, to 1.41 million subscribers. Sales also increased, to £3.38 million, from £1.65 million in the previous quarter. Andrew Ross Sorkin http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
FRENCH NET BOOKSELLER ACQUIRED
body: France Telecom S.A. said it had acquired the Internet bookseller Alapage.com. Terms were not disclosed. France Telecom said in a statement that 600,000 visitors log on to Alapage.com's Web site each month, with orders reaching 14,000 items a month. Founded in 1987, Alapage.com has emerged as one of the leading E-commerce sites for French-language content. http://www.nytimes.com

title: COMPANY BRIEFS
body: NETMANAGE INC., Cupertino, Calif., a networking-software company, said it planned to buy the Internet software maker Simware Inc., Ottawa, for $28 million in cash to strengthen its electronic-commerce business.  EXIDE CORP, Reading, Pa., the largest maker of automobile batteries, agreed to buy a majority stake in Lion Compact Energy, Midland, Mich., a closely held developer of batteries, for $20 million. BORG-WARNER AUTOMOTIVE INC., Chicago, the world's biggest maker of automatic-transmission parts, plans to invest $65 million to build more turbochargers in Germany.  GE EQUITY, the private equity arm of General Electric Co., said it would invest at least $50 million in European electronic commerce as it seeks to expand its presence on the Internet and in related technologies. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Fidelity Plans Deal With Lycos
body: Fidelity Investment announced a partnership yesterday with the Internet portal company Lycos Inc. to provide Fidelity's customers with enhanced on-line services. The partnership links Fidelity, the huge Boston-based mutual fund and discount brokerage unit of the FMR Corporation, with one of the largest Internet on-line communities. The two companies are hoping to provide a one-stop investment site for Fidelity customers through a new on-line product called Powerstreet, which has been added to Fidelity's Web site at Fidelity.com. Powerstreet will allow investors to create personalized pages that will include on-line trading tools offered by Fidelity, as well as news and other content provided by Lycos. Lycos recently bolstered its financial content through a $78 million purchase of the financial information provider Quote.com, which offers investment data. Fidelity officials said Powerstreet was intended to benefit both active traders and the occasional on-line trader. http://www.nytimes.com

title: On-Line Grocer Appoints Chief Executive
body: Peapod Inc., an on-line grocer, said today that it had named an AT&T Corporation executive, Bill Malloy, as president and chief executive. Mr. Malloy, 46, was formerly executive vice president for AT&T's wireless operations. Mr. Malloy succeeds Andrew Parkinson, chairman and a co-founder of Peapod, as president and chief executive. He will also join Peapod's board. Peapod provides on-line shopping services in Chicago, San Francisco, Boston and five other markets through partnerships with supermarket chains, including the Kroger Company in Columbus, Ohio, and the Jewel Food Stores chain in Chicago. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Sony Sets Walkman With Computer Link
body: The Sony Corporation said today that it would start selling a Walkman that fits into the palm of a hand and downloads music from the Internet while protecting copyrights. The Memory Stick Walkman is intended to fight the proliferation of illegal music exchanges on the Internet and to create a new standard for portable audio players. The Walkman will cost $430 and requires a computer with Microsoft Windows 98 to transfer music. The Walkman uses technology to protect the record industry from the illegal copying and distribution of music over the Internet. Currently, music can be downloaded from the Internet free. Memory Stick users would pay for Internet music made compatible with Sony's encryption system but would not be able to download songs from free Web sites. A Sony spokesman did not explain what form the payments would take. Users of Sony's new Walkman would move music onto something called a Magic Gate Memory Stick -- a thumb-sized rectangular card that is inserted into the player. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
BY THE WAY;
Writing a Screen-Turner
body: Plenty of New Jerseyans have published novels. A. L. Sirois, who lives in Flemington, is one of the few whose novels appears solely on the Web. His first novel, a science-fiction tale called "Blood Relations," was "published" this month by the Cascade Mountain Publishing Web site. As a technical writer for Bear Stearns in Whippany, Mr. Sirois is comfortable with the electronic world, although he intended his novel for ink on paper. When it wasn't picked up by mainstream book publishers, he got in touch with a friend and fellow science-fiction writer who does Web publishing in Oregon. "There went the fantasy of big advances," Mr. Sirois said, but he added that electronic publishers are good about passing along royalties. Readers pay by credit card and download the text of a book of their choice; "Blood Relations" costs $3.50 from www.cascadepublishing.com. Mr. Sirios, who has published short stories and a children's book, also rendered the "cover" art for his novel. He says he will produce his next book with the Web in mind, adding links to biographies of his characters and 3-D renderings of space creatures. http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
ENGAGE TECHNOLOGIES AGREES TO BUY ADKNOWLEDGE
body: Engage Technologies Inc., an Internet marketing company controlled by CMGI Inc., agreed yesterday to buy Adknowledge Inc. of Palo Alto, Calif., for $193 million in stock to add customers and Web advertising services. CMGI, the unitedstates Internet venture fund company, will initially acquire an 85 percent stake in Adknowledge for $170 million in CMGI shares. Engage will acquire the remaining 15 percent of Adknowledge for $23 million in Engage shares. In the third step, Engage will issue $170 million in Engage shares to CMGI for the 85 percent stake in Adknowledge that CMGI bought in the first step. Adknowledge provides consulting and marketing software that helps advertisers plan and execute their ad campaigns. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
NETZERO, FREE INTERNET PROVIDER, SOARS ON FIRST DAY
body: Netzero Inc., which gives people free Internet access in exchange for agreeing to see on-line advertising, rose 82 percent in its first day of trading yesterday. The company, based in Westlake Village, Calif., rose $13.125, to $29.125. About 19.5 million shares were exchanged, making it seventh among the most active issues in the unitedstates. The company now has a market value of $3 billion. Netzero sold 10 million shares at $16 each yesterday, raising $160 million. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Corrections
body: An article in Business Day on Monday about Internet companies' use of stock options to attract freelance writers misstated the age of Rufus Griscom, editor in chief and chief executive of Nerve.com, one of those using the incentive. He is 31, not 28. The article also misstated a description his site has used about itself in the past. The phrase is "literate smut," not literary smut. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
YAHOO SITE IN CHINA
body: Yahoo Inc., the top Internet search service, said it would create an Internet directory site tailored for Web users in China, expanding its presence on the mainland even as the country moves to restrict foreign investment in its information technology. Under a joint venture with the Beijing Founder Electronics Company, a unit of Founder (hongkong) Ltd., the company will form Yahoo China, which will provide links to more than 20,000 Chinese-language Web sites and offer news, finance and technology information as well as email and instant messaging. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
$350MILLION INTERNET STOCK SWAP
body: The Internet venture fund company CMGI Inc., based in Andover, Mass., and Pacific Century Cyberworks Ltd., a high-speed Internet provider in hongkong, said they would swap $350 million in stock in CMGI's first investment in Asia. CMGI will take a 5.5 percent stake in Cyberworks, and Cyberworks is buying about a 3.5 percent stake in CMGI. CMGI also signed a letter of intent to become a tenant of the Cyberport, a technology park in hongkong that Cyberworks is building. Pacific Century Cyberworks is a unit of the closely held Pacific Century Group. Richard Li, a hongkong Internet entrepreneur, is a major shareholder in Pacific Century Group. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
I.B.M. AGREES TO ACQUIRE INTERNET SECURITY COMPANY
body: I.B.M. agreed yesterday to buy the Internet-security company Dascom Inc. for an undisclosed price to strengthen its on-line commerce business. Dascom, a closely held company with about 100 employees that is based in Santa Cruz, Calif., develops technology to help businesses safely connect computer systems to the Internet. "Security has been at the forefront of the discussion about E-commerce," said Megan Graham-Hackett, an analyst at S.& P. Equity Group who rates I.B.M. a "buy." She added: "It's definitely an area where they need to own that technology. They've probably discovered that." http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
SHARES OF TWO INTERNET COMPANIES SURGE
body: Shares of two Internet companies posted huge gains on their first day of trading after initial public offerings. Shares of E.piphany Inc., a San Mateo, Calif., company whose software is used in on-line commerce, opened at $39 on the Nasdaq Stock Market after pricing late Tuesday at $16 each. The shares closed at $45.1875 on volume of 9.5 million shares. That would give the company, with its 25.8 million shares outstanding, a market value of more than $1.1 billion. Shares of the second company, Kana Communications Inc. of Palo Alto, Calif., which makes software to manage large volumes of email, jumped $36.50, to close at $51.50. Earlier, the shares reached $58.50, giving the company a market value of $1.63 billion. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
SPRINT PCS TO BUY MOTOROLA PHONES FOR $250 MILLION
body: Sprint PCS, the wireless division of the long-distance carrier the Sprint Corporation, will buy more than $250 million worth of Motorola Inc.'s new digital wireless phones for its wireless Internet service. Motorola will provide phones like its new Startac model that let customers use Sprint PCS's digital wireless network to make calls and access the Internet, as well as make analog-signal calls in areas the digital network does not cover. The network serves 4,000 unitedstates cities and communities and has licenses to offer its service to 270 million people. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
CURRENTS: ON-LINE SHOPPING;
Taking Care Of the Basics
body: Rejoice, ye minimalist on-line shoppers. This month, Muji, the Japanese-owned chain of stores specializing in spare simplicity, whether in file cabinets or pencil cases, went on line. In 1980, Muji (the full name, Mujirushi Ryohin, means "No Brand Goods") opened its first store in Tokyo. Now, there are 260 stores, most in Japan, with 12 in England and 2 in Paris. The aluminum cart, above, is 17 by 17 inches and 15 1/2 inches high ($135); a version 29 1/2 inches long is $195. Prices include shipping to the 48 contiguous states. The site is www.mujionline.com. http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo (Niwa Studios)

title:
Metro Business;
Prodigy Updates Software
body: Prodigy Communications Corporation has released a new version of its software for use with the Windows operating system that it said is Year-2000 compliant. The new software, Prodigy Internet Version 5.0, includes Microsoft's latest Internet Explorer Web browser and Outlook Express, a program that allows users to send and receive email and news. The new software will bemailed to Prodigy customers later this month and is available to new customers immediately. Prodigy, an Internet service provider, is based in White Plains. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
A Program That Lets You Talk Your Way Around
body: Don't be alarmed if you find someone muttering "whisky, whisky, whisky" at their computer. They may be using Conversa Web, which allows users to run Microsoft's Internet Explorer Web browser with their voices rather than their hands. Instead of clicking on Web page links, Conversa Web users simply read them out loud. For graphics that provide links, the program generates miniature cartoon bubbles containing a number that is read aloud to make the link -- the company calls them "saycons." Simple spoken phrases like "go back" operate the browser's navigation commands. Conversa Web can be used only to operate the browser, not for dictation. Unfortunately, the idiosyncratic spellings frequently used in Web addresses (say, "kwik" for quick") make it impossible to enter them with normal speech. Instead users must spell them out using the military-style oral alphabet ("whisky" for "w," for example). Web addresses, after they have been entered orally or by typing them in, can be put on an oral favorites list and called up with a word of the user's choosing. Conversa Web 3.0 costs $59.95. It only works on Windows-based PC's with versions 4 or 5 of Internet Explorer.   IAN AUSTEN http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo

title: Nielsen Joining Internet Venture
body: The A. C. Nielsen Corporation, the world's leading market researcher, said today that it would buy 10 percent of Netratings Inc. for $12.5 million as the companies form a joint venture to measure Internet audiences worldwide. The venture, to be called A. C. Nielsen Erating.com, will measure on-line audiences in Europe, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa. Nielsen, which measures television viewing in countries outside the unitedstates and Canada, said it and Netratings would spend $50 million in the next two years to establish the on-line service. The company is looking to capture the measuring business overseas, where Internet use is growing faster in some countries than it is in the unitedstates. Nielsen will own 80 percent of the venture, while Netratings will own 20 percent. A. C. Nielsen was spun off from the Dun & Bradstreet Corporation in late 1996. Nielsen Media Research Inc., which also was spun off from Dun & Bradstreet, provides ratings data in the unitedstates and Canada. http://www.nytimes.com

title: America Online Near Record Growth
body: The Internet services giant America Online Inc. said today that its America Online and Compuserve on-line brands were on track to post record membership growth for the first quarter of 2000. The company said it expected its America Online service to exceed last year's growth, but did not provide details. In the fourth quarter of 1999, ended in June, the service added 685,000 new unitedstates members, up from 523,000 in the 1998 quarter. America Online has more than 18 million members worldwide. So far this quarter, its other Internet service, Compuserve, with a new software version, has added more than 300,000 subscribers in North America. Compuserve provides Internet access for more than two million members worldwide. The company, which is based in Dulles, Va., plans to extend its current $400 personal computer rebate program with PC manufacturers through the holiday season. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
PERSONAL FAVORITES;
JIM McDERMOTT, Co-founder, Stamps.com
body: Actually, I've been using the Internet a lot lately to solve one of our largest relationship problems -- my complete dislike of shopping in malls. Deb, my fiancee, just gives me a list and a price range and I hit the Web. My favorites are: Macys.com, Williams Sonoma, Shopping.com and Bluemountainarts.com. I am considering a membership in Gentlehints .com, which allows users to send anonymous emails to alert employees, friends and family that they have bad breath, body odor, dandruff, etc. http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo

title: Venture Planned for Wireless Internet Link
body: Expanding from cable modems to the airwaves, the Excite@Home Corporation announced a venture yesterday with Airflash Inc., a small private company based in Redwood City, Calif., to deliver Internet information using wireless links. Excite@Home, which was formed by the acquisition of the Excite Web portal by the At Home cable modem venture, has agreed to work with Airflash exclusively in developing wireless services, an Excite@Home spokeswoman said. "Our relationship with Airflash will accelerate our ability to partner quickly and effectively with wireless carriers to bring the best of the Web to their customers," Joe Kraus, Excite@Home's senior vice president for content, said in a statement. "These steps continue our focus on providing our customers with the best personalized content wherever they are by whatever means they choose." Excite@Home and Airflash, which is developing technology to deliver digital information without wires, intend to develop personalized information services for wireless communications carriers. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
MORE FREE NET SERVICE IN ITALY
body: Wind S.p.A., the Italian mobile phone company that began operations in March, signed an accord with Yahoo Italia to provide free access to the Internet, matching offers made by its larger rivals, Telecom Italia and Tiscali. Phone companies are promoting Internet use in an attempt to capture a share of Italy's rapidly expanding Internet market. In 1998 there were only 640,000 Internet users in Italy, but the number is expected to rise to 1.55 million by the end of 1999 and to more than 3 million by the end of 2000. Wind is 51 percent-owned by Enel S.p.A., Italy's 100 percent state-owned electricity company, with the rest split between Deutsche Telekom A.G. and France Telecom S.A. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
METRO NEWS BRIEFS: NEW YORK;
Imprisoned Serial Killer Is Punished for Art Sales
body: A convicted serial killer was sent to solitary confinement for two years yesterday for having his autographs and artworks sold on the Internet. The killer, Arthur Shawcross, who strangled at least 11 prostitutes in Rochester and cannibalized some of them, also lost the right to receive packages, buy items at the prison store and make phone calls while he is in solitary, officials said . Mr. Shawcross, 54, was also barred from arts and crafts programs at the maximum-security Sullivan Correctional Facility. Inmates are prohibited from running any kind of business in prison. The authorities suspended Mr. Shawcross's arts and crafts privileges a week ago when they learned that an Internet auction site, eBay.com, was auctioning items bearing his signature. "An investigation determined that Shawcross would mail the autographs and artworks from his cell to others and receive a fee for those items," the State Department of Correctional Services said in a statement. "The items then would show up for public auction on the Internet." Mr. Shawcross was convicted of the killings in 1991 and received a sentence of 250 years to life. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
INKTOMI TO BUY WEBSPECTIVE SOFTWARE FOR $106 MILLION
body: The Inktomi Corporation agreed yesterday to acquire Webspective Software, a maker of software used for Internet content distribution and tracking, for about $106 million in stock. Inktomi, a Foster City, Calif., provider of Internet search software and other products used to speed Web site performance, said the deal would help it offer Web site content management services to the Web hosting market -- concerns that rent computer capacity to companies and manage Web sites on their behalf. Webspective, of Needham, Mass., is a privately held company financed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Charles River Ventures, Morgenthaler Ventures and Cisco Systems Inc. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Garden.com Shares Soar
body: Shares of Garden.com Inc., which operates three gardening-related World Wide Web sites, closed yesterday nearly 68 percent above the offering price in its stock-market debut. Shares of Garden.com, which runs an on-line site for content, community and garden-related commerce, closed at $19.0625. The offering was priced at $12 a share, winding up in the middle of its expected price range. Garden.com's reception surprised some analysts, since recent Internet issues focusing on consumer electronic commerce have not fared as well. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
JAPANESE INTERNET VENTURE
body: Two Japanese companies -- the Softbank Corporation and the Best Denki Company, a leading Japanese retailer of electrical appliances, said they would set up a joint venture to sell appliances and other goods through the Internet. The partners predicted annual sales of $100 million within four years. http://www.nytimes.com

title: An Ebay Report Card
body: To the Editor: In your article on on-line auctions, you quote Arlen Miller as drawing an ethical line and only getting in touch with Ebay buyers after an auction is over. On Ebay, people like Mr. Miller are referred to as "bottom feeders" and their email soliciting business is considered spam. If the recipient of such an email sends it to Safe Harbor at Ebay, the sender could find his Ebay registration canceled. It is even a gray area for the initial seller of an item who has multiples of the item to offer it to others on the bidders list.  NANCY PASSOW Englewood, N.J., Sept. 9, 1999    http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CISCO TO ACQUIRE COPENHAGEN INTERNET ACCESS PROVIDER
body: Cisco Systems Inc., the world's largest maker of computer networking equipment, said yesterday that it would acquire the closely held Internet access provider Cocom of Copenhagen for $65.6 million in stock. Cisco said the acquisition was made in an effort to expand its delivery of broadband access products by adding digital video broadcasting solutions to Cisco's cable portfolio. Cisco's shares fell $1.4375, to $70.50. The acquisition will be accounted for as a pooling of interests and is expected to close in July 2000. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Watching Hurricane Floyd Without Even Getting Wet
body: Some of the most captivating witnesses to Hurricane Floyd are not wearing TV-network-issue windbreakers. In Jensen Beach, Fla., Webcams atop a Holiday Inn (www.video-monitoring.com/martin/pan/pan.htm) provided a panoramic view of the storm's passage over the state's south coast, above. Elsewhere in the county, three people covered a Linux computer in plastic and left it running while they sought higher ground. The machine, equipped with a Webcam and a T-1 line, survived Wednesday's onslaught, recording the progress of the surf as it crashed its way up to the house. Their Web page received more than 470,000 hits in 24 hours (z.treco.net/greg).   BRUCE HEADLAM http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photos

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Newspage.com Work Goes to Grey
body: Newspage.com in Burlington, Mass., a unit of the Newsedge Corporation that delivers personalized news and information to business customers on the Web, has awarded its first off-line branding account to Grey Advertising in newyork. Billings were estimated at $10 million to $15 million. The decision came after a three-month review that had been narrowed to Grey and three other agencies: Chadwick Communications in newyork, Pro Media Inc. in Natick, Mass., and TFA/Leo Burnett Technology Group in Boston, part of the Leo Burnett Company unit of Leo Group. Beyond Interactive in Ann Arbor, Mich., recently acquired by Grey, handles the on-line duties.  http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Accounts
body: * Gillespie, Princeton, N.J., was awarded the first accounts of two Internet companies with combined billings estimated at $15 million: Gobi.com, newyork, an Internet service provider and computer leasing company, and Media and Beyond, newyork, a computer and electronics retailer. Gillespie is part of the MRM unit of McCann-Erickson World Group, owned by the Interpublic Group of Cos. * Smart Online Inc., Research Triangle Park, N.C., a company that will offer advice to small businesses on a Web site (www.smartonline.com), to the Martin Agency, Richmond, part of the Lowe Group unit of the Interpublic Group of Cos., to handle its first account. Billings were estimated at $7 million. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD NEWS BRIEFING: AMERICAS;
INTERNET STAKE SOLD
body: A group of investors led by Morgan Stanley Dean Witter & Company paid $100 million for a minority holding in Latin America's largest Internet company. The purchase of the 12.5 percent stake in the company, Universo Online, a Sao Paulo-based venture with close to 500,000 subscribers, provides some of the capital it needs to expand in the Spanish-speaking countries of Latin America. Universo Online faces competition in Latin America from companies like the Microsoft Corporation, Psinet Inc. and America Online Inc. Simon Romero http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD NEWS BRIEFING: ASIA;
CHINA'S FOREIGN NET BAN
body: The Chinese Government announced it would enforce its ban on foreign investment in operating Internet and other telecommunication services -- one of China's fastest-growing industries. Several major Chinese Internet companies are part-owned by foreign Internet or media concerns. The Minister of Information Industry, Wu Jichuan, said that since 1993, Chinese regulations have "clearly stipulated that no foreign investment is allowed in the operation of telecoms networks and services." http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
NATIONAL INFORMATION TO BUY ON-LINE SERVICES COMPANY
body: National Information Consortium Inc., which provides Internet services to governments, said yesterday that it had agreed to acquire Efed from the privately held Electronic Press Inc. for $29.6 million in cash and stock. Efed designs on-line procurement software and services for governments, allowing officials to compare and buy products over the Internet. National Information Consortium said it would acquire Efed for $15 million in cash and 606,000 of its shares. National Information's shares rose $4.125 each, or 17 percent, to $28.25 in Nasdaq trading. National Information Consortium said Efed would retain its senior management and remain in Reston, Va. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
BRITISH INTERNET TALKS
body: Britain's largest carrier of Internet traffic, Energis P.L.C., said it was in negotiations to acquire Racal Telecom, the telecommunications unit of Racal Electronics P.L.C. British reports estimated the deal could be worth 800 million pounds , or $1.29 billion. If the acquisition proceeds, the addition of Racal Telecom would make Energis the third-largest telecommunications company in Britain, behind British Telecommunications and Cable and Wireless. Energis has been expanding its business through acquisitions. Andrew Ross Sorkin http://www.nytimes.com

title: Insure Internet Access
body: To the Editor: The Federal Communications Commission and municipalities should refrain from imposing an open-access requirement on AT&T's and Time Warner's cable systems (editorial, Sept. 6). Regulatory intervention could discourage these potential suppliers from undertaking the investments necessary to offer high-speed Internet access along with competitive telephone services. However, these considerations apply equally to the investments by local telephone companies in digital subscriber lines. Under present F.C.C. policies, these companies alone are subject to the likely handicap of having to sell or share these lines with competitors at regulated prices or to offer them through a separate subsidiary. Far from enjoying their historical monopolies, they are behind AT&T and the other cable companies in this race.  ALFRED E. KAHN Ithaca, N.Y., Sept. 10, 1999  The writer is professor emeritus at Cornell University. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEW YORKERS & CO;
A Web Shop Goes From Virtual to Tangible
body: As Jaz-Michael King's three-year-old Web page design company, Merlin Web, grew bigger, customers started coming over to his house in Kensington, Brooklyn, with questions, and his staff started working there as well. "I wasn't getting any of the benefits of staying at home," he said. So he moved his design operations into an office and attached a storefront with six computers as a secondary business that would attract more customers, giving the virtual universe of the Web a tangible presence in Carroll Gardens. At the Merlin Web shop, at 354 Court Street (between President and Union Streets), the public may use any of six computers to surf the Web, design documents, set up an email account or play video games, all for $9 an hour (or $2.25 for 15 minutes). http://www.nytimes.com

title:
PRIVATE SECTOR;
A Familiar Name, a Familiar Path - Correction Appended
body: The ranks of Internet entrepreneurs have attracted yet another prestigious name: Boutros-Ghali. No, not former United Nations Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, but Teymour Boutros-Ghali, his son. The younger Mr. Boutros-Ghali, 44, born in Egypt and raised in Europe, is a former publisher of Time Inc. International. He was named chief executive of Allbusiness.com, based in San Francisco, on Tuesday. The company, which is set to get its Web site rolling later this week, aims to help small businesses find professional services, like payroll processing, legal help and recruiting. While he hasn't run a dot-com yet, Mr. Boutros-Ghali has had a hand in starting several, including Weddingnetwork.com, an on-line bridal registry of which he is a co-founder and a director. He said he ultimately decided to dive in full time with AllBusiness.com because it suited his passion for building an enterprise that has the potential to grow explosively. "We have the opportunity to become the premier, and one of the first, businesses that truly provides and consolidates an extremely fragmented industry -- and create a multibillion-dollar enterprise," Mr. Boutros-Ghali said.   MATT RICHTEL http://www.nytimes.com Correction  A brief report in the Private Sector column last Sunday, about the appointment of Teymour Boutros-Ghali as chief executive of Allbusiness.com, misstated his relationship to Boutros Boutros-Ghali, the former Secretary General of the United Nations. The younger Mr. Boutros-Ghali is a nephew, not a son. The report also misstated one aspect of his work experience. He has indeed run an Internet company before, as co-founder and chief executive of ThriveOnline, a consumer health site. Correction-Date: September 19, 1999, Sunday

title: Medical Dilemmas
body: To the Editor: Are there really too many doctors on the Internet, as your Sept. 8 letters headline suggests? My recent research, which is partly financed by the National Institutes of Health, suggests that in fact too few doctors are using the Internet as a tool in patient education. Major reasons are the volume of information, cost, diversity in patient sophistication with the Internet, and liability. Moreover, helping a diverse patient population navigate the medical information on the Internet is time-consuming. Michelle Wong (letter, Sept. 8) is right that the responsibility for protecting medical consumers who use the Web cannot fall on individual doctors like Dr. C. Everett Koop. Yet consumers, too, should have a role in establishing guidelines, not just the Government or the American Medical Association.  THELMA LEAFFER Bethesda, Md., Sept. 9, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title: A Left Click for Politics
body: To the Editor: "Democracy Finds Fertile Ground on Line" (Sept. 2) about political sites on the Web left out an outstanding Web site that articulates the liberal point of view, and does so very well. Turn Left -- The home of Liberalism on the Web (www.turnleft .com) has, in my opinion, intelligent and thoughtful articles and views about politics, philosophy and liberalism. It also has many links to opposing points of view.  ALAN HIPWELL newyork City, Sept. 2, 1999   http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CONCENTRIC NETWORK TOBUY BRITISH INTERNET PROVIDER
body: The Concentric Network Corporation, a provider of Internet services to businesses, said yesterday that it had agreed to acquire Internet Technology Group P.L.C. for £146 million ($235 million) to enter the European Internet-access market. Concentric, based in San Jose, Calif., will pay 253 pence for each Internet Technology share in cash and new Concentric shares. Concentric, of which the Microsoft Corporation owns about 4 percent, is buying Internet Technology for its Internet protocol network, the most extensive of any independent British Internet provider. Spending on Internet access in Europe is expected to balloon to $12 billion in 2001 from $2.5 billion last year. Concentric provides Internet services that allow businesses to communicate with their offices, customers and suppliers. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
PRODIGY TO BUY SMALL-BUSINESS WEB-HOST COMPANY
body: The Prodigy Communications Corporation, the Internet service provider, said yesterday that it had agreed to buy a small-business Web-host company, Bizonthe.net, from Vartec Telecom Inc. for $100 million in cash and stock. The deal will include Bizonthe.net's 80,000 subscribers, 140 employees and network infrastructure, and be part of Prodigy's strategy of catering to small businesses. Bizonthe.net, which is based in Houston, will assume management of the entire Prodigy suite of small-business services. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Chief Executive of Sabre Is Resigning
body: Michael Durham, chief executive of Sabre Holdings Corporation,who led the spinoff of the company from the AMR Corporation three years ago, has resigned. Sabre's chairman, Donald Carty, also AMR's chairman and chief executive, took over as interim chief executive. Sabre hired a search firm to look for a replacement for Mr. Durham, 48, who did not announce his future plans and was not immediately available for comment. "He has just decided it's time to pursue other interests," Barbara Kieker, a spokeswoman for Sabre, said. Mr. Durham joined AMR's finance department in 1979 and rose to become its chief financial officer before moving to Sabre in 1995 to lead the spinoff. He also oversaw Sabre's development of Travelocity.com, the No. 1 travel site on the Internet. Mr. Durham's sudden departure and the lack of a replacement stunned analysts and investors. "I'm very surprised," said Nicholas Moore, senior analyst at Jurika & Voyles Inc., which owned 992,702 Sabre shares as of June 30. "I doubt it's any indication of the strength of the company." http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
DIGITAL ISLAND SHARESSOAR ON MEDIA-DELIVERY DEAL
body: Digital Island Inc. said yesterday that it planned to build an Internet-based audio and video transmission network that would improve international delivery of Web broadcasts, and its stock surged 32 percent. Digital Island, which provides network management services to Web sites, said it had agreed to deals to enhance its network using technologies for media transmission from the Seattle-based Real Networks Inc. and Web-site viewing from the Inktomi Corporation of San Mateo, Calif. Shares of Digital Island jumped $6.125, to $25. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
I.B.M. TO OFFER SERVER FOR INTERNET SERVICE PROVIDERS
body: The International Business Machines Corporation said yesterday that it would introduce a server computer for Internet service providers, challenging Sun Microsystems in that market. The new computer, the Netfinity 4000R, will be just one and a half inches thick so it can be stacked with other servers in a small space, I.B.M. said. The machine, which will be available this month, will cost $3,000 to $4,000 and will be powered by two Pentium III processors from the Intel Corporation. Sun captured much of the market by introducing compact servers that can be easily added to a network as a company's Web business expands. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MEDIACONSULT.COM AGREES TO BUY PHYSICIANS' ONLINE
body: Mediconsult.com Inc., which provides health information and services on the Internet, said that it had agreed to buy the privately held Physicians' Online Inc. for $166.5 million in stock and the assumption of $13.5 million in debt. Mediconsult.com focuses on patients with chronic health conditions, like diabetes and asthma. Physicians' Online, based in Tarrytown, N.Y., offers services to 80,000 doctors, including access to medical data bases and email. Mediconsult.com, based in newyork, said it wanted to combine the two audiences. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
Metro Business;
Health Sites to Merge
body: Mediconsult.com Inc., which provides health information and services on the Internet, said it is buying Physicians' Online Inc. for $180 million in stock and debt. Mediconsult.com, based in newyork, focuses on patients with chronic health conditions like migraine headaches, diabetes and asthma, while Physicians' Online offers services to 80,000 doctors, including access to medical databases, news and email. Mediconsult.com said it wants to combine the two audiences, allowing it to offer features focusing on the doctor-patient relationship. Mediconsult.com plans to exchange 20 million shares of its stock for all the shares of Physicians' Online, which is privately held and based in Tarrytown, N.Y. The purchase is expected to close by the end of the year. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Internet Phone Provider Plans Stock Sale
body: Deltathree.com, a provider of low-cost phone service over the Internet, plans to hold an initial stock sale that it hopes can raise as much as $57.5 million. The company, which is based in newyork and controlled by the cosmetics heir Ronald S. Lauder's RSL Communications Ltd., filed late last week with the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell common stock. The number of shares to be sold and their estimated price range will be disclosed in a future filing. Deltathree, which was formed in 1996, manages what it says is the world's largest private network used to carry voice traffic over the Internet. The network includes 43 access points to the Internet. The Deltathree.com filing comes about a month after a stock sale by the rival Net2Phone Inc., which bills itself as the largest provider of Internet phone calls. Net2Phone shares have risen more than fivefold since the company, which is controlled by IDT of Hackensack, N.J., went public on July 29. It has received investments from Cnet Inc. and the General Electric Company's NBC broadcasting unit, and has formed alliances with America Online Inc. and the Compaq Computer Corporation. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
NOKIA BUYS ROOFTOP COMMUNICATIONS FOR $57 MILLION
body: Nokia A.B., the Finnish telecommunications equipment maker, said yesterday that it had acquired the Rooftop Communications Corporation for $57 million in a move to strengthen its capabilities in Internet protocol technology. Rooftop Communications, based in Mountain View, Calif., produces radio systems that enable high-speed wireless access to the Internet. The company employs 20 people. Nokia said the acquisition would give it additional holdings in wireless Internet access, especially in wireless Internet protocol routers. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
SYMANTEC SETS MARKETING PACT WITH AT&T AND EARTHLINK
body: The Symantec Corporation, maker of the Norton brand of utility software for personal computers, said yesterday that it had entered promotional agreements with the AT&T Corporation and Earthlink Network Inc. that will offer consumers special deals for Internet access. The company, based in Cupertino, Calif., will bundle retail copies of its software with AT&T's Worldnet Service Internet software and with Earthlink's Totalaccess Internet software. In exchange, AT&T and Earthlink will offer one month of free Internet access to users who register for their services from one of the Symantec products. Symantec's shares were up $2.875, to $32.875. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Times Raising Price
body: The suggested newsstand price for Monday-through-Saturday issues of The newyork Times in the metropolitan area will rise to 75 cents on Sept. 13, from 60 cents, the newspaper announced yesterday. The increase will not affect the Sunday paper, the national and Northeast editions or the price of home delivery when provided directly by The Times. The increase is the first since 1994. Since that time, The Times has introduced a number of changes, including daily color pages and several new or expanded sections.  http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: AMERICAS;
INTERNET SERVICE IN BRAZIL
body: The newyork-based Starmedia Network Inc. is offering an Internet access service in Brazil jointly with the AT&T Corporation, a venture that it plans to extend soon to other big Latin American nations. Starmedia, one of the biggest Latin American Internet destinations, said it would also provide Internet access in Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Mexico by the end of the year. AT&T will manage the network in Brazil and Starmedia has the option to use AT&T's network throughout Latin America. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AT&T AND INTERNET PHONE PROVIDER REACH SERVICES DEAL
body: The AT&T Corporation said yesterday that it would provide international networking services to Net2Phone Inc., enabling Net2Phone to expand its low-cost Internet-based calling service to 17 countries. The five-year contract is expected to generate more than $100 million in revenue, AT&T said. It covers countries in Asia, Europe and Africa, Net2Phone said. A dozen other countries will be considered for later expansion under the agreement, AT&T said. Net2Phone's shares jumped $12.375, to $85 in Nasdaq trading. The company, which is based in Hackensack, N.J., went public on July 29 at $15 a share. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
ISS GROUP MAKES ACQUISITION TO ADD SECURITY SERVICES
body: ISS Group Inc., a maker of security software for Internet commerce, said yesterday that it had agreed to buy closely held Netrex Secure Solutions for about $57.1 million in stock to offer customers constant security monitoring services. ISS, which is based in Atlanta, makes the Safesuite security system. Netrex, which is based in Southfield, Mich., had revenue of about $21.8 million last year. It has about 150 employees. The company had revenue of about $21.8 million last year. The acquisition of Netrex enables ISS to monitor computer systems for Internet companies from remote sites. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
NETRIX SETS ACQUISITION OF OPENROUTE NETWORKS
body: The Netrix Corporation, a provider of voice and data-networking products, agreed yesterday to acquire Openroute Networks Inc. for about $64 million in stock. Netrix, based in Herndon, Va., said it would combine its Internet telephone products with Openroute's Internet security products to offer customers private voice and data networks. Openroute is based in Westborough, Mass. Under the deal, each Openroute share will be exchanged for one Netrix common share. http://www.nytimes.com

title: End Internet Gridlock
body: To the Editor: While the traffic jams that slow the Internet to a snail's pace can indeed be alleviated by the development of new protocols to govern streaming media -- the multimedia technology that delivers real-time video and audio over the Net -- the ultimate solution lies in increasing the bandwidth available for all Internet traffic by deploying seamless broadband networks across the country (Business Day, Aug. 23). Government restrictions that limit some of the country's largest telecommunications companies from transmitting Internet data are impeding the deployment of those high-speed networks. These restrictions prevent the Internet from developing into a ubiquitous network that can deliver reliable data as well as video and audio transmissions.  MIKE MC CURRY SUSAN MOLINARI Washington, Aug. 25, 1999  The writers are co-chairmen of iAdvance, a coalition of technology companies and public-interest groups. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AXENT TO ACQUIRE 2 ALTA VISTA SECURITY SOFTWARE LINES
body: The Compaq Computer Corporation, the Houston-based personal computer maker, agreed yesterday to sell two lines of Alta Vista security software to Axent Technologies, further distancing itself from the troubled product family. Terms were not disclosed. Under the deal, Axent will develop the next version of the software products, which restrict access to computer networks and Web sites. The accord follows CMGI Inc.'s completion of its $2.3 billion purchase of a majority stake in Compaq's Alta Vista Internet search site. Compaq inherited Alta Vista when it bought the Digital Equipment Corporation last year. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
NEWBRIDGE NETWORKS MOVES ON INTERNET STRATEGY
body: The Newbridge Networks Corporation announced the first investments in its Internet strategy yesterday with the planned purchase of two affiliate companies. Newbridge, a computer networking company based near Ottawa, said it expected to spend the equivalent of about $235 million (unitedstates) in the next two years buying the Timestep Corporation, also based in Ontario, and Northchurch Communications, of Andover, Mass. Newbridge already has a 30 percent stake in each company. Timestep sells technology that secures communication on networks based on the Internet. Northchurch makes high-speed routers that provide access to data, video and other services. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
SPRINT TO OFFER LONG-DISTANCE CALLS VIA THE INTERNET
body: The Sprint Corporation said yesterday that it would begin a trial offer of long-distance calls to Asian countries over the Internet using Net2phone Inc.'s technology. Financial terms were not disclosed. Sprint, based in Westwood, Kan., said the service would be called Sprint Callternatives and would allow customers to place calls to China, hongkong, India, Japan, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. Net2phone, of Hackensack, N.J., has a service that lets users place long-distance calls through a personal computer over the Internet. The company went public at $15 a share on July 29; the shares jumped $17 yesterday, to $70.125. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
2 On-Line Retailers Split With Left Field
body: Left Field in San Francisco said yesterday that it had resigned two of its on-line accounts with estimated billings at $8 million: Amazon.com in Seattle and Drugstore.com in Bellevue, Wash. Spokesmen for both Amazon and Drugstore said the decisions to end their relationships with Left Field were mutual. The Amazon spokesman, Paul Capelli, said the account would be placed in review although a timetable for the decision had not been set. Amazon had worked with Left Field since 1996. The decision does not affect Amazon's relationship with its off-line advertiser, Foote, Cone & Belding Worldwide in Chicago, part of True North Communications. The announcement followed Drugstore's decision to place its off-line account in review. The on-line pharmaceutical retailer named Fallon McElligott in Minneapolis its agency of record last week for its account, with estimated billings of $30 million. Left Field had worked with Drugstore since the end of last year.  http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Web Street to Go Public
body: Web Street Inc., an on-line brokerage firm, filed today with Federal regulators to sell up to $50 million worth of common stock in an initial public offering. Web Street, on line at www.webstreet.com, said its service was for investors primarily in the unitedstates and Europe. It said it could execute equity and option trades at low cost and provide real-time trading information, financial market data and account information. In a preliminary filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Web Street did not disclose how many shares would be offered or the estimated price range. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
PSINET AGREES TO BUY DATA SERVICE PROVIDER
body: Psinet Inc., which provides Internet access for businesses, agreed yesterday to buy Transaction Network Services Inc. for $720 million in cash and stock so it could offer electronic-commerce services. Psinet will pay $22.50 in cash, or about $351 million, and half a share for each Transaction Network share. That is about $45 a share. Transaction Network Services shareholders can choose to receive stock, cash or both. Transaction Network provides high-speed data services for credit card and automatic teller machine transactions, and its number of Internet transactions has risen 20 percent a month this year. The shares of Transaction Network, based in Reston, Va., surged 25 percent yesterday, gaining $9 each, to $43.25, after jumping more than $6 a share on Friday. Psinet rose 31.25 cents, to $45.875. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Accounts
body: * Stockgroup.com, Vancouver, British Columbia, and Adatom.com, Milpitas, Calif., to Rocket Science Creative Ltd., newyork, to handle the first accounts of the on-line financial news site and the Web-based furniture retailer. Billings were estimated at $1.5 million over six months for Stockgroup.com and $1 million over four months for Adatom.com.  * Sina.com, Sunnyvale, Calif., to Admerasia Inc., newyork, as the first agency of record for the Internet portal aimed at people of Chinese descent. Billings were estimated at $1 million. * Neonova Network Services, Research Triangle Park, N.C., part of the Digitel Corp., to West & Vaughan, Durham, N.C., to handle the account of the Internet service provider, which had been handled in-house. Billings were estimated at $1 million.  * Skila Inc., Mahwah, N.J., which operates an on-line heath care information service, to Ryan Drossman/ MARC, newyork, part of MARC USA, as the first agency to handle its account. Billings were estimated at $1 million. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD NEWS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
DISNEY'S BRITAIN INTERNET DEAL
body: The new-media unit of the Walt Disney Company, the Buena Vista Internet Group, acquired 60 percent of the Web site Soccernet from Daily Mail and General Trust P.L.C. of Britain in an effort to expand its soccer coverage on its ESPN Web sites and to help promote the ESPN.com brand internationally. Terms were not disclosed. The move is part of Disney's strategy to develop an audience for its Web sites beyond the unitedstates. Andrew Ross Sorkin http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Graph tracks daily closes of Walt Disney, since Aug. 10.

title: Yahoo a Partner In New Web Site
body: Yahoo Inc. said today that it had teamed with Beatnik Inc., Emusic.com and Liquid Audio Inc. to start Yahoo Digital, a new music and video site on the Internet. Users of the new site, Yahoo said, will be able to watch and listen to music performances; preview, download and purchase music; remix music tracks on line and view on-demand video channels. The privately held Beatnik of San Mateo, Calif., provides technologies for the delivery of music over the Internet. Emusic.com of Redwood City, Calif., operates a Web site for sampling and buying music in the MP3 format. Liquid Audio, which is also based in Redwood City, provides software that enables musicians, record labels and retailers to deliver music over the Internet with copyright protections. Yahoo, operator of the most frequently visited site on the Internet, is based in Santa Clara, Calif. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
National News Briefs;
Student Pleads Guilty In Software Piracy Case
body: A college student has pleaded guilty to illegally distributing movies, music and software programs from his Web site in what Federal prosecutors describe as the first Internet piracy conviction under a 1997 law. The student, Jeffrey Levy, was arrested after investigators found that thousands of pirated software programs and digitally recorded movies and music had been distributed through equipment at his apartment near the University of Oregon campus in Eugene, officials said. Mr. Levy, a 22-year-old senior, could get up to three years in prison and be fined up to $250,000. The 1997 law bans the reproduction or distribution of copyrighted works. Mr. Levy is to be sentenced on Nov. 22. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Keeping the Web Open
body: To the Editor: Your Aug. 13 front-page article "Fight for Internet Access Creates Unusual Alliances" says that William E. Kennard, the chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, "has in essence sided with AT&T by formulating a policy that only the Federal Government, and not local authorities, has jurisdiction, but ruling out intervention for now." We have no intention of letting cable or any other broadband provider gain a monopoly position in broadband services. Yet a decision to regulate at this early stage would inhibit investment in and deployment of the next generation of advanced communications technologies. We have been working to foster the ability of competing technologies to reach the Internet marketplace -- for instance, local phone companies, satellite companies, wireless operators and cable. In these ways, we will make certain that all Americans receive advanced communications services as soon as possible.  DEBORAH A. LATHEN Chief, Cable Services Bureau Federal Communications Commission Washington, Aug. 20, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
E-COMMERCE VENTURE FOR CHINA
body: The News Corporation announced a strategic partnership between its joint-venture unit, the PDN Xinren Information and Technology Company, and the Oracle Corporation of Redwood Shores, Calif., to develop an E-commerce business in China. Under the agreement, Oracle will provide an Internet-based technology platform and E-commerce support services for Chinabyte, an Internet content provider begun by PDN. PDN is a joint venture between the News Corporation, the Australian media company led by Rupert Murdoch, and The People's Daily in China. Chinabyte.com specializes in information technology content. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
NTL SAYS IT IS BUYINGWORKPLACE TECHNOLOGIES OF BRITAIN
body: NTL Inc., a newyork company that owns Britain's biggest cable company in number of subscribers, said yesterday that it would buy Workplace Technologies P.L.C. for £81 million ($130 million) to enhance its range of phone and Internet services for business customers. NTL, whose shareholders include France Telecom and the Microsoft Corporation, will also assume £20 million of the debt of Workplace, which designs data, voice and video networks. NTL is beefing up its portfolio of services to compete with British Telecommunications P.L.C. in phone and high-speed Internet markets. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CBS BUYS 38% OF ON-LINE JOB ADVERTISING SITE
body: The CBS Corporation said yesterday that it had acquired a 38 percent equity stake in Jobs.com Inc. in return for $62 million in advertising, promotion and other considerations on CBS media properties over five years. The privately held Jobs.com is a Dallas-based on-line jobs posting site. CBS said classified advertising is increasingly moving from the newspaper business to the Internet and that it believed Jobs.com was well positioned to benefit from the transition. CBS will hold two seats on Jobs.com's board. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CISCO SYSTEMS TO PAY $143 MILLION FOR MAXCOMM
body: Cisco Systems Inc., the world's No. 1 maker of Internet equipment, agreed yesterday to buy the closely held Maxcomm Technologies Inc., in Chelmsford, Mass., for $143 million in stock, to expand its ability to provide high-speed Internet access to homes. Separately, Cisco, which is based in San Jose, Calif., said it had paid $49 million for a 4 percent stake in another closely held company, Akamai Technologies Inc., as part of an agreement to develop technology to increase the speed and reliability of Internet sites. Akamai, based in Cambridge, Mass., helps Web-site operators run faster and at higher capacity. http://www.nytimes.com

title: For Students, the Web Isn't 'Pork'
body: To the Editor: Re "Phone Fee for School Internet Service Seems to Be Too Popular to Overturn" (news article, Aug. 15): The Administration set out to even the playing field by insuring that all students had access to the Internet, a powerful new education tool. The goal has essentially been met, on time, and with the approval of the majority of Americans. You quote an opponent of the E-rate program who cynically calls it "pork barrel."
