The term "pork" suggests an unfair financial advantage to a special-interest group. If 80,000 schools and libraries are a special interest, can any Federal financing qualify as non-pork? Perhaps the American taxpayer understands the distinction between a tax and pork better.  PATRICIA PARISI newyork, Aug. 15, 1999  The writer is deputy secretary regional representative, Region II, Department of Education. http://www.nytimes.com

title: In Defense of NumLock
body: To the Editor: The article implies that the NumLock key no longer has much practical value. In fact, on Windows systems, the key provides a quick and convenient method for inserting useful symbols into documents. This is done (with NumLock on) by pressing the Alt key plus a four-digit code on the numeric key pad.  KENNETH J. KAHN Lawrence, N.Y., Aug. 12, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Ebay Addicts Come Up for Air
body: Now Ebay users can bid and run. In an effort to differentiate itself from competitors, the auction giant has started a paging service that will update users on the progress of their auctions when they are away from their computers. "A lot of Ebay users were telling us they go out and get busy," said Kevin Pursglove, a spokesman for the company, countering the popular image of his customers. "They've lost track of time. When they get home, the auction has ended and they've been outbid. If there is some way that we could have notified them, they would have skipped the second course or cut their cup of coffee." The service, playfully titled Ebay-a-go-go, costs $55 for about 500 messages and uses any wireless device that offers text messaging. Individuals can use their own devices or buy Ebay ones. The service notifies users when they have won an item, been outbid or sold an item. Users can sign up through www.skytel.com/ebay. Users are apparently clamoring for still more. They want the ability to bid on the run. "Eventually, the idea is to make it a two-way service," Mr. Pursglove.   JENNIFER 8. LEE http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
FREESERVE STOCK TRADING
body: The British subscription-free Internet access provider, Freeserve P.L.C., announced it would offer on-line securities trading to compete with discount brokers like E*Trade Group Inc. and the Charles Schwab Corporation, which have established sites for British Web surfers. Freeserve, Britain's largest Internet provider, hopes the new brokerage service will help differentiate it from the proliferation of other subscription-free Internet providers in Britain, including America Online's entrant to be introduced this fall, Netscape Online. Andrew Ross Sorkin (NYT) http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CALISTA, PHONE TECHNOLOGY CONCERN, BOUGHT BY CISCO
body: Cisco Systems Inc., a leading maker of computer networking equipment, announced yesterday that it was acquiring privately held Calista Inc., a provider of Internet-based phone technology, for $55 million in stock. Calista, based in England and San Jose, Calif., develops technology that allows phone systems from different vendors to work together over networks built on Internet standards. The acquisition enables Cisco, based in San Jose, to offer its customers the ability to transmit data, voice and video services across the Internet rather than over traditional phone lines, the company said. http://www.nytimes.com

title: F.C.C. Reasserts Authority Over Net Access
body: The Federal Communications Commission reasserted its authority today to regulate providers of high-speed Internet access and raised questions about how cable companies that offer such services should be classified. In a friend-of-the-court brief in AT&T's case against Portland, Ore., the F.C.C. warned that local officials could create "regulatory disparity" by exercising authority over cable companies offering Internet service. Cable officials in the Portland area required AT&T, which took over the cable-television company Tele-Communications Inc. earlier this year, to open its cable lines for use by Internet competitors. A Federal judge upheld this exercise of their authority. AT&T's legal challenge to it is currently before the unitedstates Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. In its brief, the commission said that it alone had authority over providers of high-speed Internet service -- also known as broadband. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Loss at Cablevision Widens on Spending
body: The Cablevision Systems Corporation, the largest cable television company in the newyork region, said today that its second-quarter loss had widened as it spent more on services like digital cable and Internet access. Cablevision, which is based in Bethpage, N.Y., said it had lost $167.8 million, or $1.10 a share, on revenue of $946 million. A year earlier, it posted a pro forma loss of $122.9 million, or 82 cents a share, on revenue of $805 million. The company's shares fell 25 cents, to $69.50. The company's capital spending in the first six months climbed 47 percent, to $380.9 million, as it rebuilt systems to add channels and offer Internet access and digital cable. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MICROSOFT OFFERS ON-LINE DISCOUNT AT COSTCO
body: The Microsoft Corporation said this week that it was offering MSN Internet access at a 40 percent discount to its regular price through the Costco Companies, a leading chain of warehouse-club stores, as fees for online services continue to fall. Three months of service are being offered for $35.97, or $11.99 a month, compared with MSN's regular fee of $19.95 a month, said Deanna Sanford, Microsoft's lead product manager for MSN. Microsoft, the world's biggest software maker, is moving to cut Internet access fees as it competes with the No. 1 on-line service provider, America Online Inc. In recent months Microsoft has formed partnerships with Staples Inc., Micro Center and Lan Plus Inc. to offer free PC's in exchange for MSN Internet service. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
If You've Always Wanted to Go to Harvard . . .
body: Now you can walk the hallowed halls of academe on the Internet or revisit the site of a particularly embarrassing Frosh Week episode. The Campus Tours site (www.campustours.com) has collected many of the interactive digital tours that college and university campuses put on line to lure prospective students. For example, Duke University displays its elegant Durham, N.C., campus through 360-degree panoramas, at www.duke.edu/web/duketour. Harvard University provides a virtual tour through lecture halls and dorm rooms at www.news.harvard.edu/tour. Michael Quan, who does on-line production for some universities, noted that the elaborate tours connect not only with future students but also with another critical university audience: alumni, who can be gently prodded to make generous donations after they explore some old haunts. JENNIFER 8. LEE http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo: A panoramic view of Harvard Square in Cambridge, Mass.

title: Proliferation of Passwords
body: To the Editor: I agree with your article discussing the abundance of passwords on the Internet and the frustration they can cause ("Forgot a Password? Try 'Way2Many,' " Aug. 5). As an Internet entrepreneur I was recently involved in the design and creation of a major Web site. Part of the process involved interviewing hundreds of people to learn their likes and dislikes on line. One of the top issues with users was passwords -- the average user was adamant about not having to log in to the site every time they visited. When faced with the choice of a few added options to the system (which would require a password from every user) or a simpler system with no passwords or a group password, the choice was almost unanimous for the simpler system.  GORDON BROTT Boston, Aug. 5, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title: Sprint to Offer Wireless Access to Internet
body: The Sprint Corporation said today that it planned to offer wireless Internet access in late September, a move that is seen as critical to the success of local and long-distance communications carriers. "If you don't have this, you'll be left behind," said John Garcia, senior vice president for sales and marketing at Sprint, which is based in Kansas City, Mo. The services, which will be called Sprint PCS Wireless Web, will be offered by Sprint's wireless communications unit, Sprint PCS Group. Mobile telephone customers will have access to some Web content and will be able to have information from Yahoo, like news and weather updates, delivered to their telephones. Sprint also plans to offer a wireless Web connection that will allow users to gain access to laptop and hand-held computers through their mobile telephones instead of a telephone line. Many other carriers have plans to introduce wireless Internet access, and most new mobile phones are equipped to offer Internet access. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Qwest Plan to Include Free Internet Access
body: The long-distance telephone company Qwest Communications International Inc. announced a package today that would offer free Internet access to consumers who buy its special long-distance calling services. Denver-based Qwest said the package featured free unlimited dial-up Internet service and 250 minutes of domestic long-distance calling for a flat rate of $24.95 a month. Additional minutes will be charged at 10 cents a minute. The move by Qwest, the No. 4 unitedstates long-distance telephone company, comes one day after a rival, MCI Worldcom Inc., cut evening, overnight and weekend calling rates to as low as 5 cents a minute. Long-distance companies have been battling to take advantage of their shrinking internal costs to offer discounts to customers in hopes that they also will subscribe to more lucrative services like the Internet, data and wireless. "By leveraging our Internet technologies and Web-based customer platforms, Qwest is bringing consumers the best in today's communications services," said John Taylor, senior vice president for consumer markets at the company. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Executive Promoted At New York Times
body: Darren A. Frank, an 18-year employee of The newyork Times who most recently was group director for technology advertising, has been promoted to vice president for advertising sales, effective immediately, the newspaper said yesterday. He replaces Denise F. Warren, who was promoted to vice president for strategic planning. Mr. Frank, 40, has been group director for technology advertising since last year. Before that appointment, he was managing director for the newspaper's telecommunications business, where the category grew from $6 million in 1994 to $26 million in 1998 based on his plan to capitalize on changes in the market. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
JAPANESE INTERNET VENTURE
body: A Japanese concern, the Softbank Company, said it was negotiating with the Tokyo Electric Power Company and the Microsoft Corporation on a joint venture in the telecommunications area. The comments followed a newspaper report that the three companies had agreed in principle to set up a low-cost wireless Internet connection service. Softbank and Tokyo Electric Power confirmed the talks but would not give details. The newspaper Nihon Keizai reported that the companies would begin service in the region around Tokyo in the middle of next year. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Net Address Sold at Auction for $823,456
body: Bidding for use of the Internet address Drugs.com jumped wildly every few minutes before an auction closed with an offer of $823,456. The business that submitted the winning bid on Friday wanted to remain anonymous. Several large drug companies and well-heeled speculators had expressed an interest, according to Eric MacIver, a 21-year-old Internet entrepreneur in Mesa, Ariz., who held an option on the Drugs.com domain name. "The bidder will emerge as someone of note," possibly at a news conference in a week or so, said Steve Newman, executive vice president of the on-line broker Great Domains. Great Domains, based in Los Angeles, was joined by Dotbroker.com in conducting the auction. Other Internet names currently on auction include Loans.com with a high bid as of Friday at $480,000. "We're going to set an end date in two or three weeks," Mr. Newman said of the Loans.com name auction. http://www.nytimes.com

title: ON MY… BOOKMARKS: JOHN J. BRENNAN
body: With two big roles in the mutual fund industry, John J. Brennan doesn't have much time for surfing the Web. Mr. Brennan is chief executive of the Vanguard Group, long the pioneer in index mutual funds and the No. 2 fund family in the industry, behind Fidelity Investments. But he is also chairman of the Investment Company Institute, the fund industry's trade group, at a time when it is under pressure from the Securities and Exchange Commission to bolster the power of independent fund directors. Not surprisingly, most of his Internet bookmarks are related to mutual funds or the markets, including the home pages for Bloomberg, the financial information company, and Morningstar, the mutual fund researchers in Chicago. RICHARD A. OPPEL Jr. http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo/Chart: BLOOMBERG.COM "The Web has been so important to our business life, to be able to get real-time information."  EYES ON THE SOCCER FIELD . . . A coach in a youth soccer league in suburban Philadelphia, Mr. Brennan checks its site for up-to-date information on schedules. "In the old days, somebody had to send us a letter with our standings."  . . . AND ON THE ICE He played hockey as a student at Dartmouth, so his list includes sites of both the college and The Boston Globe, where he reads coverage of the sport. "I need my fix now and then, particularly if my father calls me and we end up comparing notes."

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
INVESTMENT IN EARLY-STAGE E-BUSINESS IS STARTED
body: The International Business Machines Corporation made its first investment in early-stage E-business companies yesterday through the purchase of a $45 million stake in Internet Capital Group Inc. Internet Capital, based in Wayne, Pa., is an incubator for E-business companies, providing them with capital and expertise in areas like recruiting, marketing and sales. Internet Capital completed an initial public offering earlier this week, and its shares began trading on Thursday. In conjunction with the stock sale, I.B.M. purchased 3.75 million Internet Capital shares at the initial offering price of $12 each. Yesterday, Internet Capital shares rose $5.875, to $39.375. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
LYCOS PURCHASES CLOSELY HELD MEDIA SCIENCE
body: Lycos Inc., the Internet search directory, bought the closely held Media Science Inc. for $38.8 million in stock to bolster its Web site with software that plays music downloaded from the Internet. Lycos will issue 1.1 million shares to Media Science, a San Francisco-based company that is incorporated as Internet Music Distribution Inc. Media Science makes Sonique, a software device that allows users to play songs converted into so-called Mp3 computer files on their personal computers. The acquisition will help Lycos exploit the growing popularity of music content on the Web and fortify it against larger rivals that also are adding music-related features. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Domain Concern To Release Data
body: Network Solutions Inc., which has been battling the Federal Government over the company's monopoly on registering Internet addresses, or domains, agreed Thursday to open its data base -- the equivalent of the Internet's telephone directory -- to public use while negotiations over its monopoly continue. The Commerce Department announced the agreement as it extended for a third time, until Sept. 10, its target date for introducing full-scale competition into the domain registration business. The department and Network Solutions are wrangling over the terms under which other companies can begin adding Internet addresses to the master registry of addresses that end in .com, .net and .org, which the company still administers. Among the key sticking points has been ownership of the data base. The data had always been considered public, but earlier this year Network Solutions claimed it as the company's intellectual property. http://www.nytimes.com

title: COMPANYBRIEFS
body: GTE CORP. , the local phone company being acquired by Bell Atlantic, said it would buy back as many as 26 million shares to offset shares issued under employee benefit and dividend reinvestment programs.  CALPINE CORP., which owns stakes in power plants in 12 states, said it would buy the right to build a $350 million plant in Northern California from Enron Corp. for an undisclosed price. LABTEC INC. , a maker of computer speakers and other high-technology multimedia products, agreed to acquire Connector Resources Unlimited Inc. for an undisclosed price to add to its product lines.  PNC BANK CORP., Pittsburgh, the biggest bank in Pennsylvania, said it was adding 100 employees, partly to handle its growing electronic banking business. http://www.nytimes.com

title: European Net Use to Soar
body: The number of Europeans who use the Internet will almost quadruple by 2004, climbing to 121 million from 34 million last year, according to Fletcher Research Ltd. Germany will be the biggest single market in Europe, with 30 million users, followed by Britain, which will have 25 million, the company said. Those countries, along with France, Italy and Spain, will account for 75 percent of Europe's Internet market. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Appointment by Times Co.
body: The newyork Times Company has named Christopher D. Neimeth senior vice president for business development and strategic planning of its new Internet division, Times Company Digital. Mr. Neimeth had been group vice president of The newyork Times Electronic Media Company. Before joining The Times Company in 1996, he was a co-founder of Grey Interactive, a unit of Grey Advertising. His was among eight appointments made recently to the management team of Times Company Digital. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Executive Promoted At New York Times
body: Alyse Myers, vice president for promotion and marketing communications at The newyork Times, has been promoted to vice president for marketing services, effective immediately. The announcement was made by Janet L. Robinson, president and general manager of the newspaper, to whom she reports. In her new role, Ms. Myers will be involved in strategic planning with a focus on brand positioning and development. She will also continue to be responsible for all promotion and marketing communications for the newspaper. Additionally, she will continue to oversee community affairs, event coordinating, creative services, special sections, advertising for the paper and the newyork Times speakers bureau. Ms. Myers, 43, joined The Times in August 1979 as a telephone solicitor in the advertising department. She graduated from Queens College in 1978. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Times Appoints Editor for Week in Review
body: Susan Chira has been named the editor of the Week in Review section of The newyork Times. The appointment, effective in October, was announced yesterday by Joseph Lelyveld, the newspaper's executive editor. Ms. Chira, 41, has been deputy foreign editor of The Times since 1997. She was a correspondent in the paper's Tokyo bureau from 1984 to 1988 and chief of that bureau in 1988 and 1989. Upon returning to the unitedstates, she was national education correspondent. In 1980, she graduated summa cum laude from Harvard College, where she was elected to Phi Beta Kappa and was president of The Harvard Crimson. She joined The Times shortly after graduating and started her career with a variety of metropolitan reporting jobs. She is the author of "A Mother's Place: Choosing Work and Family Without Guilt or Blame," published by HarperCollins. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE IN $100 MILLION PACT WITH CARD MAKER
body: America Online Inc. said it had reached a $100 million agreement making Americangreetings.com the sole provider of greeting cards on America Online's Web sites. The agreement, for five and a half years, extends an existing arrangement to the America Online Web services AOL.com, ICQ, Digital City, Netscape Netcenter and Compuserve, as well as America Online's services in Canada, Britain, Australia, Japan, Germany and France. The original deal covered only basic America Online service. Americangreetings.com is a unit of the American Greetings Corporation of Cleveland. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Dispute Over On-Line Music Is Settled
body: Recording-industry executives announced an end today to all litigation over the Rio portable Mp3 Internet music player, which a Federal appeals court has ruled does not violate piracy laws. The announcement marked a formal end to months of litigation over the Rio, a pager-sized music player made by Diamond Multimedia Systems Inc. that can download and play CD-quality songs encoded in the Mp3 format. Sensing a potential new threat of music piracy, recording-industry executives asked the courts to issue an injunction barring sales of Rio. This was denied, and the companies appealed. In June, a Federal appeals court killed all hope for blocking the Rio when it ruled that the device was not primarily a recorder and thus was not subject to 1992 Federal piracy laws. In the meantime, however, both makers of Mp3 players and the recording industry have cooperated in an effort to establish guidelines for Internet music by the end of the year. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
INTERNET SPEED
body: The quest for the LAN-speed record continues. Last week, computer scientists at Duke University announced that they had developed a system for standard Internet communications over a local area network, or LAN, that moved at a rate of more than one gigabit (one billion bits) per second. According to Jeff Chase, an assistant computer science professor at Duke, that's about twice the speed of the current fastest LAN and about 20,000 times faster than communication through a telephone modem. "What we have done is provide the software support that's needed to allow others to achieve similar speeds on other networks that will arrive in the future," Dr. Chase said http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Looking Directly At a Solar Eclipse
body: Solar eclipses don't just happen every day, and they can't be seen from just anywhere. But a nonprofit group in Japan is changing that, offering live Webcasts that allow computer users to view eclipses as they happen. Its latest project is coverage of the total eclipse that will be viewable across parts of the Middle East and Europe next Wednesday. The group's Web site, www.solar-eclipse.org, will carry video images from seven observation points from England to Iran. The show begins at 4 A.M. Eastern Daylight Time and will last for about three hours, although the period when the sun is totally hidden by the moon at any given point along the route is only two and a half minutes or less.   HENRY FOUNTAIN http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Diagram shows the physics of a solar eclipse.

title: Qwest Offers High-Speed Internet Links
body: Qwest Communications International Inc., which agreed last month to merge with U S West Inc., said today that it had begun selling high-speed Internet access in 13 cities, including newyork, Chicago and Los Angeles. Qwest plans to offer digital subscriber line service in more than 30 markets by the end of the year. The service uses electronics to send data over phone lines at speeds as much as 125 times as fast as dial-up modems, and it stays on 24 hours a day. Local phone companies have been racing to sell digital subscriber line service to compete against high-speed Internet services offered by cable television companies, including the AT&T Corporation, which soon will be the largest unitedstates cable provider after its $62.5 billion acquisition of MediaOne Group Inc. U S West has been the most aggressive of the regional Bells in selling digital subscriber line service. Qwest, which is based in Denver, is also building an 18,815-mile national fiber optic network. It said the cost of its digital subscriber line service would start at $49.95 a month for consumers and $119.95 a month for businesses, with a $500 installation fee. http://www.nytimes.com

title: COMPANY BRIEFS
body: COCA-COLA BOTTLING CO. CONSOLIDATED , Charlotte, N.C., agreed to buy Lynchburg Coca-Cola Bottling Co., Lynchburg, Va., for an undisclosed price. INTERVU INC. , San Diego, which helps companies broadcast over the Internet, agreed to buy closely held software maker Netpodium Inc., Seattle, for about $37.2 million in stock.  COLLEGE TELEVISION NETWORK INC. , Atlanta, whose station broadcasts on campuses, agreed to buy the marketing firm Armed Forces Communications Inc., Santa Barbara, Calif., for about $30 million.  GERALD STEVENS INC. , Fort Lauderdale, Fla., which runs flower shops, bought the closely held Calyx & Corolla Inc., San Francisco, a catalogue seller of flowers and plants, for about $10 million in stock. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
XOOM.COM TO ACQUIRE LIQUIDMARKET FOR $46 MILLION
body: Xoom.com Inc., an on-line direct-marketing company, said yesterday that it had acquired the closely held Liquidmarket Inc. for about $46.8 million in stock to add comparison-shopping technology to its Web site. Xoom.com, based in San Francisco, has 9.2 million members and offers free Web pages and email to users who agree to receive advertising for products. Los Angeles-based Liquidmarket's software is intended to search for the best prices for products being sold by major Internet retailers and also will let Xoom.com collect information about the buying patterns of its customers. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
INTERNET CURRENCY TRADING
body: Freeserve P.L.C., the British subscription-free Internet access provider, will introduce a way to trade currencies on line in the fall. Freeserve, which has just issued shares of the company to the public, hopes to replicate the success of on-line trading firms like E*Trade in the foreign currency exchange market by substantially lowering the commissions on transactions. Globalnet Financial.com, which developed the software to run the currency trading, will operate the Freeserve service, called Matchbook FX.   Andrew Ross Sorkin http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
EUROPEAN INTERNET DEAL
body: Britain's largest carrier of Internet traffic, Energis P.L.C., will buy the pan-European telecommunications alliance Unisource N.V. for £60 million, or $97 million. The move is Energis's first expansion of its network beyond Britain and into Continental Europe where the market for Internet and data traffic is growing rapidly. Unisource, a joint venture of Swisscom A.G. and the former Dutch and Swedish monopolies KPN N.V. and Telia A.B., has been somewhat troubled, and two other companies, AT&T and Telefonica S.A. of Spain, quit the alliance recently. Andrew Ross Sorkin (NYT) http://www.nytimes.com

title: IN MY… LAPTOP CASE/DAVID SAMUEL
body: To catalogue the toys that David Samuel carries in his oversized laptop bag, it may make the most sense to start with the yo-yo and work up to the bite-sized portable music player that stores songs on a computer chip. Mr. Samuel, 27, finds that yo-yoing helps him process ideas, of which he has had plenty since America Online acquired his Internet radio company, Spinner, for close to $400 million earlier this summer. A cellular phone and a slim Sony Vaio laptop computer are also travel necessities for Mr. Samuel, a graduate of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology who founded Spinner three and a half years ago with his stepbrother and a friend. Reading for the plane includes Wired magazine and Sports Illustrated. But the gadget that marks Mr. Samuel as one who is serious about his Internet music is the Diamond Rio player, a device that stores and plays music downloaded from the Internet or transferred from CD's into a digital format called MP3. AMY HARMON http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photos: BREATH MINTS -- "Everyone needs them."  MP3 PLAYER -- "I guess every Internet radio executive has to have one."  BOAT KEY -- For when he wants to escape his email.  CD -- By the Hush, a folk-rock band.  (Ozier Muhammad for The newyork Times)

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
BRITISH TELECOM EARNINGS RISE
body: An increase in Internet use and cellular phone calls contributed to a 9.8 percent gain in British Telecommunications P.L.C.'s quarterly earnings to £534 million, or $853 million. But shareholders in the company, Britain's second-biggest telephone company behind Vodafone Airtouch P.L.C., sent its shares down 3.9 percent on fear that the company's plan to upgrade its network to allow new high-speed Internet services will cut into future profits. Andrew Ross Sorkin (NYT) http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Create Your Own 3-D Computer Body Image
body: Now the Internet wants your body as well as your soul. A new technology, developed by Adrian Hilton at the University of Surrey in England, allows people to create realistic three-dimensional computer images of themselves in a digital photo booth. The representations, called avatars, can be used as more lifelike digital personas in Internet chat rooms or in networked computer games. The first photo booth will be introduced at a digital imaging convention in Los Angeles next month. The booth takes four full-length photos of the individual, which are then mapped onto preprogrammed human forms. The resulting image is then put on a Web site and can be downloaded. There are, however, no safeguards to prevent anyone from using another person's form, so people in chat rooms can still pretend to be much better looking than they really are.   JENNIFER 8. LEE http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo: Several three-dimensional representations, known as avatars, of human models.

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Free Hard Drive Space Whenever You Need It
body: A start-up company in Santa Monica, Calif., is offering a free desktop hard drive service on the Internet. But like many Manhattan apartments, the virtual hard drive does not come with a lot of storage space. Founded this year, X:drive (www.xdrive .com) will give users 25 megabytes of remote hard drive space that is accessible from any computer with Internet access. The service is intended for users with high-speed access to the Internet, so those using traditional modems access might find X:drive slow, especially with large files. Unlike most previous Internet-based file storage services, X:drive is not on Web browsers for PC users. Instead, a special application for Windows 95 and 98 that creates a hard drive desktop icon to represent the virtual X:drive can be installed. Users can save documents directly to the drive or drag and drop files as they would to a C or A drive. Users of Macintosh and other platforms must use the slower Web-based interface. In an era of multigigabyte hard drives, 25 MB can hold only a few MP3's and a handful of Powerpoint documents. If you outgrow the allocated free space, $4.99 a month will buy an additional 25 MB.   JENNIFER 8. LEE http://www.nytimes.com

title: America Online and GTE in Internet Deal
body: America Online Inc., the world's largest Internet service, and the GTE Corporation, a local phone company that is being acquired by the Bell Atlantic Corporation, will offer high-speed Internet access to America Online subscribers in 17 states from Florida to Hawaii. Terms of the deal were not disclosed. The service, over GTE's asymmetrical digital subscriber lines, is expected to be 26 times faster than access with a computer modem through conventional phone lines. It will cost $20 plus America Online's monthly fee and be available to about four million homes by year-end. America Online has signed three other agreements with local telephone companies, including Bell Atlantic, to provide faster Internet access to its more than 17 million customers. America Online is trying to keep users from switching to rivals. Dulles, Virginia-based America Online's shares fell $1.9375, to $98.1875. Shares of GTE, based in Irving, Tex., fell 50 cents, to $74.9375. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
Metro Business;
Computer Hacking Case
body: Two former employees of Interactive Connections, now known as Screaming Media, were arrested yesterday on charges that they broke into the company's computer system and stole business plans. Ira Lee, 29, and Zissis Trabaris, 31, who had worked as software developers at the Manhattan company, were each charged with one count of unlawful and unauthorized computer intrusion. If convicted, each could face a prison term of up to five years. Interactive Connections provides news filtering and distribution services, mostly for sites on the World Wide Web. Its clients include America Online and Sun Microsystems, Federal prosecutors said. The men are accused of entering Interactive's computer system from Mr. Lee's home computer on Nov. 25, 1998, after their employment had ended, and copying proprietary files and software, then transferring the information to various computers that the two controlled. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Ebay Earnings Fell 70% in Second Quarter
body: Ebay Inc., the on-line auction company, said today that its second-quarter earnings fell 70 percent as it spent more to market its Web site and add more staff and computer systems. Net income fell to $816,000, or 1 cent a diluted share, compared with $2.73 million, or 2 cents a share, in the quarter a year earlier. Revenue rose to $49.5 million from $19.5 million. Before noncash and merger-related charges, Ebay said it earned $5.1 million, or 4 cents a share, compared with $5.2 million, or 5 cents a share, in the period a year earlier. On that basis, analysts expected Ebay to earn 3 cents, according to the First Call Corporation, which tracks company earnings. Shares of Ebay fell $3.4375, to $104.375, before the results were announced. In after-hours trading, its shares rose as high as $106.50. The fast-growing retailer has been promoting its site and making acquisitions to stay ahead of Internet rivals Yahoo Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. Ebay still has by far the largest number of auctions and registered users, giving it an edge over the competition, investors said. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
ON-LINE BANKING VENTURE
body: In a move aimed at cementing their position in the fast-growing Internet business, Sakura Bank and the electronics giant Fujitsu offered a plan to establish an on-line banking joint venture in Japan. It will be the first company specializing in on-line banking established by Japanese banks, most of which are suffering from bad loans. "We judge that now is a good time to start Internet business, with domestic Internet users expected to exceed 20 million next year," the president of Sakura Bank, Akishige Okada, said. http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CAROLINA POWER AND LIGHT MAY SELL ITS INTERNET UNIT
body: The Carolina Power and Light Company, which bought the North Carolina Natural Gas Company this month, said it might sell its Internet unit and focus on energy sales. Carolina Power, based in Raleigh, N.C., bought Interpath Communications Inc. in December 1997 for an undisclosed price. Interpath, which had 1998 revenue of $43 million, helps businesses in the Southeastern unitedstates set up Web sites and email and sells other Internet and telecommunications services. Carolina Power, which has 1.2 million electricity customers in North Carolina and South Carolina, has added new businesses because its main business, power sales, is opening to competition. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
WEBVAN GROUP RAISES $275 MILLION IN FINANCING
body: The Webvan Group, which operates the on-line grocery and drug megastore www.webvan.com, said yesterday that it had raised $275 million of financing from strategic and financial investors, representing a 6.4 percent stake in the company. The investments put a total value on the company, based in Foster City, Calif., and still privately held, of more than $4 billion. The investors included Softbank Capital Partners L.P., the Japanese-based software distributor and publisher; Sequoia Capital, a venture capital company, and investors associated with Goldman Sachs Group Inc. Earlier this month, Webvan announced it was placing a $1 billion order with Bechtel Group Inc. to design and build 26 automated warehouses across the unitedstates. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
OFFERING FOR SOFTBANK UNIT
body: Shares of the Softbank Technology Corporation soared on their debut on the Japanese over-the-counter stock market, as investors hailed the advent of electronic commerce stocks in Japan. Softbank Technology's first and only price was set at 40,000 yen ($342.76) -- more than eight times the issue price of 4,600 yen ($39.42). Softbank Technology, a wholly owned unit of the Softbank Corporation, the Japanese Internet pioneer, offers software and services related to electronic commerce over the Internet. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
FREE INTERNET ACCESS
body: A company that already offers Britons advertising-financed free telephone calls, Freedom Telecom, said it would introduce free phone Internet access in August, giving subscribers 60 minutes on line every day without charge. Freedom's offer is the latest in a series of moves by British Internet companies to drive down the cost of Web surfing. Freedom Telecom's managing director, Joshua Sayles, said he expected one million subscribers in the first six months of operation. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICAN EXPRESS BEGINS AN ON-LINE BANKING SERVICE
body: The American Express Company, which has products ranging from its signature green charge cards to traveler's checks, started an Internet bank yesterday, stepping into the on-line banking arena with its powerful brand name. The on-line banking service (www.americanexpress.com/banking) will take deposits, offer credit lines, give rebates on automated teller surcharges and provide free electronic bill payment, in addition to money market and checking accounts and certificates of deposits, American Express said. American Express's stock price jumped $3, to $137. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
INTELLIQUEST AGREES TO SELL DIRECT-MARKETING DIVISION
body: Intelliquest Information Group Inc., a technology market-research company, agreed yesterday to sell its IQ2.net direct-marketing division to Naviant Technology Solutions for $46.5 million in cash. IQ2.net owns a data base of Internet-user households and provides related marketing services. Intelliquest, based in Austin, Tex., will also enter a partnership with Naviant, a closely held technology consulting company in Newtown Square, Pa., to use the combined Naviant-IQ2.net data base for its Internet research. Intelliquest said it planned to focus on its main research and growing Internet businesses. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: WORLD TRADE;
BRAZIL ON-LINE BANKING
body: An agreement was reached between Banco do Brasil and ZAZ, the Internet provider owned by the Spanish company Telefonica S.A., to provide the bank's clients with limited free Internet access to promote on-line banking. The accord gives Banco do Brasil and ZAZ clients five free hours a month of web access. Banco do Brasil, Brazil's largest bank, with nine million customers, is negotiating similar agreements with Internet companies throughout the country. Its competitors, Banco Bradesco and Unibanco, two large private-sector banks, already provide sophisticated on-line banking services to clients. Simon Romero (NYT) http://www.nytimes.com

title: China Accuses Engineer
body: The police in China's southwestern city of Chengdu have arrested an engineer accused of divulging state secrets on the Internet, according to a report in the China Business Daily. The report said that an assistant engineer at a research institute posted articles about China's development of new style fighter planes on the Internet in May, and that the articles were widely distributed on Internet sites. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Circuit City on the Web
body: Circuit City Group, the No. 2 unitedstates consumer-electronics retailer, has begun selling on its Web site, www.circuitcity.com., with offerings of about 800 products, including camcorders, digital cameras, phones and vacuum cleaners. Circuit City said it would add more products before the Christmas season and would eventually include large appliances and personal computers. The company said on-line shoppers would be able to avoid shipping costs by picking up their orders at its stores. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Investment in Webhire
body: Webhire Inc., which produces Internet software to assist in corporate recruiting and hiring, said this week that Softbank Capital Partners L.P. had agreed to invest $20 million in it and buy 1.67 million Webhire shares from Amazon.com Inc. The investments -- a total of about $31 million -- will give Softbank, the Internet investment arm of the Softbank Corporation, the Japanese software distributor, a 40 percent interest in Webhire, which is based in Lexington. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
A New Place on the Internet To Explore Space's Wonders
body: On Tuesday, the 30th anniversary of the moon landing, no giant steps were made into space but a small step was made on the Web. Space.com, a new site devoted to the world beyond Earth, was officially launched in newyork. Space.com is the brainchild of Lou Dobbs, a former CNN executive who has had a lifelong fascination with space. "I used to watch the early attempts to launch rockets and sit there and watch all those Atlas rockets blow up," he said. The day was also supposed to see the launching of a new shuttle mission, the first to be commanded by a woman, Eileen Collins. After the flight was delayed, Sally Ride, the first American woman in space and a Space.com executive vice president, flew in from Cape Canaveral for the Web site's party. "At least I got to take part in one successful launch today," Dr. Ride said.   STEPHEN C. MILLER http://www.nytimes.com

title: Seeing Schizophrenia
body: To the Editor: Readers who are interested in obtaining a glimpse of the visual distortions caused by schizophrenia ("A Virtual Reality That's Best Escaped," July 8) need only use a search engine to find Web sites about "Wain's cats." Louis Wain was a prominent British artist at the turn of the century who was diagnosed with schizophrenia. His pictures of cats began as sweet, sentimental images of friendly, furry, purring animals. As his disease progressed, the cats in his paintings gradually became sinister, menacing, fierce, demonic and terrifying. When I studied general psychology, decades before the Internet existed, Wain's cat paintings were the accepted way of showing the visual distortions perceived by a mind being ravaged by schizophrenia.  ALFRED KOHLER newyork City, July 8, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title: MTV Makes a Music-Download Deal
body: The MTV unit of Viacom Inc. said yesterday that music buyers on its various World Wide Web sites would be able to securely download music as a result of an agreement with Rioport, a unit of Diamond Multimedia Systems Inc. Financial terms were not disclosed, but under the deal, MTV Networks Online will provide Web content and promotional support. It will also get an equity stake in Rioport and part of the revenue from selling digitally distributed music, which is expected to be available in the fourth quarter this year. Rioport will provide software to manage the music and take care of licensing, assemble content and receive Web-based promotions across all of MTV's on-line properties, including MTV.com, VH1.com, Nick.com, Sonicnet and a new music site not yet introduced, the Buggles Project. "Our audience demands and expects that we help them download music," said Fred Seibert, the president of MTV Networks Online. "Rioport provides us with the opportunity to be able to do so in a secure and easy way." The method, he said, is compliant with the Secure Digital Music Initiative, the music industry standard for downloading music from the Internet. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Yahoo Completes Deal
body: Yahoo Inc. said today that it had completed its of Broadcast.com Inc. for $5.05 billion in stock and options, adding audio and video programming. Yahoo will take a third-quarter charge of about $22 million for the acquisition. The company will exchange 0.7722 Yahoo share for each share of the Dallas-based Broadcast.com and will convert Broadcast.com options into 5.12 million Yahoo options. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
FREE INTERNET SERVICE
body: Bowing to the emergence and growing popularity of free Internet services in Britain, AOL Europe announced that it would introduce one next month. The company, a joint venture of America Online Inc. and Bertelsmann A.G., hopes to compete against subscription-free newcomers like Freeserve, a unit of Dixons Group P.L.C., which displaced America Online as Britain's most-used Internet service provider. Called Netscape Online, the new service will not replace America Online's other subscription-based services like AOL U.K. and Compuserve.   Andrew Ross Sorkin http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Marketers Set Test Of TV-Internet Link
body: Four large marketers said they would take part in a large study measuring the effect of a new technology on television viewing and Internet use. The participants in the study, commissioned by Worldgate Communications in Trevose, Pa., and conducted by Nielsen Media Research, are General Motors, the Kraft Foods unit of the Philip Morris Companies, Sprint and Warner-Lambert. The study, covering 1,000 households in Ohio, will test the effects of channel hyperlinking technology, which enables TV viewers to use the Internet through links tied to the programs they see.  http://www.nytimes.com

title: Reuters Shares Rise After Inquiry Ends
body: Shares of Reuters Group P.L.C. rose yesterday a day after it said that Federal prosecutors would not charge the company with improperly obtaining information from a big competitor, Bloomberg L.P. Reuters American depository receipts -- each representing six shares of the British company -- rose 62.5 cents yesterday, to $86.625, in Nasdaq trading. In London, Reuters shares rose 15 pence, to 918 pence. A Federal grand jury in newyork has been investigating the relationship between a Reuters subsidiary, Reuters Analytics, and Cyberspace Research Associates Inc., a newyork company set up several years ago by a former Bloomberg employee. Prosecutors were looking into whether Cyberspace Research assisted Reuters Analytics Inc. in improperly obtaining Bloomberg data that could have allowed Reuters to copy Bloomberg's analysis programs. Reuters said on Thursday that the unitedstates Attorney had told the company that prosecutors had closed the investigation.  The unitedstates Attorney's office in Manhattan declined to comment. The chief executive of Reuters, Peter Job, told The Associated Press the company was gratified that no charges would be filed. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Appointment by Times Co.
body: The newyork Times Company announced yesterday that Lynn O. Matthews, publisher of The Sarasota Herald-Tribune in Florida, will become president and chief operating officer of the company's regional newspaper group. The group, based in Atlanta, operates 21 newspapers in the South and in California. Mr. Matthews, 55, will assume his post upon the retirement of the current president, James C. Weeks, scheduled for the end of the year.   http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
SOFTBANK'S STOCK SOARS
body: After the company announced it would restrict its $15 billion investment portfolio purely to Internet companies, the shares of the Softbank Corporation surged to a record high. Softbank, which has stakes in more than 100 companies doing business on line, will begin realigning its portfolio by selling its 80 percent interest in the memory-chip-module maker Kingston Technology. Softbank also said it approved a decision by Ziff-Davis Inc., a publisher of computer magazines, to consider selling businesses to improve its stock price. Softbank holds a stake of about 69 percent in Ziff-Davis. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Another Venture in Art Auctions for Ebay
body: Greg Manning Auctions Inc. agreed today to form a venture with Ebay Inc.'s Butterfield & Butterfield unit to auction fine art and collectibles on Ebay's Internet site. Financial details of the venture, which is to make its debut this fall, were not disclosed. Greg Manning, an auctioneer of stamps and collectibles based in West Caldwell, said it would supply the items to be auctioned. Ebay is based in San Jose, Calif. The agreement is part of Ebay's move into high-end auction items, an effort begun with the April agreement to acquire Butterfield & Butterfield, one of the world's largest auction houses. Greg Manning is expected to add to the expertise in premium markets in North America, Europe and Asia that Butterfield & Butterfield has brought to Ebay. Greg Manning said that it would be a significant participant in the Ebay-initiated venture and that its brand name will be used. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Blowing the Whistle
body: To the Editor: "Addition to Consumer's Arsenal: Net Complaint Services for Hire" (July 8) omitted www.ftc.gov. People who think they've been the victim of a fraud should report it to the Federal Trade Commission on line; fraud complaints become part of Consumer Sentinel, an important database that is available to nearly 200 law enforcement agencies in the unitedstates and Canada.  JOAN Z. BERNSTEIN Washington, July 9, 1999  The writer is the director of the Bureau of Consumer Protection at the Federal Trade Commission. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMAZON REPORTS STAKE IN GEAR.COM, A SPORTS RETAILER
body: The on-line retailer Amazon.com disclosed yesterday that it held a 49 percent minority stake in Gear.com, an on-line discount sporting-goods retailer. The announcement came a day after Amazon.com began selling toys and electronics on its Web site. It also sells several other products, including books, music and videos. An Amazon.com spokesman, Bill Curry, declined to disclose the dollar value of the investment, which was made sometime before July 1. Gear.com offers close-out merchandise at 20 percent to 90 percent off retail costs. Both companies are based in Seattle. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
KOHLBERG KRAVIS BUYS 49% STAKE IN BIRCH TELECOM
body: Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Company agreed to pay as much as $110 million for 49 percent of the closely held telephone provider Birch Telecom Inc., the first telecommunications investment for the world's largest leveraged-buyout company. Kohlberg Kravis said it would pay $60 million initially for a 35.3 percent stake, with an option to increase that to 49.1 percent for another $50 million in nine months. Birch, based in Kansas City, Mo., was founded in 1997 and provides local and long-distance phone services, Internet access and World Wide Web site-host services in Kansas, Missouri and Texas. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
ONSALE TO ACQUIRE EGGHEAD.COM, A RIVAL ON-LINE RETAILER
body: Onsale Inc. agreed yesterday to buy a rival on-line retailer, Egghead.com Inc., for about $400 million in stock to create one of the Internet's largest sellers of computer equipment, electronics and software. Onsale will pay 0.565 a share, or about $12.70, for each Egghead.com share. The company will operate under the name Egghead.com and have an estimated $500 million in sales this year. Shares of Egghead.com, based in Liberty Lake, Wash., fell 31.25 cents, to $11.75, while Onsale, based in Menlo Park, Calif., fell $1.50 a share, to $21. Onsale's @Auction site holds auctions for products including PC's, electronics, sporting goods and vacation packages. http://www.nytimes.com

title: High-Speed Net Service Set for New York
body: The Bell Atlantic Corporation, the largest local phone company in the nation, plans to begin offering high-speed Internet services to newyork City customers today, seeking to get a jump on its cable television competitors. The service, called digital subscriber line, or D.S.L., can carry information more than 100 times as fast as traditional dial-up modems and also lets users make and receive phone calls while simultaneously surfing the Internet. Bell Atlantic and other local phone companies are pushing to roll out the new services to customers before competitors like Time Warner Inc. make them available through cable-television wires. In newyork, for example, Time Warner is set to team up with the AT&T Corporation to offer phone and high-speed data services. Bell Atlantic said the new high-speed services will be available today in parts of Manhattan and will be extended to other boroughs as well as Long Island. The company already offers D.S.L. services in parts of northern New Jersey. The cost of the service ranges from $49.95 for the slowest speed to $189.95 a month for the fastest, the company said. The newyork-based company's shares rose yesterday $1.50, to $63.75. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Locking the Door
body: To the Editor: "High-Speed Lines Leave Door Ajar for Hackers" (July 8) states that customers with dial-up Internet access receive a different I.P. address each time they dial in (known as "dynamic" I.P. addressing). In fact, many I.S.P.'s offer "fixed" I.P. addressing as an add-on for their dial-up customers, often (but not always) for an extra fee. The diagram with the article contains some real howlers in the example I.P. addresses given. The four numbers that make up an I.P. address must be between 0 and 255; each of your examples contains numbers larger than this.  AARON SHERBER Baltimore, July 8, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title: Purchase for Macromedia
body: Macromedia Inc., a maker of Web publishing and animation software, has agreed to acquire the closely held Elemental Software for about $24 million in stock to gain software for companies doing business on the Internet. The San Francisco-based Macromedia will pay about 625,000 of its shares for Elemental, which is based in Carlsbad, Calif. Its products including Drumbeat 2000 and eStore Builder. Macromedia had fourth-quarter sales of $44 million. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
EXCITE@HOME TO ACQUIRE IMALL FOR $425 MILLION IN STOCK
body: Excite@Home said yesterday that it had agreed to acquire iMall Inc. for stock valued at $425 million to expand its electronic commerce capabilities on the Excite Internet portal. Under the agreement, iMall stockholders will receive 0.46 Excite@Home share for each iMall share. Based on Monday's closing price, the deal values iMall's shares at $23.69. Shares of Excite@Home fell $1.5625, to $49.9375, and iMall slipped 31.25 cents, to $22, in Nasdaq trading. IMall, based in Santa Monica, Calif., is an electronic commerce services company. Excite@Home, based in Redwood City, Calif., provides high-speed access to the Internet via cable TV. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
VERIO AGREES TO ACQUIRE DIGITALNATION FOR $100 MILLION
body: Verio Inc., a provider of Internet services, said yesterday that it was buying the privately held Web host company Digitalnation Inc. for $100 million in cash. The acquisition will add more than 1,200 servers to Verio's network, which includes more than 260,000 Web sites. The company gave no further details of the transaction. Each of Digitalnation's servers is typically dedicated to a single high-traffic Web site. Based on revenues for the three months ended May 31, Digitalnation, based in Alexandria, Va., said it expected annual revenue of $9.4 million. Verio, based in Englewood, Colo., had revenue last year of nearly $121 million. Shares in Verio were up $2.15625 at $77. http://www.nytimes.com

title: MP3.com Raises Offering
body: The Internet music company MP3.com Inc. has raised the number of shares in its pending initial public offering to 12.3 million from 9 million. The new total includes 3.3 million shares for sale to Arkaro S.A., a unit of Groupe Arnault. MP3, based in San Diego, also said it intended to offer the shares at $16 to $18, up from the previous $9 to $11. MP3.com operates a Web site that distributes MP3 software, which compresses music into files that can be downloaded from the Internet and stored on personal computers. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Chief of Circulation Named by The Times
body: Scott H. Heekin-Canedy, vice president for strategic planning at The newyork Times, has been appointed the newspaper's senior vice president for circulation. He succeeds Richard H. Gilman, who was named by the parent Times Company yesterday to be publisher of The Boston Globe. Mr. Heekin-Canedy's appointment was announced by Janet L. Robinson, president and general manager of The Times. Mr. Heekin-Canedy, 47, has held his strategic planning post since 1997 and had been group director in that department since 1994. A 1974 graduate of Williams College, he has a Doctor of Laws degree from the Northeastern University School of Law and an M.B.A. in marketing and finance from Columbia University. http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo: Scott Heekin-Canedy

title: A Strong Debut for Liquid Audio Stock
body: Shares of Liquid Audio Inc., which sells software that lets consumers download music from the Internet, more than doubled today in their first day trading. The company based in Redwood City rose $21.5625, to $36.5625, as 9.3 million shares changed hands on the Nasdaq.  Lehman Brothers Inc. handled the sale. The company ended trading with a market value of $658.7 million. Liquid Audio sells software and services that give artists and music companies the ability to distribute music over the Internet. The company said its technology was used by such independent record labels as Beggars Banquet and Rounder Records. Liquid Audio has "all the right names behind it," said David Menlow, president of IPO Financial Network in Milburn, N.J. Liquid Audio sold 4.2 million shares at $15 each, raising $63 million, 59 percent more than expected. The sale represented a 23 percent stake. Investors include Hummer Winblad Venture Partners, a San Francisco-based venture capital firm, which owns about 15 percent of the company; the Intel Corporation, 14 percent, and Vulcan Ventures Inc., an investment company in Bellevue, Wash., with 6 percent. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CBS IS ACQUIRING 35% OF MEDSCAPE IN EXCHANGE FOR ADS
body: The CBS Corporation said yesterday that it was acquiring a 35 percent stake in Medscape Inc., an on-line provider of medical information, in exchange for $150 million worth of promotion over the next seven years. CBS has been expanding its on-line business by exchanging advertising on its television, radio and outdoor advertising holdings for stakes in small Internet companies. In the Medscape deal, CBS will work with the company to create a new health care site for consumers. The site is now geared toward medical professionals. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Computer Shock
body: To the Editor: My face began to twitch as I imagined the agony Dr. Edward Rothman was going through as he was trying to set up his new computer, get connected to the Internet, achieve his personal objectives and see the full potential of being on line ("Agony, Ecstasy, Agony: Enter the Computer," July 1). It's too bad no one informed Dr. Rothman of the one thing that would have prevented all of the stress and headaches in the first place. It's simple; he should have bought a Macintosh!  SEAN BRENNAN North Arlington, N.J., July 1, 1999   http://www.nytimes.com

title: Lycos and RCN Form a Strategic Alliance
body: The RCN Corporation and Lycos Inc. said today that they had formed a business alliance that would marry Web content developed by Lycos with RCN's high-speed telecommunications network. In the alliance, RCN, which is based in Princeton, an operator of a fiber optic network, will gain content for its 500,000 residential customers, most of them concentrated in the Boston-to-Washington corridor. For its part, Lycos, an Internet portal operator based in Waltham, Mass., will position itself for entry into the developing Internet broadband market. "The game will be won or lost, and brands will be made or not, in the analog environment," the chief executive of Lycos, Robert J. Davis, said in an interview. High-speed access "is an important component of our strategy now in the sense we're building broadband products," Mr. Davis added, "but as it relates to users it still has a few years ahead of it." Although it will be "another three, four, five years before broadband really hits its stride," Mr. Davis said, Lycos is using deals like the partnership with RCN to position itself as early as possible. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Behind Web's Success
body: To the Editor: Scott McNealy, the chief executive of Sun Microsystems, in his July 5 Op-Ed article defending Silicon Valley entrepreneurs, says that "Wall Street brokers, lawyers and career politicians have what I call nonjobs. They don't make anything other than money." Sure, many of us may be tempted to criticize lawyers, stockbrokers and politicians. Still, one wonders where Mr. McNealy would be without them. Who would handle the initial public offering for his company? Who would sue Microsoft in an effort to break its stranglehold on competition? Who would have paid for the initial technology that got the Internet going in the first place? If the Internet has taught us anything, it is that the next century's economy will require literate experts to turn information into knowledge.  WILLIAM ANTHOLIS Charlottesville, Va., July 5, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
WOLTERS KLUWER AGREESTO ACQUIRE BANKERS SYSTEMS
body: Wolters Kluwer unitedstates, a subsidiary of the Dutch publishing company Wolters Kluwer N.V., said yesterday that it had agreed to buy Bankers Systems Inc. of St. Cloud, Minn., a provider of legal documents, software and services for the financial services industry, for $190 million. Bankers Systems, with a customer base that includes 14,000 financial institutions, specializes in electronic and print forms for account, loan and retirement plan administration. After the deal, Bankers Systems, which posted revenues of about $100 million in the 1999 fiscal year, will become part of CCH Inc., a Wolters Kluwer unit that provides tax and business law information. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Motorola Unit to Add 1,400 Positions
body: The Network Solutions Sector unit of Motorola Inc. said today that it planned to create 1,400 positions in engineering and in research and development. Network Solutions makes and sells Motorola's cellular infrastructure and wireless communications systems. The company said it would recruit workers worldwide to fill research and development positions in Code Division Multiple Access, Global Systems for Mobile Communications, wireless local loop, integrated digital enhancement network and Internet protocol technologies. The company said the expansion was related to its plan for an all-Internet protocol-based platform for wireless systems. The Motorola unit said it had been working on the Internet protocol-based architecture for more than a year. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
BRITISH INTERNET PROVIDER SOLD
body: Cable and Wireless P.L.C. said it had bought Internet Network Services Group, Britain's largest independent Internet service provider, but did not state the price. The company also declined to comment on news reports of an imminent bid for Cable and Wireless itself. The reports spurred a 6.6 percent increase in Cable and Wireless stock to £8.33 ($13.1364). The Sunday Times of London said Cable and Wireless had been approached by would-be buyers including Deutsche Telekom A.G., France Telecom S.A., the Bell Atlantic Corporation and SBC Communications Inc.   Alan Cowell http://www.nytimes.com

title:
METRO NEWS BRIEFS: NEW YORK;
Cable Service Disrupted For 30,000 Customers
body: Cable television service for about 30,000 customers on the West Side of Manhattan was disrupted for several hours yesterday after a telephone-conduit maintenance crew severed a major underground television fiber-optic cable, a Time Warner spokeswoman said. The spokeswoman, Harriet Novet, said that the cable, at 45th Street and 11th Avenue, was cut about 9 A.M., blacking out service in an area bounded by West 40th and West 59th Streets, the Avenue of the Americas and 11th Avenue. She said service was restored, in stages, to most customers by 3 P.M. and to nearly all by 5 P.M. The cable -- actually a bundle of 30 fiber-optic lines, each supplying service to as many as 1,000 customers -- was cut by a crew employed by Empire City Subway Company, a subsidiary of Bell Atlantic that maintains telephone-wire conduits in Manhattan and the Bronx. Ms. Novet said that the affected customers were entitled to compensation for the service disruption, and that any who called would get credit. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
INTERNET INVESTMENT FUND
body: One of the world's top backers of Internet businesses, the Softbank Corporation, formed partnerships with Vivendi S.A. of France and Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation to invest in unitedstates on-line companies that are expanding overseas. Softbank, which is based in Tokyo, will receive investments totaling $300 million from the two companies for a new $1.2 billion unitedstates Internet investment fund. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
A Multimedia Site For a Multifaceted Man
body: Benjamin Franklin, the classic American overachiever, would surely be proud of The Electric Ben Franklin (www.ushistory.org/franklin), a Web site that has recently been introduced. Not only does it include the full texts of his autobiography and his contributions to The New-England Courant and the Declaration of Independence, but the site also features a few electronic liberties. Visitors are invited to watch videos of an impersonator expounding on what Franklin might have thought about the Internet. The Quotable Franklin page applies animation to the image of Franklin's face on the $100 bill. The result could be considered lifelike: his mouth is always moving.   LISA GUERNSEY http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Software Will Let You Mingle With the Crowd at a Web Site
body: Although email, chat rooms and instant messaging have turned parts of the Internet into a conversation parlor, surfing the Web is still a solitary activity. Or it was before Gooey, a new communal Web-surfing program. Gooey, which can be downloaded free at www.getgooey.com, places a rectangular box on your screen. When you visit a site, the box lists other Gooey people who are at the same site at the same time. You can then send messages to anyone else -- or everyone else -- who is scrolling through the site with you. You can also start what the originators of Gooey call "dynamic roving communities" by leading other members to sites that you are visiting. More than 32,000 people have downloaded Gooey since it came out in June, the company said. "It's like there are walls between those who are surfing the Internet," said Shai Adler, co-chief executive of Hypernix Technologies, Gooey's parent company. But with Gooey, he said, "there's a way to communicate." Gooey members also share something else: ads on the Gooey box.   LISA GUERNSEY http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
P.& G. and Yahoo To Expand Links
body: The Procter & Gamble Company and Yahoo Inc. said yesterday that they would significantly expand their relationship as P.& G. seeks to intensify its advertising and marketing efforts on the Internet. Under the agreement, for undisclosed financial terms, Yahoo is putting up Web sites for P.& G.  brands like Pampers (pampers.yahoo.com) and Pepto-Bismol (pepto.yahoo.com), as well as including P.& G. brands like Cascade, Dawn and Folgers in sampling programs like Welcome Home From Yahoo (realestate.yahoo.com). The deal gives P.& G. "the potential to be one of our largest advertisers," said Jeff Mallett, president and chief operating officer at Yahoo in Santa Clara, Calif. Procter also has Internet deals with America Online and Excite, while Unilever , a competitor, has deals with America Online and Microsoft. The goal is to develop campaigns that "truly enable us to reach consumers in new ways that become a relevant and integrated part of their lives," said Denis Beausejour, vice president for advertising worldwide at P. &G. in Cincinnati.  http://www.nytimes.com

title: Microsoft Offer On Net Service
body: The Microsoft Corporation, the world's largest software maker, is offering new subscribers who sign up for its MSN Internet access service a $400 credit to buy a personal computer. The offer is available through Staples Inc. stores and Microcenter stores, an MSN customer service representative said. Microcenter is a small consumer-electronics chain based in Ohio. Consumers must sign up for MSN for three years as part of the promotion, according to a Staples salesman. MSN's ISP service costs $19.95 a month. Microsoft's MSN Internet service has struggled to gain new subscribers and catch up to America Online Inc., the world's largest on-line service with more than 17 million members. MSN, which has an estimated 1.5 million to 1.8 million subscribers, is ranked No. 3 behind AT&T's WorldNet Internet access service and America Online, according to the market researcher Forrester Research Inc. The MSN special "is a decent deal," said Bruce Kasrel, a Forrester analyst. But, he added, "It's not enough to put them over the top." Mr. Kasrel said the three-year commitment to MSN service may make consumers wary because they do not like to be locked into contracts. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Intel Investment in London
body: The Intel Corporation, the world's biggest computer chip maker, will invest $48 million in an Internet server center in London to establish its first electronic-commerce hub outside the unitedstates. The center will have as many as 5,000 computer servers channeling millions of Web pages each day and will be built in the next 12 months, according to the Invest in Britain Bureau in London. Servers help manage computer networks. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
Rio to New Delhi, by Desktop;
How much do Web sites tell a traveler? Eight correspondents explore cities they know on the Internet
body: SIFTING through the many Web sites that offer tourists information about foreign cities can be fascinating or frustrating. How can first-time, English-speaking travelers planning a trip to Tokyo, for instance, know if a Web site is steering them in the right direction? Eight newyork Times correspondents offer their views of selected Web sites for cities they know well: Rio de Janeiro, Tokyo, London, Paris, New Delhi, Cape Town, Vancouver and Sydney. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
CHINA.COM OFFERING
body: An Internet provider partly owned by the state-run New China News Agency plans to raise $68 million with an initial public offering of stock next week in the unitedstates. The China.com Corporation is a hongkong-based Chinese-language Internet provider offering Web services, E-commerce and advertising for mainland China, Taiwan and hongkong. It registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell more than 4.2 million shares at $14 to $16 each in a Nasdaq stock offering. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
BELLSOUTH AGREES TO $5 BILLION CONTRACT WITH NORTEL
body: The BellSouth Corporation agreed yesterday to buy at least $5 billion of equipment and services from the Nortel Networks Corporation, as it seeks to update its worldwide networks with Internet technology. Nortel based in Brampton, Ontario, will supply BellSouth with equipment to handle wireless, data and Internet traffic over a 10-year period. BellSouth, based in Atlanta, is the dominant local telephone service provider in nine Southeastern states. It expects to sign a contract, the biggest ever for Nortel, by July 31. This year, it plans to spend $1 billion on Nortel gear. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Microsoft in Deal for Swedish Company
body: Skandia Insurance A.B., the top insurer in Scandinavia, said today that it had accepted a bid from the Microsoft Corporation of 1.1 billion kronor ($130 million) for Sendit A.B., a Swedish software maker, paving the way for a takeover. Earlier this month, Skandia raised its stake in Sendit to 20 percent, double the 10 percent needed to block a takeover under Swedish law. Last month Sendit urged shareholders to accept Microsoft's bid of 325 kronor a share, at the time a 41 percent premium. Skandia now owns 20.9 percent of Sendit. A purchase would give the world's largest software maker access to Sendit's main product, Internet Cellular Smart Access, which enables users to browse the Internet and send email over a cellular phone. Microsoft expects sales of mobile phones with Internet access to surpass laptop computers next year. Sendit's software is based on Microsoft's Backoffice platform using the Windows NT Server. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: AMERICAS;
LATIN INTERNET STAKE
body: A consortium that includes the Bear Stearns Companies; the Quantum Fund, headed by George Soros, and Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst, the Dallas investment firm, said it had paid $44 million for 35 percent of El Sitio, the Internet access provider. El Sitio, which had sales of $1 million last year, has 300,000 registered users and has bases in Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, Uruguay and the unitedstates. A Hicks associate, Cesar Diaz, said the fund considers El Sitio "the main gateway serving the Latin American market." http://www.nytimes.com

title: Apple Aid for Refugees
body: To the Editor: I was pleased to see coverage of how the Kosovo refugees at Fort Dix, N.J., are using the Internet to search for information on lost relatives ("For Kosovo's Scattered Refugees, the Internet Is a Lifeline," June 10).  One detail that was missing from the article was that the 12 computers at Fort Dix were iMacs, donated by Apple Computer. But I wonder why it was that Apple responded to those refugees' need and not the other, much larger personal computer makers? Too bad more computer makers don't "Think Different."  SUSAN M. SANDERSON Basking Ridge, N.J., June 14, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
HEALTHEON AND ITS MERGER PARTNER MAKE INTERNET DEALS
body: The Healtheon Corporation said yesterday that it would provide health care information to Yahoo Inc. under an Internet content and marketing agreement. Terms were not disclosed. Meanwhile, Healtheon's merger partner, WebMD Inc., said it would develop a health Web site with Reader's Digest Association Inc. Healtheon is acquiring WebMD in a stock deal currently valued at more than $8 billion. The combined company already has marketing and distribution deals with such outlets as Microsoft's MSN and WebTV, At Home's Excite, Lycos Inc. and Time Warner's CNN. Reader's Digest, based in Pleasantville, N.Y., said it had invested $13 million in WebMD as part of the pact. Healtheon's stock was up $5.75, to $88.25. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
METROMEDIA TO BUY ABOVENET FOR $1.55 BILLION
body: Metromedia Fiber Network Inc. said yesterday that it would acquire the Internet service provider Abovenet Communications Inc. in a stock swap worth about $1.55 billion. Metromedia said it would exchange 1.175 shares of its stock for each of Abovenet's shares. Abovenet's stock rose $4.0625, to $40.8125, and Metromedia's shares fell $5, to $37.50. Abovenet, which is based in San Jose, Calif., will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Metromedia, which is based in White Plains. Metromedia, which installs and leases fiber optic cables, said that together, the companies would be able to offer improved Internet access and telecommunications service. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Internet Camera to Capture The Best of Baby Videos
body: As if MP3 wasn't confusing enough, here comes MPEG-4. At PC Expo, Sharp Electronics introduced the Internet Viewcam, the first consumer product to use MPEG-4, a new video-compression format. That means you won't just be getting baby pictures over the Internet; you'll be getting baby video. The MPEG-4 format squeezes videos into files that can be quickly uploaded and downloaded from the Net over dial-up modems. The camera, which also works as a digital still camera, sells for $699 (available on line at www.sharp-usa.com), is slightly larger than a pack of cards and is 8.5 ounces with batteries and memory card. Because the videos taken with the Internet Viewcam are compressed, the movies aren't exactly theater quality. But Sharp expects a lot of interest in the camera and the format. "Which would you rather send in email?" said D. Michael Lyons, an associate vice president for marketing at Sharp. "One JPEG image or 10 seconds of video?" LISA GUERNSEY http://www.nytimes.com Graphic   Photo

title: Ebay Deal in Germany
body: Ebay Inc. said today that it had acquired the German on-line trading company Alando.de A.G. for an undisclosed sum. Alando.de, with more than 50,000 registered users, will operate under its current address before being changed to ebay.de later this year. It was Ebay's second move into Europe, where it already owns a British auctioning site. Ebay operates the most widely used American Internet auction. http://www.nytimes.com

title: MP3.Com Public Offering
body: The Internet music company MP3.com Inc. set the terms today for its initial public offering. The company said it would sell up to nine million shares of common stock for $9 to $11 each. The company's Web site is a major distributor of software related to MP3 technology, which compresses music into files that can be transferred through the Web and stored on personal computers or other electronic devices. MP3 has worried the music industry because it lacks copyright protection and a system for collecting royalties. http://www.nytimes.com

body: PANTRY INC., Sanford, N.C., a convenience store operator, agreed to buy the closely held R&H Maxxon Inc., Aiken, S.C., another convenience store operator, for an undisclosed amount.
