Shares of Flycast, based in San Francisco, surged 20 percent, climbing $7.50 each, to $45.50, in Nasdaq trading, while CMGI gained $2.1875 a share, to $102.50. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Intel Online Begins Web Hosting Service
body: The Intel Corporation started a subsidiary today that will operate corporate computing systems over the Internet. Intel plans to invest more than $1 billion in the new business, Intel Online Services Inc., which opened at a site near Intel's headquarters in Santa Clara, Calif. Intel said its initial customers included the e-Citi unit of Citigroup, Excite@Home Shopping Service, and NEC. Intel also said it was working with Web development companies including iXL Enterprises Inc., PricewaterhouseCoopers, Proxicom, Razorfish, US Interactive, and Uunet on the new venture. The on-line service, first announced by Intel in April, is the company's entry in the fast-growing market for so-called Web hosting. Such companies typically house and maintain a corporation's server computers at a remote site. By offering regular software updates, duplicate power sources and backup capabilities, Web hosts give their customers greater reliability and predictable costs for their operations. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Fidelity Plans Deal With Lycos
body: Fidelity Investment announced a partnership yesterday with the Internet portal company Lycos Inc. to provide Fidelity's customers with enhanced on-line services. The partnership links Fidelity, the huge Boston-based mutual fund and discount brokerage unit of the FMR Corporation, with one of the largest Internet on-line communities. The two companies are hoping to provide a one-stop investment site for Fidelity customers through a new on-line product called Powerstreet, which has been added to Fidelity's Web site at Fidelity.com. Powerstreet will allow investors to create personalized pages that will include on-line trading tools offered by Fidelity, as well as news and other content provided by Lycos. Lycos recently bolstered its financial content through a $78 million purchase of the financial information provider Quote.com, which offers investment data. Fidelity officials said Powerstreet was intended to benefit both active traders and the occasional on-line trader. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Merrill Planning For Late Trading
body: Merrill Lynch & Company plans to offer after-hours trading to its five million brokerage customers next year, the head of the firm's brokerage unit said at a conference in San Francisco yesterday. The announcement by John L. Steffens came two weeks after Merrill bought 14.3 percent of Archipelago, an electronic communications network. In addition, Merrill, the nation's largest securities company, added Internet trading in July for customers who pay a flat annual fee for an account that includes financial advice. No-frills on-line trading, for $29.95 a trade, will be available by the end of the year. "Clients are continuously asking, 'What have you done for me lately?' " Mr. Steffens told the Jupiter Communications financial services forum. "If you don't meet their highest expectations, they are going to drive their assets right to your competitor." In addition to Archipelago, Merrill owns stakes in three other electronic communication networks, Optimark Technologies; Primex Trading, an electronic auction market planned for 2000, and Brut, an electronic network introduced last year. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
ENGAGE TECHNOLOGIES AGREES TO BUY ADKNOWLEDGE
body: Engage Technologies Inc., an Internet marketing company controlled by CMGI Inc., agreed yesterday to buy Adknowledge Inc. of Palo Alto, Calif., for $193 million in stock to add customers and Web advertising services. CMGI, the unitedstates Internet venture fund company, will initially acquire an 85 percent stake in Adknowledge for $170 million in CMGI shares. Engage will acquire the remaining 15 percent of Adknowledge for $23 million in Engage shares. In the third step, Engage will issue $170 million in Engage shares to CMGI for the 85 percent stake in Adknowledge that CMGI bought in the first step. Adknowledge provides consulting and marketing software that helps advertisers plan and execute their ad campaigns. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
NETZERO, FREE INTERNET PROVIDER, SOARS ON FIRST DAY
body: Netzero Inc., which gives people free Internet access in exchange for agreeing to see on-line advertising, rose 82 percent in its first day of trading yesterday. The company, based in Westlake Village, Calif., rose $13.125, to $29.125. About 19.5 million shares were exchanged, making it seventh among the most active issues in the unitedstates. The company now has a market value of $3 billion. Netzero sold 10 million shares at $16 each yesterday, raising $160 million. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
I.B.M. AGREES TO ACQUIRE INTERNET SECURITY COMPANY
body: I.B.M. agreed yesterday to buy the Internet-security company Dascom Inc. for an undisclosed price to strengthen its on-line commerce business. Dascom, a closely held company with about 100 employees that is based in Santa Cruz, Calif., develops technology to help businesses safely connect computer systems to the Internet. "Security has been at the forefront of the discussion about E-commerce," said Megan Graham-Hackett, an analyst at S.& P. Equity Group who rates I.B.M. a "buy." She added: "It's definitely an area where they need to own that technology. They've probably discovered that." http://www.nytimes.com

title: America Online Near Record Growth
body: The Internet services giant America Online Inc. said today that its America Online and Compuserve on-line brands were on track to post record membership growth for the first quarter of 2000. The company said it expected its America Online service to exceed last year's growth, but did not provide details. In the fourth quarter of 1999, ended in June, the service added 685,000 new unitedstates members, up from 523,000 in the 1998 quarter. America Online has more than 18 million members worldwide. So far this quarter, its other Internet service, Compuserve, with a new software version, has added more than 300,000 subscribers in North America. Compuserve provides Internet access for more than two million members worldwide. The company, which is based in Dulles, Va., plans to extend its current $400 personal computer rebate program with PC manufacturers through the holiday season. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
CMGI to Acquire On-Line Company
body: CMGI Inc. in Andover, Mass., said yesterday that it had signed an agreement to acquire Adforce Inc. in Cupertino, Calif., an on-line advertising services company. Under terms of the stock-for-stock tax-free merger, estimated at approximately $500 million, CMGI will issue 0.262 CMGI share for every share of Adforce. Chuck Berger, 45, will continue as chairman and chief executive at Adforce, which has about 150 employees working with clients like Adsmart, Netscape and 24/7 Media Inc.  http://www.nytimes.com

title:
IN MY … DUFFEL BAG;
RICHARD S. BRADDOCK - Correction Appended
body: RICHARD S. BRADDOCK, the former Citicorp president who is now chief executive of Priceline.com, carries a small duffel bag instead of a traditional briefcase. He is a little embarrassed about that. It's sort of a triumph of optimism over reality because I put a lot of things in there," said Mr. Braddock, as he surveyed the bag. "It makes for a very sick, sort of bedraggled brief-case." Mr. Braddock, whose company lets Internet users bid for airline tickets, hotel rooms and other items, regularly shuttles between offices in Manhattan and Stamford, Conn. He uses the bag to stash magazines, a few crucial electronic devices and business documents he needs to peruse. "It's sort of exciting to go in there because I find things I forget about," he said. Among the discoveries are copies of three magazines - Business Week, Wired, and The newyorker - all of which he has yet to read. Standard items include a Palm Pilot, a dictaphone and a calculator. That calculator could come in handy. Although Priceline's stock has plummeted from a high of $165 a share earlier this year after initial public offering to $58.25, Mr. Braddock's stake is still hundreds of millions of dollars.   TIMOTHY L. O'BRIEN http://www.nytimes.com Correction  Pictures with the "In My . . ." feature last Sunday, showing Richard S. Braddock, the chief executive of Priceline.com, and the contents of his duffel bag, carried an incorrect credit. The photographer was Frances Roberts, for The newyork Times. Correction-Date: September 26, 1999, Sunday Graphic   Photo: WAITING FOR THE LOGO Mr. Braddock thinks about replacing this bag with on embroidered with the Priceline logo. But he may wait, he says, because switching "seems like a daunting task when I stare at the bag." FORMLESS BUT FUNCTIONAL He eschews traditional briefcases - the old-fashioned kind with hinges and hard sides - because owning one cause him to be "too diligent" about organizing. TWO'S COMPANY He uses another bag to carry "non-essentials," like office documents, to be read while traveling. (Rubdy Washington for The newyork Times)

title:
INVESTING: FUNDS WATCH;
Gauging the Reach Of Lower Commissions
body: Individual investors have seen stock-trading commissions plunge as on-line brokerage firms and the electronic trading networks compete with the major stock exchanges. But have mutual funds -- and fund shareholders -- seen any benefit? Maybe not. The Securities and Exchange Commission is reviewing stock-trading practices at a number of fund companies to see if they are getting the cheapest stock-trading commissions. Because funds trade in such large volumes, they have always paid less than individual investors. But rapid technological changes and the new competition faced by stock exchanges should be causing commissions to fall further. In a June speech, Lori Richards, director of the S.E.C.'s compliance office, described this review as "a series of inspections to learn how funds insure that they're getting 'best execution.' Best execution is not easily quantifiable," Ms. Richards said, "because it encompasses lots of factors." Chris Ullman, an S.E.C. spokesman, added last week: "The key here is to understand the usage of E.C.N.'s, and the extent to which customers are benefiting from lower costs that can be attained when trading." RICHARD A. OPPEL Jr. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Datek Sets Volume Mark
body: The Internet broker Datek Online said today that it had achieved a Wall Street first, executing 1,000 trades in the 90 minutes before the markets opened at 9:30 A.M. Datek said it had also extended its evening trading hours to 8 P.M., creating a 12-hour trading day for individual investors. The on-line broker trades through Island ECN. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD NEWS BRIEFING: AMERICAS;
INTERNET STAKE SOLD
body: A group of investors led by Morgan Stanley Dean Witter & Company paid $100 million for a minority holding in Latin America's largest Internet company. The purchase of the 12.5 percent stake in the company, Universo Online, a Sao Paulo-based venture with close to 500,000 subscribers, provides some of the capital it needs to expand in the Spanish-speaking countries of Latin America. Universo Online faces competition in Latin America from companies like the Microsoft Corporation, Psinet Inc. and America Online Inc. Simon Romero http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MEDIACONSULT.COM AGREES TO BUY PHYSICIANS' ONLINE
body: Mediconsult.com Inc., which provides health information and services on the Internet, said that it had agreed to buy the privately held Physicians' Online Inc. for $166.5 million in stock and the assumption of $13.5 million in debt. Mediconsult.com focuses on patients with chronic health conditions, like diabetes and asthma. Physicians' Online, based in Tarrytown, N.Y., offers services to 80,000 doctors, including access to medical data bases and email. Mediconsult.com, based in newyork, said it wanted to combine the two audiences. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
Metro Business;
Health Sites to Merge
body: Mediconsult.com Inc., which provides health information and services on the Internet, said it is buying Physicians' Online Inc. for $180 million in stock and debt. Mediconsult.com, based in newyork, focuses on patients with chronic health conditions like migraine headaches, diabetes and asthma, while Physicians' Online offers services to 80,000 doctors, including access to medical databases, news and email. Mediconsult.com said it wants to combine the two audiences, allowing it to offer features focusing on the doctor-patient relationship. Mediconsult.com plans to exchange 20 million shares of its stock for all the shares of Physicians' Online, which is privately held and based in Tarrytown, N.Y. The purchase is expected to close by the end of the year. http://www.nytimes.com

title: 2-Hour Crash at Waterhouse Net Trading
body: TD Waterhouse Group Inc. said yesterday that its trading system was down for nearly two hours, preventing the more than one million investors who use the firm from trading stocks through its Web site. The system crashed at about 10:30 A.M. and service was restored at about 12:15 P.M., a spokesman said. The spokesman said the crash occurred after Automatic Data Processing Inc., which routes buy and sell orders between the broker and the stock exchanges, encountered technical problems. The crash was the second at TD Waterhouse as a result of problems at Automatic Data. System crashes have occurred from time to time among on-line brokers as the surge in users has often overwhelmed their networks. John Hogan, president of Automatic Data's brokerage services group, attributed the failure to a malfunctioning component in its operating system. He said his group served about five or six on-line brokers, but he declined to identify them or say whether they had the same problem as TD Waterhouse. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Schwab E-Trade Is Interrupted - Correction Appended
body: Customers of the Charles Schwab Corporation were unable to buy or sell stock on line for about an hour yesterday because of computer troubles at the company, the nation's largest discount brokerage firm. Schwab said its systems were down between 11 A.M. and noon. Tracey Gordon, a company spokeswoman, said the cause of the problem was unknown. The San Francisco-based company handles about 147,700 on-line trades a day for its 6.2 million active investor accounts. Temporary failures are not uncommon among on-line brokerages, and are usually fixed within a few hours. Schwab charged customers the $29.95 on-line commission if they were forced to place their orders by telephone. Shares of Charles Schwab fell $2.9375, to $38.3125, on the newyork Stock Exchange. http://www.nytimes.com Correction  A headline in Business Day yesterday about an interruption of on-line trading at a discount brokerage firm referred imprecisely to the company. It was Charles Schwab; the mention of "E-trade" was not a reference to the E*Trade Group. Correction-Date: September 1, 1999, Wednesday

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MARKETING ALLIANCE WITH AMERICA ONLINE ANNOUNCED
body: CompUSA Inc. and America Online Inc. announced a marketing alliance yesterday under which CompUSA would begin selling computers with a custom keyboard that has a key for connecting directly to America Online. CompUSA, a Dallas-based retailer of personal computers and related products, said it would preload America Online and Compuserve software onto its PC's and sell the software in its stores. CompUSA will also offer classes at some stores on how to use the America Online software. Also under the deal, special rates for 24-hour CompUSA customer support will be offered to America Online and Compuserve members. CompUSA operates 210 stores in 82 unitedstates metropolitan areas. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING -- AMERICAS;
BRAZILIAN EXCHANGE EXTENDS HOURS
body: In an effort to recover trading volume that has migrated to the newyork Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq stock market, the Sao Paulo stock exchange will extend trading hours into the evening starting next month. The exchange, Latin America's largest, will allow electronic trading from 6 P.M. to 10 P.M. By catering to investors and brokerage firms that have begun trading stocks on line, the exchange hopes to offset the effect of a tax on financial transactions that has sapped volume.   Simon Romero http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Web Street to Go Public
body: Web Street Inc., an on-line brokerage firm, filed today with Federal regulators to sell up to $50 million worth of common stock in an initial public offering. Web Street, on line at www.webstreet.com, said its service was for investors primarily in the unitedstates and Europe. It said it could execute equity and option trades at low cost and provide real-time trading information, financial market data and account information. In a preliminary filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Web Street did not disclose how many shares would be offered or the estimated price range. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
National News Briefs;
Student Pleads Guilty In Software Piracy Case
body: A college student has pleaded guilty to illegally distributing movies, music and software programs from his Web site in what Federal prosecutors describe as the first Internet piracy conviction under a 1997 law. The student, Jeffrey Levy, was arrested after investigators found that thousands of pirated software programs and digitally recorded movies and music had been distributed through equipment at his apartment near the University of Oregon campus in Eugene, officials said. Mr. Levy, a 22-year-old senior, could get up to three years in prison and be fined up to $250,000. The 1997 law bans the reproduction or distribution of copyrighted works. Mr. Levy is to be sentenced on Nov. 22. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: ASIA;
E-COMMERCE VENTURE FOR CHINA
body: The News Corporation announced a strategic partnership between its joint-venture unit, the PDN Xinren Information and Technology Company, and the Oracle Corporation of Redwood Shores, Calif., to develop an E-commerce business in China. Under the agreement, Oracle will provide an Internet-based technology platform and E-commerce support services for Chinabyte, an Internet content provider begun by PDN. PDN is a joint venture between the News Corporation, the Australian media company led by Rupert Murdoch, and The People's Daily in China. Chinabyte.com specializes in information technology content. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CBS BUYS 38% OF ON-LINE JOB ADVERTISING SITE
body: The CBS Corporation said yesterday that it had acquired a 38 percent equity stake in Jobs.com Inc. in return for $62 million in advertising, promotion and other considerations on CBS media properties over five years. The privately held Jobs.com is a Dallas-based on-line jobs posting site. CBS said classified advertising is increasingly moving from the newspaper business to the Internet and that it believed Jobs.com was well positioned to benefit from the transition. CBS will hold two seats on Jobs.com's board. http://www.nytimes.com

title: COMPANYBRIEFS
body: COMPUWARE CORP., Farmington Hills, Mich., a developer of testing, management and development software, won a 10-year, $1 billion contract to take over information systems for the Detroit Medical Center, the academic health center of Wayne State University. AMERICA ONLINE INC., Dulles, Va., the Internet service provider, said it would invest in the closely held Tivo Inc., Sunnyvale, Calif., which sells a video recorder that lets subscribers skip ads.  GLOBALSTAR TELECOMMUNICATIONS LTD., newyork, which expects to start a satellite-based telephone network in September, said four of its satellites were launched yesterday on a Boeing Co. Delta II rocket. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Account Decisions By 2 Advertisers
body: Two on-line advertisers have made decisions on their accounts. Drugstore.com in Bellevue, Wash., said yesterday that it had named Fallon McElligott in Minneapolis as the first agency to handle the account of the company, an on-line pharmaceutical retailer. The decision came after a four-week review that had been narrowed to Fallon McElligott and other unidentified finalists. Billings were estimated at $30 million. Roxy.com in Marlborough, Mass., named three finalists in a review for its first branding account, with billings estimated at $10 million to $15 million. They are CGN in Boston, part of Epsilon Data Management; Gotham Inc. in newyork and Hanft Byrne Raboy & Partners in newyork. The review is being handled by Pile & Company in Boston and a decision is expected next month.  http://www.nytimes.com

title: Executive Leaves First Boston for Softbank
body: Two and a half years after he helped define the Internet brokerage industry by compiling its first rankings and statistics, Bill Burnham is leaving the Credit Suisse First Boston Corporation to become general partner of a new $1.2 billion venture capital fund of the Softbank Corporation. Mr. Burnham, 28, will join the Tokyo-based Softbank on Monday. He will be one of the new fund's four general partners, along with Ron Fisher, Charles Lax and Masayoshi Son, Softbank's chief executive. The fund will invest in companies that are likely to go public within a year and invest "opportunistically" in public companies, Mr. Burnham said. It has already made a half-dozen investments. Mr. Burnham will develop a research staff for Softbank and will be based in San Francisco before relocating to the company's main Silicon Valley office in Mountain View, Calif. Softbank, Japan's largest distributor of packaged software and hardware, has stakes in more than 60 Internet-related companies. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MICROSOFT OFFERS ON-LINE DISCOUNT AT COSTCO
body: The Microsoft Corporation said this week that it was offering MSN Internet access at a 40 percent discount to its regular price through the Costco Companies, a leading chain of warehouse-club stores, as fees for online services continue to fall. Three months of service are being offered for $35.97, or $11.99 a month, compared with MSN's regular fee of $19.95 a month, said Deanna Sanford, Microsoft's lead product manager for MSN. Microsoft, the world's biggest software maker, is moving to cut Internet access fees as it competes with the No. 1 on-line service provider, America Online Inc. In recent months Microsoft has formed partnerships with Staples Inc., Micro Center and Lan Plus Inc. to offer free PC's in exchange for MSN Internet service. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
24/7 MEDIA BUYS email MARKETER TO EXPAND DATA BASE
body: 24/7 Media Inc., an Internet advertising company, acquired the electronic-mail marketer Consumernet for $52 million to expand its data base of consumers' email addresses and spending habits. The closely held Consumernet markets consumer information. It has more than three million names in its data base, which includes in-depth profiles on consumers and their buying patterns. More than 125 Internet sites use the data base to tailor ads and promotions to individual site visitors. Adding Consumernet will allow 24/7 Media to offer advertisers and Web publishers a wider array of email marketing services. Shares of 24/7 Media fell $2.25 each, to $22.875. http://www.nytimes.com

title: E*Trade to Start 2 Mutual Index Funds
body: E*Trade Group Inc., the Internet brokerage firm, said today that it would start mutual funds based on electronic commerce and international indexes, bringing to six the number of its home-grown funds. E*Trade, based in Menlo Park, said its asset management unit had filed documents with the Securities and Exchange Commission to offer the two index funds, which will seek to mimic the performance of baskets of securities. One will be based on a Goldman, Sachs electronic commerce index, and the other will be based on the EAFE index of about 1,100 securities listed on the stock exchanges of 20 developed markets in Europe, Australia and Asia. Investors in the funds will need to establish an E*Trade account, and the funds will then communicate with investors primarily through electronic means, the filing said. E*Trade opened its first name-brand fund to investors in February, an S.& P. 500-stock index fund that attracted $30 million in assets in four months. In May it filed to create three other funds. Internet brokers are seeking ways to attract assets so they can continue to grow when trading slows. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Deal by America Online
body: The Wit Capital Corporation, an on-line investment bank, will offer after-hours stock trading through America Online Inc. under an agreement that gives Wit exclusive access to America Online's 17 million customers. Wit will pay America Online an undisclosed sum to be the sole tenant for six months on its after-hours center, which is scheduled to open by Nov. 1 as part of the company's personal finance site. America Online will sell ads for Wit and will promote securities research done by Wit. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE IN $100 MILLION PACT WITH CARD MAKER
body: America Online Inc. said it had reached a $100 million agreement making Americangreetings.com the sole provider of greeting cards on America Online's Web sites. The agreement, for five and a half years, extends an existing arrangement to the America Online Web services AOL.com, ICQ, Digital City, Netscape Netcenter and Compuserve, as well as America Online's services in Canada, Britain, Australia, Japan, Germany and France. The original deal covered only basic America Online service. Americangreetings.com is a unit of the American Greetings Corporation of Cleveland. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
INTERNET CURRENCY TRADING
body: Freeserve P.L.C., the British subscription-free Internet access provider, will introduce a way to trade currencies on line in the fall. Freeserve, which has just issued shares of the company to the public, hopes to replicate the success of on-line trading firms like E*Trade in the foreign currency exchange market by substantially lowering the commissions on transactions. Globalnet Financial.com, which developed the software to run the currency trading, will operate the Freeserve service, called Matchbook FX.   Andrew Ross Sorkin http://www.nytimes.com

title: America Online and GTE in Internet Deal
body: America Online Inc., the world's largest Internet service, and the GTE Corporation, a local phone company that is being acquired by the Bell Atlantic Corporation, will offer high-speed Internet access to America Online subscribers in 17 states from Florida to Hawaii. Terms of the deal were not disclosed. The service, over GTE's asymmetrical digital subscriber lines, is expected to be 26 times faster than access with a computer modem through conventional phone lines. It will cost $20 plus America Online's monthly fee and be available to about four million homes by year-end. America Online has signed three other agreements with local telephone companies, including Bell Atlantic, to provide faster Internet access to its more than 17 million customers. America Online is trying to keep users from switching to rivals. Dulles, Virginia-based America Online's shares fell $1.9375, to $98.1875. Shares of GTE, based in Irving, Tex., fell 50 cents, to $74.9375. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MESSAGEMEDIA TO BUY REVNET SYSTEMS FOR $66 MILLION
body: Messagemedia Inc. agreed yesterday to buy Revnet Systems Inc., a maker of direct email marketing software, for about $66.5 million in stock. Messagemedia, a provider of email-based marketing and customer relations management, said it planned to acquire Revnet of Huntsville, Ala., for about four millions shares. Messagemedia's shares were up $2.1875 each, to $18.4375. Messagemedia, based in Boulder, Colo., said it expected the deal to close in August. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: AMERICAS;
ROYAL BANK IN INTERNET DEAL
body: Royal Bank of Canada said it was teaming with America Online Inc. in a new Internet-based partnership and taking a 20 percent equity stake in AOL Canada Inc. for $60 million. Royal and its unitedstates subsidiaries will also forge marketing deals worth more than $7.5 million with America Online in the unitedstates and Canada. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Brokerage Chief Hired at E*Trade
body: E*Trade Group Inc., the Internet brokerage firm, hired Frank J. Petrilli, president and chief operating officer of TD Waterhouse Group Inc., to run its brokerage business. Mr. Petrilli, 48, succeeds Kathy Levinson as president of E*Trade Securities Inc. Ms. Levinson remains president and chief operating officer of the parent company, which is based in Menlo Park. Mr. Petrilli will have primary responsibility for retail brokerage, asset management and clearing. He will also oversee the firm's move into the institutional brokerage business through its $122 million purchase of TIR Holdings Ltd. as well as other acquisitions. At TD Waterhouse, which is 89 percent-owned by the Toronto-Dominion Bank, Mr. Petrilli helped manage the acquisition of the discount brokerages Kennedy Cabot and Jack White. TD Waterhouse said Keith Gray, a former executive who built TD Green Line, Canada's biggest discount brokerage, and played a role in Toronto-Dominion's 1996 acquisition of Waterhouse Investor Services, would assume Mr. Petrilli's role as chief operating officer. http://www.nytimes.com

title: MTV Makes a Music-Download Deal
body: The MTV unit of Viacom Inc. said yesterday that music buyers on its various World Wide Web sites would be able to securely download music as a result of an agreement with Rioport, a unit of Diamond Multimedia Systems Inc. Financial terms were not disclosed, but under the deal, MTV Networks Online will provide Web content and promotional support. It will also get an equity stake in Rioport and part of the revenue from selling digitally distributed music, which is expected to be available in the fourth quarter this year. Rioport will provide software to manage the music and take care of licensing, assemble content and receive Web-based promotions across all of MTV's on-line properties, including MTV.com, VH1.com, Nick.com, Sonicnet and a new music site not yet introduced, the Buggles Project. "Our audience demands and expects that we help them download music," said Fred Seibert, the president of MTV Networks Online. "Rioport provides us with the opportunity to be able to do so in a secure and easy way." The method, he said, is compliant with the Secure Digital Music Initiative, the music industry standard for downloading music from the Internet. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
WORLD BUSINESS BRIEFING: EUROPE;
FREE INTERNET SERVICE
body: Bowing to the emergence and growing popularity of free Internet services in Britain, AOL Europe announced that it would introduce one next month. The company, a joint venture of America Online Inc. and Bertelsmann A.G., hopes to compete against subscription-free newcomers like Freeserve, a unit of Dixons Group P.L.C., which displaced America Online as Britain's most-used Internet service provider. Called Netscape Online, the new service will not replace America Online's other subscription-based services like AOL U.K. and Compuserve.   Andrew Ross Sorkin http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
E*TRADE TO BUY TIR HOLDINGS OF IRELAND FOR $122 MILLION
body: E*Trade Group Inc., the on-line brokerage firm, said yesterday that it would buy the Dublin-based clearing firm TIR Holdings Ltd. for about $122 million in stock. E*Trade, which has alliances with many other international on-line brokerage firms, would further its global push by adding TIR, which is active in markets in more than 35 countries. E*Trade, which now caters to retail customers, plans to put its technology architecture on top of TIR's network so that institutional investors could also eventually make automated trades on its network. E*Trade's stock slipped 43.75 cents, to $37.875. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
TRAVEL ADVISORY: ATTRACTION;
For Would-Be Brokers
body: For on-line traders who want a glimpse of the real thing (and can still afford it), there's Stock Market Place in Toronto. The 6,000-square-foot exhibit, in the center of the financial district, recreates the bustle of floor trading with a global media wall and hands-on exhibits. Stock Market Place, 130 King Street West, Toronto, (416) 947-4676, is open Monday to Saturday 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. Admission $3.40, students and seniors $2, at $1.47 Canadian to the U.S. dollar. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Rushmore to Buy Two Day-Trading Firms
body: Rushmore Financial Group Inc. said today that it would buy two day-trading firms in a continued expansion of its on-line investing business. Rushmore, a financial services company based in Dallas, bought the closely held Millennium Daqcom/Dallas L.P. and Daqcom International L.L.C. for an undisclosed amount of cash and common stock. The firms, which have combined annual revenue of more than $4.1 million, provide and manage day-trading centers in Dallas and Houston. Last month, Rushmore bought a trading software company, Block Trading Inc., and a money management firm, the John Vann Company. title: Paperless Trading
body: To the Editor: Re "New Breeds of Investors, All Beguiled by the Web" (May 16), which looked at the types of people who use on-line stock trading: Nothing if not ironic was the accompanying illustration, which showed a dozen electronic "mice" scurrying out from under your stock-listings pages and heading for a hunk of cheese. title: Your Average Traders
body: To the Editor: Lori Aks Rosenberg (letter, May 7) writes that thanks to Internet trading, "the brokerages have finally eschewed snobbery and embraced the ordinary guy as a customer." Her "olden days" image of the millionaire tycoon at the ticker-tape machine is only partly true. Published in 1873, William Worthington Fowler's book "10 Years in Wall Street" told of the hard-sell efforts of stock promoters to push shaky oil and gold companies on working people. Investors would troop to brokerage offices on their lunch hours to collect dividends, only to hear that none existed. Brokers, stock promoters, mining and drilling executives all made plenty even if the ground yielded nothing. Today, regardless of innovations in law or the World Wide Web, the hard sell continues to scream the profit potential while whispering the risk. Internet trading can be like having a bookmaker or a croupier in your living room.  GREG DONIO newyork, May 9, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title:
INVESTING: DIARY;
Offerings on Line? Better Get in Line
body: Investors who signed up with on-line brokerages to get access to initial public offerings of stocks are instead getting a lesson in the laws of supply and demand. Last week, Andrew D. Klein, founder of the fast-growing Wit Capital, an on-line brokerage firm in newyork, sent a message to the company's 41,000 customers, asking them to stop calling to inquire about the status of newly offered shares they might be seeking to buy. "We appreciate that many of you are frustrated by the fact that you have not received allocations in our I.P.O.'s," the message said. "As we have told you in the past, the demand in the market has outstripped the supply." A lawyer for Wit declined to comment, because the company has entered the quiet period after the registration of its own initial offering. Also last week, The Wall Street Journal reported, 500 customers of Datek Online of Iselin, N.J., had their accounts credited with shares from Goldman Sachs Group's much sought-after initial offering on Tuesday, only to be told later that the shares did not exist. The mistake was a result of a "communications breakdown" with Goldman, said Robert O. Bethge, chief marketing officer for Datek. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Populist Stockbrokers
body: To the Editor: Arthur Levitt, the chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission, misses the point in his criticism of on-line brokerage advertising (Business Day, May 5). The brokerages have finally eschewed snobbery and embraced the ordinary guy as a customer. And thanks to the Internet, well-established brokerages are available to the small investor at reasonable fees. Mr. Levitt should be investigating why traditional brokers continue to charge outrageous fees to their trusting clients.  LORI AKS ROSENBERG Short Hills, N.J., May 5, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

body: Internet advertising more than doubled during 1998, according to a report for the Internet Advertising Bureau in newyork prepared by the New Media Group of PricewaterhouseCoopers. Internet ad revenue reached a record $1.92 billion last year, the report said, up 111.8 percent from $906.5 million in 1997. For the fourth quarter of 1998, ad revenue totaled $655.6 million, an increase of 33.6 percent from $490.6 million in the corresponding period of 1997. The ability of the Internet to blend "traditional brand building, retail sales and customer service in one place" is the reason that ad revenue "has grown so quickly," Rich LeFurgy, chairman at the bureau, said. "And we're expecting continued strong growth as traditional advertisers still sitting on the sidelines start to come on board."  http://www.nytimes.com

title: E*Trade Results Beat Forecasts
body: Outpacing the rapid growth of the on-line trading industry, E*Trade Group yesterday exceeded forecasts for the first three months of 1999 and reported financial results showing robust gains in revenue and new clients. Excluding a one-time gain of $20 million from an investment, E*Trade lost $14.3 million, or 12 cents a share, in its second quarter, which ended on March 31. While E*Trade, which is based in Palo Alto, Calif., earned $4.5 million, or 5 cents a share, in the corresponding period last year, the latest loss was smaller than the roughly 17 cents a share that analysts surveyed by the First Call Corporation had expected the company to lose. E*Trade's shares rose 21.7 percent yesterday in Nasdaq trading, gaining $16, to $89.8125, after plunging 50 percent in the last week amid a barrage of profit taking among on-line broker stocks. The company reported second-quarter revenues of $126.7 million, up 44 percent from the final three months of 1998 and more than double its revenue in the corresponding period a year ago. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
INVESTING: FUNDS WATCH;
Warding Off the Buying Hordes
body: Few mutual funds have benefited as much from the stock market's recent rally as Janus 20, the $26 billion fund whose strategy of holding 20 to 30 mostly large-capitalization growth stocks has more than doubled its investors' money since the beginning of 1998. In becoming essentially a proxy for the handful of stocks like America Online, Dell Computer and Microsoft that have fueled much of the market's rise, Janus 20 has also been one of the few large funds to significantly outpace the Standard and Poor's 500-stock index lately, attracting billions of dollars of money from new investors along the way. Not anymore. Citing fears that performance could be hurt if money continues to flow in, Janus says it will close the fund to new investors tomorrow, though not to existing shareholders and others who invest in the fund through certain retirement plans and financial advisers. While the fund is already up 20.5 percent this year -- after a 73.4 percent return last year -- Janus described the closure as "a proactive move to protect its ability to deliver superior performance."   RICHARD A. OPPEL Jr. http://www.nytimes.com

title: 850 Jobs Gone in America Online Merger
body: America Online, which said last week that it would dismiss 700 to 1,000 workers after its acquisition of Netscape Communications, announced this week that it has now eliminated 850 workers. The company, the big Internet service provider, made the cuts on Wednesday. About half came from its 10,000-member staff here; the others from Netscape's 2,500-employee work force, mostly at Mountain View, Calif. Early Wednesday morning, managers met face-to-face with those given dismissal notices. The dismissals were effective immediately, and most employees affected left the building soon after they were notified. America Online officials said the workers received a minimum of three months' salary and health benefits, plus an offer of help in finding employment. http://www.nytimes.com

title: JB Oxford Holdings Will Restate Earnings
body: JB Oxford Holdings Inc., an on-line brokerage firm, said today that it was restating earnings for the second quarter of 1998 after the Securities and Exchange Commission determined it must record an interest charge of $2.5 million. The stock of JB Oxford fell 62.5 cents, to $7.25, in Nasdaq trading. The shares had risen ninefold in less than a month, to $15.875 on Feb. 4, as investors snapped up on-line brokerage firms. The noncash charge against earnings stems from a May 1998 transaction when a group led by Christopher L. Jarratt gained control of the Los Angeles-based JB Oxford from a company led by Felix A. Oeri. Mr. Jarratt replaced Mr. Oeri as JB Oxford's chief executive. Mr. Jarratt's group invested $6 million and was issued $2 million of convertible debt, causing the interest charge, a company spokeswoman said. Including the charge, the company lost $2.8 million, or 20 cents a share, in the second quarter, compared with a loss of $309,000, or 2 cents a share, without the charge. In the second quarter of 1997, the company earned $105,000, or a penny a share. JB Oxford disclosed in January that it was under investigation by the S.E.C. and a Federal grand jury. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Nasdaq May Extend Trading Until 9 P.M.
body: The Nasdaq stock market is considering whether to expand trading hours to as late as 9 P.M., its president, Alfred R. Berkeley 3d, said today. A Nasdaq committee is also considering whether to open trading as much as an hour earlier, Mr. Berkeley said. Trading now starts at 9:30 A.M. and ends at 4 P.M. "It would be more convenient for American individual investors that want to trade," Mr. Berkeley said. "There's a consensus the market should be open till 9 P.M." The proposal is being driven by individual investors who want to trade on line after working hours, Mr. Berkeley said. Institutional investors and broker-dealers are able to trade after-hours on private trading networks. The newyork Stock Exchange has also said that next year it may extend its trading hours to between 5 A.M. and midnight. Nasdaq's Quality of Markets Committee will consider the proposal during the next one to three months before it goes to the board of the National Association of Securities Dealers, which runs Nasdaq, Mr. Berkeley said. If the association's board decides to proceed with the proposal, it would require approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission. http://www.nytimes.com

title: E*Trade Acquiring Another Web Site
body: E*Trade Group, the No. 3 on-line brokerage firm, said today that it had agreed to acquire Clearstation Inc., a financial World Wide Web site with 90,000 registered members. E*Trade, based in Palo Alto, said it would pay an undisclosed number of shares for Clearstation, which is based in San Francisco. The site being purchased, www.clearstation.com, was opened in July 1998 by Doug Fairclough, an Internet software developer, and Kris Skrinak, a former Wall Street trader and financial software developer. It offers technical and fundamental analysis tools, including message boards, personalized alerts and the ability to track multiple portfolios of stocks. E*Trade has gained almost one million registered members for its free Web site, www.etrade.com, since September 1998 as it tries to gain market share in the Internet brokerage industry. Its share of on-line trades last quarter grew to 11.8 percent from 10.9 percent, its first such gain in a year, according to Credit Suisse First Boston. Shares of E*Trade rose $2.0625 today, to $59.9375. The stock is up 53 percent in the last six weeks. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
INVESTING: DIARY;
DLJ Direct Takes On Japan
body: If Japan's still fledgling Internet trading business ever takes off, at least one American brokerage firm will be there to claim a piece of the pie. DLJ Direct, the discount subsidiary of Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette and one of the top on-line firms in the unitedstates, will begin a Japanese Internet securities firm with Sumitomo Bank, Japan's second-largest lender. DLJ Direct will own 50 percent of the new company, DLJ Direct SFG Securities, which will begin operations in June. Sumitomo Bank will own 20 percent, with the remaining 30 percent divided among a variety of Japanese companies. Japanese and foreign companies are expecting a boom in Japan's on-line securities business later this year, when fixed commissions are eliminated. As of February, Japan had just 36,991 on-line trading accounts. By contrast, the unitedstates has 5 million on-line investors, according to the American marketing company NFO Worldwide.  http://www.nytimes.com

title: Web Problems At Trading Firm
body: Waterhouse Investor Services Inc. shut off its Web trading service for almost two hours at the start of trading yesterday because of a data-processing disruption. Waterhouse customers could not make trades through the Web site from 9:30 A.M. until 11:10 A.M. because of the problem in files processed by Automatic Data Processing Inc., a spokeswoman, Melissa Gitter, said. The newyork-based Waterhouse is the second-largest on-line brokerage firm, after the Charles Schwab Corporation. "We did take the trading portion of the site down due to a processing error," Ms. Gitter said. "Every other portion of the site was available," including account balances and stock quotes, she said. Customers who could not trade on line could do so over the phone or at the firm's branches. Yesterday's disruption was the first since January for Waterhouse, which is owned by Toronto-Dominion Bank. Some other on-line brokers have had multiple shutdowns in recent months as industry volume has surged. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Arab Web Censorship
body: To the Editor: The Saudi Government has made no secret of its censorship of its citizens' access to the Internet ("The Internet's 'Open Sesame' Is Answered Warily," Riyadh Journal, March 18). But this is only the most recent such effort by a Middle Eastern government to block the flow of data in cyberspace. Iran and Bahrain block Web sites by political opposition movements; the United Arab Emirates blocks a site by a gay activist group, ; and Tunisia blocks sites by human rights groups. For more than a year Bahrain detained an engineer it suspected of emailing information to dissidents overseas. Elsewhere, governments have made Internet access too expensive for all but a small elite. Governments should not trample on international law protecting the right to receive and exchange information.  HANNY MEGALLY newyork, March 19, 1999  The writer is executive director, Human Rights Watch, Middle East and North Africa Division. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
Arab Web Censorship;
Pakistan Is Wired
body: To the Editor: "The Internet's 'Open Sesame' Is Answered Warily" (Riyadh Journal, March 18) implied that the Internet is banned in many Muslim countries, and is just now slowly being introduced in some of them. But the examples cited include only a few Middle Eastern countries and Iran. In Pakistan use of the Internet has grown quickly over the past five or six years. And Malaysia was planning a "cybercity" to attract business before the recent economic crises there. Even in Bangladesh, nonprofit organizations are providing Internet access to the poor. Conservatives all over the world are concerned about the effect of pornographic, racist and propaganda on the Web, including the unitedstates, where Congress passed the Communications Decency Act before it was declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in 1997.  SHAHBAZ CHAUDHARY Ann Arbor, Mich., March 18, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title: Glitches at Schwab And E*Trade Sites
body: On-line customers of the Charles Schwab Corporation and E*Trade Group Inc. had trouble buying and selling stock for a few minutes yesterday in the latest computer glitches involving Internet brokers. The Web site operated by Charles Schwab, the largest unitedstates discount and Internet broker, went down for about 15 minutes at 10 A.M., a spokeswoman, Tracey Gordon, said. The failure was the second in less than a month. Schwab receives about 60 percent of its trading orders through the site. E*Trade appeared to suffer a less severe failure, with only some customers having difficulty placing their orders. Lisa Nash, vice president for customer management, said the site never went down entirely. On-line brokers have struggled with numerous delays and failures in recent months as the exploding popularity of Internet trading has strained their computer systems. Schwab's mishap prevented customers from executing trades, reading analyst reports and reviewing portfolios, the spokeswoman said. Shares of Schwab, whose site went down for 20 minutes on March 1, were down $2.0625, at $86.4375. Shares of E*Trade were off $1.375, at $55.50. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
NBC and 24/7 In Marketing Deal
body: The NBC unit of the General Electric Company and 24/7 Media Inc. in newyork, a Web advertising company, have signed a three-year agreement to collaborate on television and Internet marketing plans for local advertisers. As part of the deal, NBC will take a small stake in 24/7 as 24/7 and NBC-Interactive Neighborhood, an on-line network of NBC stations featuring local community information, create ad packages for the local NBC stations and their Web sites. A nationwide sales staff based at the NBC stations and 24/7 offices will sell the ad packages. The alliance is part of NBC's efforts to find new revenue streams apart from traditional sales of commercial time.  http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
LOTUS PACIFIC TO BUY STAKE IN TURBONET COMMUNICATIONS
body: Lotus Pacific Inc., which offers on-line trading services and Internet access through television sets, agreed to buy 81 percent of the cable modem maker Turbonet Communications for $80 million in restricted stock as it seeks to broaden its customer base. Turbonet will not be able to sell the stock until it has annual revenue in excess of $30 million and pretax annual profit of $6 million. Turbonet, based in San Diego and partly owned by the Toshiba Corporation, currently has annual revenue of about $2 million. Lotus Pacific, based in Piscataway, N.J., offers Internet access though TV set-top boxes in hotel rooms. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Schwab Says It Settled Customers' Claims
body: The Charles Schwab Corporation, the biggest on-line broker, said today that it had settled claims from some customers who tried to cancel orders for shares in the fast-rising initial public offering of Theglobe.com Inc. Shares of Theglobe.com, which offers users the chance to build personalized Web sites, surged more than tenfold in the first day of trading, Nov. 13, to $97, from its offer price of $9, before closing at $63.50. They closed at $32.0625 two days later. About 1,500 Schwab customers tried to cancel orders to buy Theglobe.com shares before trading began, and Schwab was able to process cancellations from 1,200, a company spokesman, Glen Mathison, said. "We have been settling with those 300 customers," he said. In January, Schwab barred on-line trading of initial public offerings for the first 24 hours and limited the amount of shares in certain Internet stocks that could be bought using borrowed money. Schwab's shares rose $2.00 each, to $83. The settlements were first reported today in The Wall Street Journal. http://www.nytimes.com

title: COMPANY BRIEFS
body: DIGITAL COURIER TECHNOLOGIES INC., Salt Lake City, a developer of electronic-commerce software, agreed to acquire Databank International SKB, a credit card transaction processing firm, in a deal valued at more than $50 million. 24/7 MEDIA INC., newyork, said it had expanded its on-line advertising and marketing business by acquiring Sift Inc., Sunnyvale, Calif., a provider of email-based direct marketing services, for $22 million in stock.  SAFEGUARD SCIENTIFICS INC., Wayne, Pa., a technology investment and management company, will acquire an 80 percent stake in Aligne Inc., a technology-management consulting firm founded by Safeguard's president, Harry Wallaesa, for $17.6 million in stock. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
METRO NEWS BRIEFS: NEW YORK;
Spitzer Seeks Laws Protecting Web Users
body: Legislation to make it easier for Internet users to maintain on-line privacy and to fend off unwanted email was proposed yesterday by State Attorney General Eliot L. Spitzer. Concern about computer and software systems capable of discerning personal information about Web users has been increasing. The Manhattan Democrat said his bill would prevent companies from selling information about Web users without authorization. A companion bill is aimed at protecting users from mass transmissions of junk email. Mr. Spitzer would require marketers to provide identifying information with email and give consumers the chance to decline future transmissions. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
INVESTING: DIARY;
No Stopping the On-Line Parade
body: Investors keep funneling record numbers of stock trades through the Internet, and average trading volumes are expected to rise at least 25 percent in the first quarter of this year, an industry analyst said last week. Buoyed by heavy trading in shares of Internet companies, on-line brokerage firms should process an average of 425,000 trades a day in the first quarter, up from 340,000 a day in the fourth quarter of 1998, said the analyst, Bill Burnham of CS First Boston. The projected 25 percent increase in on-line trading is less than the 34 percent gain reported in the fourth quarter. That is because Mr. Burnham expects a slight decline in March, based on current trends. "It's a conservative estimate; actually brokerages are now running at a 30 percent growth rate," he said, adding that trading volumes were trailing off slightly in February after a very strong January. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
VERIO TO PAY AMERICA O NLINE FOR WEB SERVICES DEAL
body: The Internet-service provider Verio Inc. will pay America Online Inc. at least $42.5 million to become the on-line service company's exclusive operator of Web sites for businesses. America Online will also get a share of future revenue in the deal, which includes a Verio and America Online Web site that will offer Verio Web services and Internet commerce products, the companies said yesterday. Verio will receive on-line advertising and promotion of the venture. Verio shares rose $4, to $36.50, while America Online's fell 81.25 cents, to $86.25. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
Metro Business;
Spitzer Sets Up Unit To Look Into Internet
body: The newyork State Attorney General, Eliot L. Spitzer, is creating a bureau to investigate Internet matters, including on-line trading, consumer fraud, privacy issues and child pornography. Mr. Spitzer is already investigating, for example, the on-line brokerage E*Trade Group, whose stock trading system crashed four times over three days last month. "The Internet is rapidly becoming Main Street, Wall Street and a shopping mall all wrapped into one," Mr. Spitzer said. "We need to develop rules of the road that make it safe for consumers." newyork is the second state, after Pennsylvania, to set up an Internet bureau, he said. Mr. Spitzer said his office had received hundreds of complaints involving the Internet. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
Latest Land Rush: Virtual Real Estate;
What Users Don't Know
body: To the Editor: Re "Caveat Emptor on the Web: Ad and Editorial Lines Blur" (front page, Feb. 26): Barry M. Schuler, the head of America Online's flagship on-line service, argues that users don't care about the financial relationship between America Online and its content providers; "they care about whether it is convenient and does what they want it to." But how can users complain about lack of disclosure if they don't know that undisclosed financial relationships exist? The seeming "recommendation" is in fact a paid advertisement. The breach of the traditional boundary between editorial and advertisers took place a long time before the Internet came into existence. Many decades ago hobby magazines started reviewing products in ostensibly unbiased reviews. It was brought to a high art by some computer magazines in the 1980's, whose "editors' choice" selections were often bonanzas for the products chosen, and such selections were mainly portioned out among major advertisers.  RICK ROBINSON Marietta, Ga., Feb. 26, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title: Schwab's Web Site Fails Briefly Again
body: Customers of the Charles Schwab Corporation, the nation's largest discount and Internet broker, could not place stock trades through the company's Web site for about 20 minutes yesterday morning, its fourth computer system failure this year. Schwab's Web site went down for 20 minutes at 10 A.M., Eastern time, because of a software problem, said Tracey Gordon, a spokeswoman. Ms. Gordon said the problem was probably related to Schwab's efforts to increase the site's capacity. On Wednesday, Schwab's site went down for an hour and a half after the market opened because the firm tried to install a second mainframe computer to increase the site's capacity. Schwab will install the second mainframe computer over the next couple of weeks, Ms. Gordon said. The company suffered two brief computer system failures in January. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Web Ads and Footing the Bill
body: To the Editor: The article "But First, Another Word From Our Sponsor" (Feb. 18) heightened my concerns. My advertisement-free site for children, howtoloveyourdog.com, which to me is a labor of love and an extension of my teaching career, is seen by friends as a commercial opportunity. While I am content spending hours a day building and maintaining the site, there are costs involved. How to Love Your Dog teaches compassion, commitment and responsibility -- values we all want our children to develop. Will I sacrifice the presentation of those values by permitting advertising banners on at the top of my page? Finding the right balance of content and advertising is a challenge for everyone.  JANET WALL San Diego, Feb. 19, 1999 http://www.nytimes.com

title:
Metro Business;
Wireless On-Line Trading
body: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter & Company's Discover Brokerage, the seventh-largest on-line brokerage, has said it will offer customers the ability to trade stocks using wireless hand-held computers this spring. Discover said it was working with Aether Technologies International LLC of Owings Mills, Md., which has developed real-time trading software. Discover Brokerage customers who use hand-held computers with Palm Computing or Windows C.E. operating systems with wireless connections will be able to conduct trades, track accounts and receive real-time quotes from all unitedstates equity and options exchanges, the companies said. "There are vast opportunities for enterprises to gain competitive advantages through wireless data solutions," David Oros, president and chief executive of Aether, said in a news release. Fidelity Investments, the fifth-largest on-line broker and the biggest unitedstates mutual fund company, said Feb. 3 that its on-line investing customers could use certain wireless pagers to make trades. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MERRILL LYNCH TO PURCHASE D. E. SHAW UNIT
body: Merrill Lynch & Company confirmed yesterday that it had signed a definitive agreement to buy D. E. Shaw & Company's Internet technology unit as part of a plan to compete in the on-line trading business. Financial terms were not disclosed. Merrill Lynch said it expected to begin on-line entry of some customers' orders for securities and mutual funds in the next few weeks. The Wall Street Journal reported yesterday that Merrill Lynch was likely to pay $25 million to $35 million for the unit, D. E. Shaw Financial Technology L.P. Merrill Lynch intends to offer investors services, including trading, at roughly the same fees it now charges for securities sold through brokers, The Journal reported. http://www.nytimes.com

title: America Online Fills Job
body: America Online Inc. said today that Marc Andreessen, the co-founder of the Netscape Communications Corporation, would become America Online's chief technology officer upon the close of its acquisition of Netscape, expected to take place in the early spring. In the newly created position, Mr. Andreessen will report to America Online's chairman and chief executive, Steve Case. His responsibilities will include evaluating emerging technologies and reaching out to the wider technology community. Mr. Andreessen currently serves as Netscape's chief technology officer, and has served as a director on Netscape's board since April 1994. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Trading Activity Surges at Charles Schwab
body: The Charles Schwab Corporation, the nation's largest Internet broker, said today that the average number of trades a day on which it earned a commission was 184,000 last month, up 144 percent from a year earlier, as on-line trading soared. The San Francisco-based company's average daily trades rose 48 percent from December. The average daily number of on-line trades in January was 153,000. Investors put $8.8 billion of net new assets into Schwab, bringing the company's customer assets to $521 billion. The average number of trades customers place with Schwab a day is important since commissions account for about half of the discount broker's revenue. The gain came as the average number of shares changing hands daily on the newyork Stock Exchange rose 24 percent in January from December and 34 percent from a year ago. Schwab rose $3.6875 today, to $66.375. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
INVESTING: DIARY;
For Internet Users, Safety Is an Issue
body: What worries Internet users when it comes to trading stocks on line? Safety, first and foremost, according to a poll by CBS News and cbs.marketwatch.com. The survey, conducted between Jan. 27 and Feb. 2, found that security was the No. 1 concern of 35 percent of the 876 respondents. Execution of trades was the next-biggest worry, cited by 10 percent. Traditional publishers should take note: The quality of financial data available on the Internet was only the No. 3 concern, cited by just 6 percent. (Three percent cited all three.) Indeed, 80 percent of respondents said financial news and information available on the Web was as reliable or more reliable than that available from traditional sources. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
On-Line Advertising Doubles in Quarter
body: Revenue from on-line advertising more than doubled during the third quarter of 1998, according to a report released yesterday by the Internet Advertising Bureau in newyork, pushing total revenue above $1 billion for the first three quarters of last year. Third-quarter revenue was $491 million, an increase of 116 percent compared with $227 million in the period a year earlier, the association said, using figures compiled by PricewaterhouseCoopers in newyork.   http://www.nytimes.com

title: Closed Briefly For Some Repairs
body: E*Tra de, an Internet brokerage firm, had computer problems twice yesterday. Its World Wide Web site would not accept trades from customers for more than an hour in the morning, and sporadically in the afternoon. E*Trade, which handled an average of 42,000 trades a day in the last quarter, said that its business had hardly been affected. Kathy Levinson, the company's president, asserted that on-line trading companies are being held to a higher standard than brokerage firms have been in the past. "In the traditional way that people invested," she said, "it didn't matter if their broker was out to lunch. No one cared if their trade was placed at 10 A.M. or 11. There is a new breed of on-line trader, and higher expectations have been set." http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
BANK ONE AND AMERICA ONLINE SIGN CREDIT CARD DEAL
body: America Online Inc., the No. 1 on-line service, signed a five-year agreement to market credit cards over the Internet with the Bank One Corporation's First U.S.A. unit, the largest provider of Mastercard and Visa cards in the unitedstates. Through the agreement, First U.S.A. will pay American Online up to $500 million to be the provider of a co-branded card and be the exclusive marketer of credit card products and services on America Online, the Compuserve on-line service, AOL.com and AOL Instant Messenger in the unitedstates and Canada. The two companies established a co-branded Visa card in 1996, and the new agreement extends that connection. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Technology for Blind Users Even Reads the Internet Ads
body: This week I.B.M. started selling technology that allows blind users to hear the World Wide Web. Called Home Page Reader, the software, which costs $149, uses a speech synthesizer not just to read the text on a given Web page but also to describe the graphics and even advertisements. Other screen readers are capable of reading Web-page text. But Paul Luther, a manager with International Business Machines' special-needs unit, said the Home Page Reader was designed specifically with the Web in mind and tailored to reading pages built in HTML. "If there's a picture of a person on bicycle, the Home Page Reader will say, 'There's a picture of a person on a bicycle,' " he said. "Then the blind user can say, 'I'm not interested in this,' and move on." (And when there's a banner advertisement, it will probably say: "Loading, loading, still loading. Go take a nap; I'll call you in 20 minutes.") http://www.nytimes.com

title: Schwab Increases Technology Margins
body: The Charles Schwab Corporation increased to 70 percent from 50 percent today the amount of investor assets required to back up any of 23 Internet and computer-related stocks bought with borrowed money. It was Schwab's second increase in its maintenance margin since December, when the company, the biggest on-line brokerage operation, increased the required amount of assets backing investments in certain stocks to 50 percent from 35 percent. "Schwab is reviewing all their client accounts to look at their access to margin, and they're also protecting themselves," said Henry McVey, an analyst with Morgan Stanley Dean Witter. "They're taking an active stance to what has been a hot area for on-line retail trading." Many brokerage firms set their maintenance margin above the 25 percent required by the National Association of Securities Dealers. The N.A.S.D. requirement is different from the Federal Reserve's requirement that bars investors from borrowing more than half of a stock's value on a first-time margin purchase. Among the stocks affected are two rivals of Schwab in the on-line brokerage industry: E*Trade and Ameritrade Holdings. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
EUROMONEY PUBLICATIONS TO BUY INTERNET SECURITIES INC.
body: Euromoney Publications P.L.C. said it would pay $32.2 million for a controlling 80 percent stake in Internet Securities Inc., a Boston-based provider of on-line financial information about emerging markets. Euromoney, a British publisher of finance magazines, will also invest $11 million in Internet Securities to help the company expand. Euromoney said it did not expect Internet Securities, which lost $5.7 million in 1997, to be profitable until the fiscal year ending Sept. 30, 2001. Euromoney, based in London, is a unit of Daily Mail and General Trust P.L.C. http://www.nytimes.com

title: Group Moves to Limit Internet Music Piracy
body: In a move designed to cut down piracy of music on the Internet, three dozen software and hardware companies and on-line retailers plan today to endorse the use of a so-called certificates of authentication that would accompany songs and albums distributed digitally. Record companies and other authorized sellers of licensed music would be able to include the certificates, which would appear on a computer monitor when users open a music file, said Gerry Kearby, chief executive of Liquid Audio. His company makes on-line audio software and is a leader of the new group, the Genuine Music Coalition. Various factions in the record industry, including musicians and executives, are pondering ways to cope with what they say is rampant proliferation of pirated music files on the Internet. Mr. Kearby said the certificate will not prevent illegal copying, but is meant to help publicize the names of licensed dealers, provide links to their World Wide Web sites, and perhaps deter users from making unlicensed copies of music. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
INVESTING: DIARY;
Network Trading Gains
body: Electronic stock-trading networks that allow investors to buy and sell shares anonymously accounted for 28 percent of all Nasdaq trades in 1998, up from about 24 percent in 1997. Trading has exploded on such networks, called ECN's, leading even traditional brokerages like Merrill Lynch to invest in them. Merrill; Goldman, Sachs; Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, and the market maker Knight/Trimark Group own parts of Brut L.L.C., while Goldman and E Trade Group, the No. 2 on-line brokerage, each bought a 25 percent stake in Archipelago L.L.C. Reuters Group's Instinet was the biggest ECN, handling about 16 percent to 18 percent of the Nasdaq market's trades last year, said Bill Broka, Nasdaq's senior vice president for trading and market services. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
TRAVEL ADVISORY;
Letting Your Fingers Reserve a Campsite
body: Camping reservations for the most popular National Park areas can be made on the Internet, using a Visa, Mastercard or Discover credit card. The secure Internet address is reservations.nps.gov. The site, which was launched Jan. 5, provides data, including what is available, for 23 parks and 3 tours. Bookings may be made five months in advance. The service operates from 10 A.M. to 10 P.M., Eastern time. Reservations can still be made by telephone; the number for most campsites is (800) 365-2267; for Yosemite, it is (800) 436-7275, and for Carlsbad Caverns, Mammoth Cave and Frederick Douglass tours, (800) 967-2283. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
TRAVEL ADVISORY;
Ski Web Site Lists Resorts, Snow Reports
body: Winter-sports enthusiasts can now plan their vacations at www.skiresorts.com on the Internet. One feature of the site, begun in late October, is an online booking directory for more than 400 resorts throughout the world that allows comparison shopping and room reservations. The site also includes information about weather, snowfall, lift ticket prices and trail maps. In addition, about 2,000 vacation properties, including hotels, condominiums and rental homes, can be reviewed and booked directly. Twice-daily snow reports are provided for some 500 mountains, with hourly weather updates for more than 1,500 places.. Information about lodging, dining, transportation, child care and activities is available for featured ski towns -- currently Vail and Aspen, Colo.; Lake Tahoe and Mammoth, Calif.; Park City, Utah; Jackson Hole, Wyo.; Sun Valley, Idaho, and Whistler in British Columbia. Discounts are offered regularly on the site, and last-minute travelers can sign up for email alerts of special deals. A related site, www.mountainzone.com, provides news about skiing and snowboarding. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE ENLARGES ITS STAKE IN TEL-SAVE.COM
body: America Online Inc. has enlarged its share of ownership in Tel-Save.com Inc. to about 15 percent and said it had extended its marketing agreement with Tel-Save, a reseller of telephone services, by two years. America Online said it would make a $55 million investment in Tel-Save.com common stock at $19 a share and would exchange about $19 million in Tel-Save.com warrants for common stock. The investment will add to America Online's current holding of about 8 percent, according to Gabriel Battista, who became Tel-Save's president and chief executive yesterday. Since 1997, Tel-Save, which is based in New Hope, Pa., has sold phone services to the customers of America Online, which is based in Vienna, Va. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
E*TRADE ANNOUNCES 2-FOR-1 STOCK SPLIT
body: E*Trade Group Inc., the on-line brokerage company, said yesterday that it would split its shares 2 for 1. The stock split will double the number of diluted shares to 95.8 million, but halve their value. The new shares will be issued Jan. 29 to shareholders of record as of Jan. 15. E*Trade shares jumped 18 percent, gaining $8.65625, to $55.4375. Last week, the stock rallied after E*Trade said its free Web site had gained more than 500,000 registered users since September. E*Trade, based in Palo Alto, Calif., lost $15.7 million, or 33 cents a diluted share for the fourth quarter, which ended Sept. 29. http://www.nytimes.com

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
America Online Loses in Court
body: A Federal judge has rejected a request by America Online Inc. for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction to block Worldnet Service AT&T from using the Internet phrases "You Havemail," "Buddy List" and "I M," AT&T said today. America Online uses a similar phrase, "You've Got Mail," to inform subscribers that email has been sent to them. Buddy List and I M are used by the AT&T I M Here instant messaging service, which is available free to AT&T Worldnet Service users. The ruling, by Chief Judge Claude Hilton of the Federal District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, came in a hearing on Dec. 24. "We realize this is just the first round, but AT&T is confident we will also prevail at trial," said James Cicconi, AT&T's general counsel and executive vice president for law and government affairs. A representative for America Online could not be reached immediately. America Online must now proceed with the case on a regular schedule. http://www.nytimes.com

title: America Online Passes Milestone
body: America Online Inc. said this week that its worldwide membership had passed 15 million as the company, the No. 1 on-line service, attracted new members at a record rate because of a marketing campaign for its upgraded software. America Online, based in Dulles, Va., added one million members in seven weeks. The company said that on Christmas Day, it added more new members than on any other day in its history. America Online has been distributing millions of copies of its version 4.0 software in places ranging from gas stations to school cafeterias and is running television and radio advertisements. The service is also featured in the Time Warner Inc. film "You've Got Mail. America Online also operates Compuserve, an Internet service aimed at professionals and technology workers, with about two million members. http://www.nytimes.com

title: U.S. Relaxes Rules on Encryption Sales
body: The unitedstates Commerce Department said today that it had issued rules relaxing unitedstates export limits on data-scrambling technologies, considered vital for secure electronic commerce and Internet communications. These rules, which become effective on Thursday, carry out the policy changes announced in September by Vice President Al Gore. They end the need for licenses for sales of powerful encryption products to companies worldwide in several key industry sectors after a one-time review by the Commerce Department. The new rules virtually eliminate restrictions on selling powerful computer data-scrambling products to subsidiaries of unitedstates corporations. The rules relax controls for encryption products sales to health and medical organizations in 46 countries by almost all foreign subsidiaries of unitedstates companies as well as non-unitedstates companies. Privacy advocates have criticized the plan for helping big companies while ignoring concerns of ordinary Internet users.

title:
THE MARKETS;
Shift in S.& P. 500 Listing
body: America Online Inc., the No. 1 on-line service, will replace Venator Group in the Standard & Poor's 500-stock index effective after the close of trading on Dec. 31, S.& P. said. Internet stocks have been among this year's best performers, and the industry has experienced explosive growth in the last few years. The 500-stock index, the benchmark against which professional money managers are judged, currently has no Internet stocks. America Online, with a market capitalization of $63 billion, will be larger than all but 38 of the companies in the S.& P. 500. Venator, formerly the Woolworth Corporation, has a market capitalization of $924 million.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
DELL COMPUTER TO PRE-INSTALL AMERICA ONLINE SOFTWARE
body: The Dell Computer Corporation, the top direct seller of personal computers, said yesterday that it would use America Online Inc.'s on-line service as the default Internet provider on its consumer computers sold in the unitedstates and Canada. Dell began to ship America Online's software on computer disks with its Dimension and Inspiron computer systems yesterday. Early next year, Dell's computers will be pre-installed with the America Online service. Terms were not disclosed. America Online has signed agreements with other PC makers like the Compaq Computer Corporation to feature it as the default Internet provider. Dell said America Online would feature links to Dell's World Wide Web services.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AT HOME TO PURCHASE INTERNET ADVERTISING PROVIDER
body: The At Home Corporation, an Internet service provider, said yesterday that it had agreed to acquire the closely held Narrative Communications Corporation, a provider of Internet-based advertising, in a stock deal valued about $89 million. At Home will use Narrative's Enliven software and technology to create advertisements for the World Wide Web. At Home, based in Redwood City, Calif., provides Internet access through coaxial cable. At Home will issue between 1.34 million and 1.55 million shares of its common stock to acquire Narrative, based in Waltham, Mass.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Juno Online Services Taps DDB Needham
body: Juno Online Services L.P. in newyork, the Internet service provider owned by D. E. Shaw & Company L.P., named DDB Needham newyork to handle its integrated marketing account, which had been handled by Jordan McGrath Case & Partners in newyork. Billings were estimated at $20 million. The decision came after a three-month review that had been narrowed to DDB Needham newyork, part of Omnicom Group, and three other finalists in newyork: Bozell Worldwide, part of True North Communications; Draft Worldwide, a unit of Interpublic Group of Companies, and Fallon McElligott.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CENDANT EXPECTS TO MEET 1999 EARNINGS EXPECTATIONS
