body: The Cendant Corporation, the consumer services company humbled earlier this year by an accounting scandal, said yesterday that it expected to report earnings through the end of next year that were in line with Wall Street's expectations. Cendant, based in Parsippany, N.J., said it also planned to begin a previously announced $1 billion stock repurchase program. Excluding one-time charges, Cendant expects fourth-quarter earnings from operations to equal the 19 cents a share predicted by analysts surveyed by the First Call Corporation. It also said it might put up for sale its on-line businesses, including the interactive dating service Match.com, the book sales Web site Books.com, and Netmarket, an Internet shopping service.

title:
Metro Business;
On-Line Insurance Move
body: Hartford Financial Services Group said on Tuesday that it would join with Juno Online Services to sell auto and homeowner insurance on the World Wide Web. The company, which offers property and casualty insurance, said the five-year agreement with Juno, an Internet service provider, would let Juno users receive information and price quotes for insurance coverage on line. Hartford Financial said that it hoped to reach the growing number of people who use the Internet to shop for financial services. The company's Affinity Insurance Center in Farmington, Conn., which processes claims for its independent alliances with banks and organizations like the American Association of Retired Persons, will manage the on-line business.

title:
NEWS WATCH;
An Alliance With Netscape Will Add to AOL's Web Power
body: The Microsoft Corporation as the Internet's monolith? Think again. A new analysis of America Online's plan to buy Netscape might spare Microsoft the on-line-monopoly moniker. If the buyout goes through, Web sites owned by AOL will become by far the most dominant gateways to cyberspace, according to the survey, by Cyber Dialogue, an Internet research firm based in newyork. The company's report says that after an AOL-Netscape alliance, one in every three American adults would start each Web experience from an AOL-owned site. These sites would include AOL's proprietary service, used by 14 million people worldwide, AOL's home page on the Web and Netscape's Netcenter portal. That dominance won't be without challenges, however, said Thomas E. Miller, vice president of Cyber Dialogue. In particular, he said, AOL would have to fuse two vastly different cultures -- the newbies and neophytes of AOL with the relatively more sophisticated surfers who regularly log onto Netcenter. "The attitudes of the two audiences are really quite different," Mr. Miller said. "The challenge is going to be how to blend them."

title: Competition on the Net
body: To the Editor: You argue (editorial, Nov. 25) that America Online and Netscape merged because Microsoft somehow forced Netscape into dissolution, yet you leave out the fact that Netscape sold for more than $4 billion because of the phenomenal growth that both companies see ahead. That's a mighty price and a rosy philosophy for an industry in which you doubt there is sufficient competition. You conclude that "only when companies know they can get their products to the consumer will they have the incentive to innovate." America Online has 15 million subscribers. Netscape attracted AOL because it attracts millions of consumers to Netcenter, where people can download Netscape Navigator or Communicator. The reason there are thousands of companies starting up in this industry each year is because the Internet is the one sure bet in business today: You can get your product to consumers any time, anywhere.  ROBERT J. HERBOLD Chief Operating Officer, Microsoft Redmond, Wash., Nov. 30, 1998

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
New Program For Geocities
body: Geocities, which offers free personal Web pages to computer users, is introducing what is being described as its first major integrated communications program. The program, which includes print, Internet and radio advertising and a new corporate identity, begins tomorrow. The work is the first from Young & Rubicam Inc. in newyork, which was awarded the account, with billings estimated at $15 million to $20 million, in October. Y.& R. units including Young & Rubicam Advertising, Wunderman Cato Johnson, Landor Associates and Brand Dialogue are bringing out the program, which is centered on a new theme describing Geocities as "a virtual population explosion." The ads and corporate identity effort introduce a lower-case letter "g" to promote Geocities. The letter, with a dot inside to represent an eyeball, becomes a character displaying several moods. "We are convinced this effort will increase our visitor traffic," said Thomas R. Evans, president and chief executive at Geocities in Santa Monica, Calif. Geocities has 2.9 million users, or "homesteaders," who have created an estimated 22 million pages of personalized content in the company's on-line community.

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Visits to News Sites Decline, For Understandable Reasons
body: Major news organizations may wince at first glance at the latest figures on the decline in popularity of their on-line sites. According to Media Metrix, an on-line research company that compiles monthly figures on Internet usage, in October, MSNBC attracted 5.1 million visitors, down from 6.4 million in September. CNN dropped to 4.6 million from 7.1 million; USA Today to 3.3 from 3.9 and The newyork Times on the Web to 1.6 million from 1.8 million. Did the nation suddenly become less interested in daily events? Only temporarily, said Doug McFarland, senior vice president of Media Metrix. He said the declines seem so large because they follow a sharp rise in September, fueled by the publication of the Starr report and other revelations about President Bill Clinton and Monica Lewinsky. Graphic   Photo

title:
THE MARKETS;
New Options Exchangeto Start in 2000
body: A consortium of securities brokers and the on-line trading firm E*Trade Group Inc. yesterday announced the formation of a new electronic options exchange called the International Securities Exchange, which plans to begin operating in the year 2000. Participants in the venture include the Ameritrade Holdings Corporation, Herzog Heine Geduld Inc. and the Compaq Computer Corporation, the personal computer manufacturer. Memberships in I.S.E. have been sold to broker dealers organized under the umbrella of Adirondack Trading Partners, which is expected to provide I.S.E. with its initial trading business. The consortium is still raising operating funds and is awaiting approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission to go into business. The company plans to compete with established options exchanges like the Chicago Board Options Exchange that conduct business on traditional trading floors. Two of I.S.E.'s selling points are that it envisions reduced costs and faster execution than the traditional exchanges.

title: Finding Opponents on Line
body: To the Editor: I greatly enjoyed the article on on-line games ("I Don't Know Who You Are, but You're Toast," Oct. 29), but there are a few ways to find Internet opponents that were not mentioned. Some games use a feature called game trackers, free engines that search for on-line games in progress. They require no downloading besides the game and are very effective. Avara (www.ambrosiasw.com) by Ambrosia comes with a game tracker.  CHARLES GEORGE Davis, Calif., Oct. 29, 1998

title: AT&T Plans Internet Sales - Correction Appended
body: The AT&T Corporation said today that it planned to sell At Home Corporation's high-speed Internet access separately from At Home's on-line information services. The move would let customers access the Internet through At Home via cable lines and pay other companies like America Online Inc. for information. AT&T's chief executive, C. Michael Armstrong, said that the plan would be similar to agreements America Online had to sell its content to customers of other Internet access providers. Correction  A brief report in Business Day on Friday about AT&T's plans for the At Home on-line network misstated the sales arrangement. C. Michael Armstrong, AT&T's chief executive, said that while At Home's Internet access and information offerings would be sold as one service, other companies could connect to the network to offer At Home customers their services. He did not say At Home's Internet access would be sold separately. Correction-Date: October 31, 1998, Saturday

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Spending Growth Rate For On-Line Ads Slows
body: The increase in spending for on-line advertising during the second quarter of 1998 moderated somewhat from recent explosive gains, according to a report from the Internet Advertising Bureau in newyork. Marketers spent $423 million in the second quarter of this year, the association reported, using figures compiled by PricewaterhouseCoopers, up 97 percent from the $214 million spent in the second quarter of 1997. In the past, the quarter-to-quarter gains have been much larger; for instance, in the fourth quarter of 1997, revenue rose 206 percent from the fourth quarter of 1996.

title: America Online Adds 40 Retailers
body: America Online, the world's largest on-line service, said yesterday that it had added 40 new retailing partners, including Toys "R" Us Inc., to the shopping section of its on-line services, bringing the total to 11O. America Online, with 13 million members, has said 95 percent of the retailers who have agreements to sell on its service renew those partnerships. It noted that most of the agreements with its retailing partners extend to its Web site, www.aol.com, and to its Compuserve on-line service. The announcement appeared to be stoking the company's stock, which rose $2.125, to $124.125. Among the other new partners added to what America Online calls its Shopping Channel, are the retailer Macy's, which is owned by Federated Department Stores Inc. and the apparel maker Bugle Boy.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Microsoft Deal For Banc One
body: The Microsoft Corporation has signed a five-year, $90 million agreement with the First USA unit of the Banc One Corporation that is being described as the largest such deal involving Internet advertising. The agreement, to be formally announced today, makes First USA, based in Wilmington, Del., the exclusive credit card advertiser on most of the on-line programs and services on Microsoft's MSN network. Banner ads and other on-line displays asking computer users to apply for Visa and Mastercard credit cards issued by First USA are to appear on MSN properties like MSNBC, Hotmail, Carpoint and Expedia. "We think this is a pretty strong endorsement of the MSN as one of the pre-eminent distribution points on the Internet," said Charlotte Guyman, general manager for MSN sales, operations and marketing at Microsoft in Redmond, Wash. First USA, which is one of the largest Internet financial marketers, joins companies including Barnes & Noble, Lycos, Snap and Unilever as major MSN advertisers.

title:
National News Briefs;
Suit Filed to Block Internet Smut Measure
body: Attacking an hours-old Federal statute intended to restrict children's access to pornography on the Internet, a coalition of 17 organizations filed suit yesterday in Federal District Court in Philadelphia to block the measure, which they say violates the free speech provisions of the First Amendment. The measure, the Child Online Protection Act, was a small part of the budget bill passed by Congress this week and signed by President Clinton on Wednesday. It does not take effect for 30 days.

title: Congress Passes Anti-Piracy Bill
body: Legislation intended to protect books, music, computer software and other works from Internet pirates cleared its last congressional hurdle today, winning unanimous approval by the House of Representatives. The Senate approved the measure last week. It will now go to the White House, where President Clinton is expected to sign the bill into law. The main provisions of the legislation would shield telephone companies and on-line service providers from liability when a customer illegally transmits or posts copyrighted works on their networks. The bill is a compromise involving the telephone industry, on-line service providers and Hollywood producers and writers. The competing interests had been haggling for more than two years over the issue of when and under what circumstances a company would be liable for copyright infringement. The legislation would also make it a crime to circumvent technological protections used to prevent copying of copyright-protected works. The bill also retains the "fair use" principal -- which lets schools, libraries and others make limited copies of copyrighted works.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Trade Group Forming For Internet Issues
body: A group of Internet marketing and promotion executives have formed the Internet Direct Marketing Bureau in newyork, a trade organization that will address such issues as email advertising and on-line privacy. Paul Grand, 30, chief executive at Word of Net Promotions in Sherman Oaks, Calif., is heading a steering committee for the association, which will hold its first meeting on Nov. 11 in Scottsdale, Ariz. The new group plans to elect a chairman, president and vice president and hire an executive director in the next year.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Bertelsmann Online Names Ogilvy One
body: Bertelsmann Online in newyork, a unit of Bertelsmann A.G., said yesterday that it had named Ogilvy One Worldwide in newyork as the first agency to handle advertising for BOL.com, its on-line bookselling venture. Though billings were not disclosed, Advertising Age estimated them at $30 million. The decision came after a three-week review that had been narrowed to Ogilvy One, part of the Ogilvy & Mather Worldwide division of WPP Group P.L.C., and three other agencies in newyork: DDB Needham, a unit of Omnicom Group; Digital Pulp, and TBWA Chiat/Day, also owned by Omnicom.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Accounts
body: * Auction Universe, newyork and Yalesville, Conn., an on-line auction Web site owned by the Times Mirror Co., named two agencies to handle accounts with combined billings estimated at $10 million. Romann Group, newyork, will handle traditional advertising and Modem Media. Poppe Tyson, newyork, part of True North Communications, will handle creative and media placement for on-line advertising. Also, R/GA Interactive, newyork, another unit of True North, was named to handle Web site design. * Chasetel Wireless Communications, Chattanooga, Tenn., to Johnson Group, Chattanooga, as the first agency to handle its account. Billings were estimated at $4 million. Johnson Waterhouse, Chattanooga, will handle public relations.

title: Big Marketers Join to Upgrade Internet Ads
body: Seven top marketers are joining the At Home Corporation, which operates the At Home Network Internet service, to create and test the larger, more elaborate types of on-line advertising that were the subject of a meeting last month on interactive marketing sponsored by the Procter & Gamble Company. Susan Bratton, advertising director for the At Home Network in Redwood City, Calif., identified the marketers as the AT&T Corporation, the Bank of America unit of the BankAmerica Corporation, First USA, the Intel Corporation, Johnson & Johnson, Levi Strauss & Company and Toys "R" Us. The marketers will run ads that use so-called rich media techniques, which take advantage of the large bandwidth, or network carrying capacity, of At Home. Such ads are bigger than those now usually associated with the Internet and can offer animation, sound and full video. The test, to be conducted by IPSOS-ASI, a market research company in Stamford, Conn., and co-sponsored by Intel, will evaluate the effectiveness of the ads using traditional measurements like recall, awareness and intent to purchase the products advertised. Results are to be made available in December.

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Turning a Cursor Into an Ad But Mainly Just for Laughs
body: To view the newest form of advertising on the Web, you don't have to point and click. Just point and look. Comet Systems, a newyork company, has begun licensing software that can turn the cursor itself into any graphic or animation. Comedy Central, one of the cursor's early adopters, now offers the technology on its Web site to PC users (www.comedycentral.com). Visitors can surf with a cursor that looks like the animated character Kenny, from the show "South Park," or "Dr. Katz" from the show of the same name, or the comedy network's logo. Visitors to the site must first download the free Comet Systems software, which takes little more than 10 seconds (www.cometsystems. com). The year-old Comet Systems is marketing its malleable cursor as a way for companies to get their messages across in a pointed fashion. For instance, the 1-800-Flowers site is going to feature a cursor that morphs into a price tag when it is scrolled over certain sale items; other times is a red rose beside the numbers "1-800." Graphic   Photo

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
On-Line Ad Spending Seen Rising Tenfold
body: On-line advertising spending will reach more than $15 billion worldwide in 2003 from $1.5 billion in 1998, according to a report released yesterday by Forrester Research Inc. in Cambridge, Mass. The report, "Media's Global Future," predicted that on-line ad spending in North America would grow to $10.5 billion in 2003 from $1.3 billion in 1998. Spending overseas will be led by Europe, according to the report, where it will increase to $2.8 billion in 2003 from $105 million this year.

title: U.S. Cites Violation Of Internet Privacy
body: The Federal Trade Commission said that a popular site on the World Wide Web had lied to more than two million subscribers when it told them that it would not disclose personal information it had collected from them. In the Government's first enforcement action to safeguard privacy on the Internet, the commission said it had reached a settlement with Geocities, the company that runs the site, to stop making such promises. "Geocities misled its customers, both children and adults, by not telling the truth about how it was using their personal information," said an agency official. The company admitted no wrongdoing and was not fined for its actions. But it did post a new statement about how it uses the information it collects, including age, education, occupation, income and personal interests. Article, page A15.

title: Executive Changes
body: CENDANT CORP., Parsippany, N.J., promoted Mary Mahoney to president and chief executive of its Howard Johnson hotel chain, succeeding Stephen Phillips, who will become chief executive at the AFM Hospitality Corp. in Toronto. CREDIT SUISSE FIRST BOSTON, newyork, hired Jack Kirnan of Salomon Smith Barney Inc. as a managing director and deputy head of unitedstates stock research. E*TRADE GROUP INC., Palo Alto, Calif., the second-largest electronic brokerage house in the unitedstates, named Debra Chrapaty president and chief operating officer of its technology unit. She will still report to the company's chief executive and president, Christos Cotsakos.

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Firm Offers On-Line Trading For Chinese-Speaking Investors
body: Chinese speakers who may have felt left out of the on-line stock market can now buy and sell shares through a Web site run by Charles Schwab (www.schwab.com/chinese). The site, which was announced in an advertising campaign that began yesterday, focuses on Chinese-speaking investors in the unitedstates, China, hongkong, Singapore and Taiwan. People using Microsoft Internet Explorer 4.0 can download Chinese fonts that allow them to communicate with the brokerage in traditional or simplified Chinese.   TINA KELLEY

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Double Click Starts A Local Ad Service
body: Double Click Inc. in newyork, an Internet advertising network, is introducing a service to deliver local and regional ads to audiences of 70 Web sites. The service, Double Click Local, will combine the geographical capabilities of the company's ad delivery system, known as Dynamic Advertising Reporting and Targeting, and the network's 10 interest groups to enable advertisers to reach computer users on such sites as Alta Vista, Automobile magazine, the Food Network, Travelocity and U. S. News & World Report.

title:
Compressed Data;
Chat Software Company Joins America Online
body: Decisions of the digital age: What do you do when your small technology start-up is bought by America Online for $287 million? The founders of Mirabilis, based in Tel Aviv, know. They flew the entire staff to newyork for a weekend-long celebration. So on Friday, 68 Israeli software developers filled the back of Lot 61, a nightclub on West 21st Street in Manhattan, doing in real time what users of their product do on line: chat. Mirabilis, in its two years of existence, has developed a formidable following for its chat software, called ICQ -- short for "I seek you." The company says 14 million people have downloaded the free software, a figure that surely piqued the interest of America Online, the biggest Internet service provider in the unitedstates, which has about an equal number of members and a much larger marketing budget. The marriage of Mirabilis with America Online has raised the eyebrows of the company's faithful. To counter concerns that its essence would disappear under the America Online umbrella, Mirabilis has posted a letter on its Web site at www.mirabilis.com assuring users that the company's staff, spirit and free distribution will remain the same.   LISA NAPOLI Graphic   Photo: Steven Jobs of Apple Computer. (Associated Press)

title: COMPANY BRIEFS
body: ZAPATA CORP., Houston, said its Zap Corp. Internet subsidiary had agreed to acquire Coolchat Inc., Pleasanton, Calif., a free Web chat site with 300,000 members. Terms were not disclosed.  R. R. DONNELLEY & SONS CO., Chicago, a printing company, said the 450 employees at a Lackawanna County, Pa., printing plant might lose their jobs as the company considered its long-term future. TIGER MANAGEMENT L.L.C., newyork, a hedge fund run by Julian Robertson, and an affiliate reported that they hold a 10.1 percent stake in Federal-Mogul Corp., Southfield, Mich., a manufacturer of auto and truck parts.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
SOFTBANK OF JAPAN IN $400 MILLION ON-LINE DEAL
body: The Softbank Corporation, Japan's largest software distributor and an investor in on line companies, agreed to pay $400 million for 27.2 percent of E*Trade Group Inc., the biggest Internet-based brokerage firm.  Softbank paid $25.56 a share for 15.6 million new shares of E*Trade. E*Trade last traded at $24.50, down $1.0625, before trading in the stock was halted. E*Trade is the latest addition to Softbank's collection of Internet companies. The Tokyo-based company increased its stake in Yahoo Inc., the most-visited Internet directory, to 31 percent earlier this week. It also owns 35 percent of Geo Cities, a World Wide Web-based community, and 71 percent of Ziff-Davis Inc., a media company specializing in computers and software.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
VERISIGN BUYS SECURE IT, RIVAL IN INTERNET SERVICES
body: Verisign Inc., an Internet security company, said yesterday that it had acquired the closely held Secure It Inc. for about $69.1 million of stock. Verisign, based in Mountain View, Calif., issued 1.67 million shares to buy Secure It, a 20-month-old company based in Norcross, Ga., that provides Internet security consulting, testing and educational services to clients.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Unilever Developing On-Line Programs
body: Unilever, the British-Dutch consumer products giant, said yesterday that it had signed agreements with America Online Inc. and the Microsoft Corporation to develop interactive marketing and new media programs for brands including Lipton tea, Ragu spaghetti sauce and Dove soap. Though terms were not disclosed, the Daily Fax edition of Advertising Age said the spending was considerably more than $20 million over three years, a significant on-line advertising budget for a packaged-goods marketer. The America Online deal involves developing World Wide Web ads and promotions. The Microsoft deal gives Unilever access to advertising on Microsoft's on-line services as the two companies develop new ways to advertise consumer goods on the Web. Unilever will establish an Interactive Brand Center in newyork, staffed with marketing executives, Internet experts and information technology specialists, to help coordinate the alliances.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
2 Associations To Join Operations
body: The Internet Advertising Bureau in newyork and the Internet Local Advertising and Commerce Association in Oakland, Calif., said yesterday that they would combine operations under the bureau name. The more than 50 members of the association, which represents broadcasters, newspapers and others involved in local Internet services, will become bureau members, bringing the bureau's total membership to more than 300. The bureau will also form a Local Advertising Committee to be headed by Jim D'Arcangelo, 45, a founder of the association who is president of NFO Ad:Impact in Stamford, Conn. Rich LeFurgy, senior vice president for advertising at Buena Vista Internet Group in newyork, a unit of the Walt Disney Company, will continue as chairman of the bureau. Also yesterday, the bureau released figures for Internet ad revenue, showing that revenue in the first quarter of 1998 totaled $351.3 million, up more than twofold from $129.5 million in the corresponding period of 1997. And the bureau presented its first annual Marketer of the Year Award, which went to the Intel Corporation for leadership in the use of the Internet as an effective marketing tool.

title: Editors' Note
body: An article on Friday reported settlements by the Navy and America Online with a highly decorated sailor who was investigated by the Navy after he posted a computer message, under an anonymous email address, in which he described himself as gay. America Online, which divulged the sailor's real name to the Navy, agreed to pay him damages for violating his privacy. Under the Navy's part of the agreement, the 36-year-old sailor will retire with full benefits and with tens of thousands of dollars to pay his legal fees. The first paragraph of the article described the settlements as a "victory for gay rights." That phrase was supplied in editing. It failed to take the Navy's view into account. And it did not reflect any opinion expressed by the sailor, Master Chief Petty Officer Timothy R. McVeigh, whose lawyer has commented only on the privacy aspects of the episode. The Navy, which withheld comment at the time, now says the settlement was in no way a victory for gay rights, since the service was achieving at least part of what it wanted: the departure of Mr. McVeigh, because of what appeared to be a declaration of homosexuality.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
YAHOO BUYING VIAWEB, A WEB-MARKETING SOFTWARE MAKER
body: The Internet directory company Yahoo Inc. agreed yesterday to buy the privately held software maker Viaweb Inc. in a stock deal valued around $49 million. Yahoo, which is aiming to broaden its offerings, expects to incur a one-time charge of about $45 million in its second quarter relating to technology acquired in the deal. It plans to issue about 455,000 common shares in exchange for all Viaweb shares, options and warrants outstanding. Viaweb, based in Cambridge, Mass., has 21 full-time employees. It makes software for building and operating on-line commerce Web sites. Shares of Yahoo, which is based in Santa Clara, Calif., jumped $4.375 yesterday, to $109.375.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
E-TRADE AND SOFTBANK TO FORM ON-LINE CONCERN IN JAPAN
body: E-Trade Group Inc. will set up an on-line securities company in Japan with the Softbank Corporation to take advantage of deregulated trading commissions, the companies said. Softbank, based in Tokyo, will own 58 percent of the venture, which will be set up this month with capitalization of 2.7 billion yen, or $19.4 million. E-Trade, an on-line securities company based in Palo Alto, Calif., will own the other 42 percent. The venture, which will be aimed at individual investors, will handle transactions for stocks, bonds and other financial products, and will provide corporate and stock market data. It plans to start operations later this year, Nikkei English News reported.

title: America Online In a Settlement
body: America Online Inc. agreed today to pay $2.6 million to 44 states to settle complaints that it misled consumers about fees and phone rates. The states also contended that America Online made unauthorized charges to the accounts of some customers for books, software and services. The states, which range from Alaska to Florida, had investigated America Online's advertising practices for two years. The agreement comes more than a year after America Online was threatened with suits regarding service delays caused after it switched to a flat-rate fee. Under the settlement, America Online "must clearly inform consumers in advance whenever there is going to be a price increase or substantial service change," said the Attorney General of Massachusetts, Scott Harshbarger. America Online, which said the settlement was not an admission of wrongdoing, has worked with the states to improve its advertising, said a company spokeswoman, Tricia Primrose. "This is setting standards that the attorney generals intend to apply to the entire industry," she said. Shares in America Online rose $1, to $83.50.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Two Agencies Make Acquisitions
body: Two agencies made acquisitions yesterday involving interactive advertising. Arnold Communications in Boston acquired Circle Interactive L.L.C. in Boston and merged Circle with its Arnold Interactive unit to form a stand-alone agency that will operate under the Circle name. Terms were not disclosed. Eric Snyder, 40, and Dave Batista, 30, founding partners at Circle, will head the merged agency as president and chief creative officer, respectively. The merged Circle has 22 employees and revenue estimated at $3 million from clients like Bell Atlantic, Data General, McDonald's and Volkswagen. Arnold is a unit of Snyder Communications. And TMP Worldwide in newyork expanded its on-line career services by acquiring two career-advice Web sites, About Work and Student Center, from Ivillage in newyork for $1.7 million in cash. The sites will join TMP's present job data bases, the Monster Board and the On-line Career Center.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Accounts
body: * Canandaigua Wine Co., Canandaigua, N.Y., to Trone Advertising, Greensboro, N.C., to handle advertising and promotion for a new wine brand, Arbor Mist. Billings were estimated at more than $6.5 million for the first six months. Trone handles other Canandaigua brands like Mystic Cliffs wine, Paul Masson brandy and Cook's champagne. * Internet Shopping Network, Sunnyvale, Calif., a unit of USA Co., to I-traffic Inc., newyork, to handle on-line advertising and customer acquisition, previously handled in-house. Billings were estimated at $5 million to $6 million.  * Alpine Lace Brands Inc., Norwood, N.J., a unit of Land O'Lakes Inc., to the Ad Store, newyork, to handle advertising for the cheese and meat maker, which had been handled by Linnett & Harrison, Millburn, N.J. Billings were estimated at more than $1 million.

title:
NEWS WATCH;
Kodak and AOL Plan To Offer Photos on Web
body: In a bold move designed to revive its digital photography operation, the Eastman Kodak Company announced this week that it had joined with America Online in a service to be introduced in the fall. Kodak will permit AOL's 12 million subscribers to drop off rolls of films at any of about 30,000 photo-processing shops in the unitedstates. Once the film is developed, the images can be digitized and sent to their owners over the Internet as email. The service will be called You've Got Pictures, a twist on AOL's familiar digitized voice that beckons users to open their electronic mailboxes. In addition to sending pictures over the Internet, the service will also let users store their photographs in virtual albums as well as send them to others as email. Kodak, which posted $500 million in losses last year in its digital operation, has already turned to the computer chip manufacturer Intel to help it come up with a digital camera that might catch the consumer's eye. The company also bought Picture Vision, an on-line competitor, netting some 40,000 customers in the process.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Agency.com Buys Rest of Online Magic
body: Agency.com in newyork, an interactive marketing and communications agency, said yesterday that it had acquired the shares of Online Magic that it did not already own. Terms were not disclosed. Online Magic, an on-line services company with offices in London and newyork, was already majority owned by Agency.com. Online Magic, with 90 employees working for clients like General Motors and Hewlett-Packard, will become an autonomous subsidiary of Agency.com, which has 130 employees working for clients like American Express and Texaco. Eamonn Wilmott, 35, will continue as managing director of Online Magic in London. Andy Hobsbawm, 34, president of Online Magic in newyork, will relocate to London as chief creative officer for Europe.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
KODAK AND AMERICA ONLINE TO OFFER PHOTOS VIA INTERNET
body: The Eastman Kodak Company is expected to announce today that it is joining with America Online to offer developed photographs via the Internet. Starting this fall, America Online subscribers who drop film off with participating retailers can, for the charge of from $5 to $7, have small versions of their pictures uploaded directly to America Online within 48 hours. The America Online subscriber can put the pictures in on-line photo albums, and can electronically order prints. America Online, Kodak and the retailers will split the profits from the extra fees and from reprint orders. The system uses technology created by Picturevision Inc.; Kodak owns 51 percent of Picturevision, and America Online plans to buy 10 percent of the remaining shares.

title: Both Sides of Spam
body: To the Editor: This is in response to the article on spam ("The American Way of Spam," May 7). You put us in the same category as all spammers. We are not in the same category. Most people who send bulk email are sending either pyramid schemes or pornography. We take a strong stand against both. We refuse to send any type of scam or porn ad. We are not criminals. The criminals are those that threaten our lives, and the lives of our families, those that send viruses to our servers and try to crash our Web sites. If someone does not want to receive our mail, we give them the opportunity to be removed from our lists, and we honor those requests. I.S.P.'s say that no one wants to receive these advertisements. If this were true, then we would not be in business because nobody would respond to our ads. This is the first time in the history of advertising that a small business can be on a level playing field with a large company, and they don't like it.  JOE MELLE Norristown, Pa., May 12, 1998  The writer is president of TSF Marketing.

title: COMPANY BRIEFS
body: SOLECTRON CORP., Milpitas, Calif., an electronics maker, said it would buy I.B.M.'s electronic-card assembly and test centers. Terms were not disclosed. NETWORK ASSOCIATES INC., Santa Clara, Calif., said it had bought the closely held Secure Networks Inc., adding to its line of products that protect corporate networks from hackers or others who might steal data.  GEORGIA GULF CORP., Atlanta, a manufacturer of chemicals and plastic products, acquired the closely held North American Plastics, Jackson, Miss., a plastics manufacturer, for an undisclosed price.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Miscellany
body: * Greenfield Online Inc., Westport, Conn., a market research company, will offer a series of syndicated research studies about two markets: college students and homosexuals.

title: NEWS WATCH
body: STARBUCKS ON THE WEB -- Hardly satisfied with conquering the downtown corners of practically every major city in North America, the Starbucks Coffee Company announced this week that it was setting its caffeine-widened gaze on the Internet. Starbucks, a coffee giant based in Seattle, has turned to Organic, an interactive communications agency based in San Francisco, to help it create an on-line retail branch to extend its "Starbucks experience," a company spokesman said. Organic's chief executive, Jonathan Nelson, said the agency had done similar work for companies like Nike and Harley-Davidson.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Technology Accounts Are Awarded on Friday
body: There were two decisions on Friday involving two technology-related accounts, for which the billings were not disclosed. The Starbucks Coffee Company in Seattle named Organic in San Francisco as the first agency to handle its interactive account. The decision came after a two-and-a-half-month review that included nine other undisclosed agencies. And Paging Network Inc., a wireless communications network in Plano, Tex., named the Martin Agency in Richmond to handle its national account, which had been handled by various agencies on a project basis. Martin, a unit of the Interpublic Group of Companies, was awarded the account without a formal review.

title: Schwab on Line in Britain
body: The Charles Schwab Corporation said here today that its Charles Schwab Europe unit had begun an on-line investing service in Britain. Schwab said the on-line service would provide individual investors with trading, real-time prices, portfolio screening, market and economic news, comprehensive information on listed companies and historical price data and charts. Schwab had revenue last year of $2.29 billion.

title: America Online Alliance
body: America Online will announce an alliance today with thestreet.com, a financial news service on the World Wide Web. Under the arrangement, America Online subscribers will be given access to selected information from the Web site on a delayed basis, and offered a discount on its annual subscription fee. The alliance is the latest in a series of efforts to promote thestreet.com by James J. Cramer, a hedge fund manager who founded it with Martin Peretz, editor in chief of The New Republic, in late 1996.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
New Chief Executive For Link Exchange
body: Link Exchange Inc. in San Francisco, an Internet advertising network, has named Mark Bozzini to the new position of chief executive. Mr. Bozzini has handled sales and marketing duties for companies that include the Pete's Brewing Company in Palo Alto, Calif., where he served as president and chief executive, and the Seagram Company in newyork. Link Exchange counts more than 200,000 Web sites as members of its ad network.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
On-Line Advertising Spending Triples
body: Spending for on-line advertising more than tripled last year compared with 1996, according to a report yesterday from the Internet Advertising Bureau in newyork. Marketers spent $906.5 million in 1997, the association reported, using figures compiled by Coopers & Lybrand, compared with $266.9 million in 1996. In terms of quarter-to-quarter gains, revenue in the first quarter rose 333 percent from the first quarter of 1996; 313 percent in the second quarter; 200 percent in the third quarter, and 206 percent in the fourth quarter. Consumer-related products represented 31 percent of total on-line advertising spending, the report said, compared with 30 percent for computers and computing products, which had formerly dominated the medium. Financial services accounted for 18 percent, followed by telecommunications at 11 percent.

title: Excite to Acquire Advertising Site
body: Excite, the Internet search service, has agreed to buy Classifieds2000, a World Wide Web site that posts classified advertising, for $48 million in Excite stock. Like its larger rival, Yahoo, Excite wants to transform itself from simply a jumping-off point for Web surfers to a broader service with a variety of features that keep users lingering and reading its advertising. Local services, like classifieds and telephone "yellow pages" listings, represent big draws for users and large pools of potential advertising, said George Bell, the chief executive of Excite. Classifieds2000 allows individuals to post listings without charge, but charges fees to display classified ads from businesses. It also sells so-called banner advertisements, which are displayed prominently on Web sites. Helped by a surging stock price, Excite has made several acquisitions over the last year, using its own shares as currency. In October, it bought Netbot, a provider of Internet shopping software, for $35 million in stock. Then in January, it spent $89 million in stock for Match Logic, which provides demographic information to Internet advertisers.

title: Battling Junk email May Become Easier
body: Sendmail, the most popular software used to deliver email on the Internet, is getting a powerful set of tools to fight the junk mail known as spam, which is increasingly clogging cyberspace and filling mailboxes of Internet users with unwanted promotions on subjects as diverse as get-rich-quick schemes and pornography. The new version of Sendmail, to be announced today by its creator, includes a variety of anti-spam features, including the ability to reject mail from known spam addresses and a mechanism that will force spammers to disclose their real Internet addresses. Internet experts said the improvement could seriously crimp the ability of promoters to fire off millions of advertisements each day in the form of email messages. Business Day, page D1.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
CMG INFORMATION ACQUIRES ACCIPITER FOR $35 MILLION
body: CMG Information Services Inc. said yesterday that it had bought closely held Accipiter Inc. for $35 million in stock, adding technology that tracks on-line users to its Internet ventures. CMG, a direct marketer that invests in Internet companies, will combine Accipiter with its Engage Technologies unit, which sells market research on how people use the World Wide Web. CMG intends to use Accipiter's technology to increase advertising revenue at its ventures. The technology lets on-line advertisers change the ads that Web surfers see based on user profiles. Shares of CMG, which is based in Andover, Mass., fell 81.25 cents, to $57.75, in Nasdaq trading.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Internet Bureau Locates in New York
body: The Internet Advertising Bureau, an association for on-line advertising, has established a headquarters and named its first director. The association, which has more than 175 members, is locating its headquarters in newyork. Frank Dudley, president of FX Dudley Communications in newyork, becomes director of the bureau. Mr. Dudley, 36, will be responsible for overseeing operations like membership service and recruitment as well as supervising the association's Web site (www.iab.net). In addition, Rich LeFurgy, 41, was re-elected chairman of the association for 1998. He is senior vice president for advertising at ABC News/ ESPN Internet Ventures, a unit of the Walt Disney Company in newyork. Richy Glassberg, 34, vice president and general manager at Turner Interactive Marketing and Sales in newyork, part of Time Warner Inc., was re-elected vice chairman.

title:
Metro Business;
Stock Offering Increases
body: Doubleclick Inc., an Internet advertising company in newyork, increased the size and anticipated price range of its initial public offering yesterday, a day before the shares are expected to begin trading. The company now expects to sell 3 million shares at $16 to $17 each, according to an amended filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. In Doubleclick's original December registration, the company said it would sell 2.3 million shares at $12 to $14 each.

title: Cisco to Buy Wheelgroup for $124 Million
body: Cisco Systems Inc. said today that it had agreed to acquire the privately held Wheelgroup Corporation in a deal worth about $124 million. Cisco said in a statement that it would exchange between 1.8 million and 2 million shares of its common stock for all the outstanding shares of Wheelgroup. Based upon Cisco's closing share price today of $65.50, up 56.25 cents, the deal has a value of about $124 million. Cisco said it would take a one-time charge against its after-tax third quarter earnings of between 8 cents and 13 cents a share in connection with the acquisition. The deal has been approved by the boards of both companies and is expected to close by mid-March. Cisco said the acquisition of Wheelgroup would create a more secure environment for Cisco's customers to do business on the Internet. Wheelgroup makes intrusion detection and security scanning software products. Its technology delivers a radar-like intrusion detection system that identifies and responds to unauthorized intrusions and hackers. The majority of Wheelgroup's 75 employees will remain in their current offices in San Antonio.

title: America Online Reports a Profit
body: America Online Inc. yesterday reported a better-than-expected $20.8 million profit in the second quarter, one day after announcing a 10 percent membership fee increase to pay for upgrading its network. America Online, the nation's largest on-line service, said its profit resulted from lower marketing expenses, fees from 1.3 million new customers and higher ad revenues. The profit came even as America Online increased spending by nearly 50 percent to expand its network to handle the new members. The nation's largest on-line service plans a $2 increase in its $19.95 monthly fee in April and is also cutting 500 jobs in its newly acquired Compuserve unit. America Online said its profit in its second fiscal quarter, ended Dec. 31, amounted to 17 cents a share on a diluted basis, compared with a loss of $129.1 million, or $1.37 a share on a diluted basis, in the quarter a year ago, when the company recorded years of pent-up marketing costs. Overall revenues grew 45 percent, to $592 million from $409.4 million. The quarterly results slightly beat the 16-cents-a-share profit expected by analysts surveyed by First Call.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Razorfish Teams Up With Avalanche
body: Two newyork agencies that specialize in interactive advertising, Avalanche Systems and Razorfish, said yesterday that they would form a strategic partnership, as Razorfish is acquiring a majority stake in Avalanche. Terms were not disclosed. The deal comes as Madison Avenue's initial rosy view of the prospects for on-line advertising gives way to a more realistic perspective of the field as competitive and costly. The investment also follows reports in trade publications that Avalanche, which serves clients like Cosmopolitan magazine, Warner Music Group and Carnegie Hall, was seeking a partner to invest additional capital. Michael Block, 41, chief executive of Avalanche, is leaving to pursue other interests, the agency said; Jeff Dachis, 31, Razorfish chief executive, will also serve as Avalanche chief executive. Troy Tyler, 32, Avalanche operations director, becomes executive vice president and chief operating officer, and Peter Seidler, 39, continues as chief creative officer.  Razorfish clients include America Online, CBS, I.B.M., Sony and Time Warner. Omnicom Group in newyork owns a minority interest in Razorfish through Communicade, a unit devoted to interactive agencies.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Internet Ad Monitors In Strategic Alliance
body: Two companies are combining units that track advertising spending on the Internet as they agree to a strategic alliance. The Intermedia Advertising Solutions unit of Competitive Media Reporting in newyork, owned by VNU USA, will acquire the Adspend Data Report from Jupiter Communications in newyork. Terms were not disclosed. Adspend will be combined with Intermedia's Interwatch service to create a data base with information on ad spending on more than 325 World Wide Web sites. Joseph Philport, president of Intermedia, and Gene DeRose, chairman and chief executive of Jupiter, said the alliance would involve cooperative ventures between Competitive Media, which tracks ad spending for advertisers, agencies and media, and Jupiter, a leading Internet consulting company. Jupiter estimates that on-line advertising will total $1.4 billion in 1998, double the estimated $700 million spent in 1997.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
EXCITE AGREES TO BUY MATCHLOGIC FOR $120 MILLION
body: Excite Inc. said yesterday that it had agreed to buy the closely held Matchlogic Inc. for about $120 million in stock. Excite will exchange 3.2 million shares of its common stock for all of Matchlogic's outstanding stock. Excite's shares rose $4 each yesterday, to $37.50, making the deal worth $120 million. Matchlogic is expected to add $22 million in revenue to Excite in 1998. Excite, based in Redwood City, Calif., is the No. 2 Internet directory behind Yahoo. It said it would begin using Matchlogic's Internet advertising services on its site in March to improve targeting of advertisements. The services will also be used on Webcrawler, Excite's other on-line directory.

title: America Online Sues 3 on Junk email
body: America Online Inc. said today that it had sued three companies as part of its effort against unsolicited bulk email, also known as "spam." The lawsuit by the world's No. 1 on-line service, with 10 million subscribers, was filed in unitedstates District Court in Alexandria, Va. It seeks to prevent the companies from sending large quantities of unsolicited junk email to America Online subscribers, the company said. The lawsuit also seeks damages from all three companies. The companies named in the suit are IMS of Knoxville, Tenn.; Gulf Coast Marketing of Baton Rouge, La., and TSF Marketing and TSF Industries of Riverside, Calif. None returned phone calls seeking comment. According to America Online, the three companies have sent its subscribers tens of thousands of unsolicited email messages. America Online said that in a similar lawsuit it had won a Federal court order barring another company, Over the Air Equipment Inc., from sending unsolicited email to its subscribers.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Miscellany
body: * Double Click Inc., newyork, opened Double Click Iberoamerica, an Internet advertising sales network covering Portugal, Spain and Latin America, in a joint venture with Telefonica Publicidad e Informacion, a division of Telefonica, Spain's national telephone company.

title:
Updates: Media and Technology;
New Outlet for Hamill
body: One more editor, into the breach. Pete Hamill, the former editor of The Daily News, will write a regular column for Digital City NY, an entertainment and city on-line guide that will start on America Online and the World Wide Web early next year. Mr. Hamill joins a list of contributors that includes the playwright Wendy Wasserstein and the monologuist Spalding Gray. America Online Studios, the content arm of America Online, said Mr. Hamill will write "newyork Chronicles" monthly, with weekly updates. Digital City NY will offer information and commentary on topics ranging from resturants, off-Broadway shows and street fairs to bagel shops and sample sales, America Online said. In addition, the site hopes to distinguish itself from other city on-line guides "by raising the bar editorially with original content by quintessential newyorkers such as Pete Hamill," Guy Carcia, the site's executive producer, said in a statement.   ROBIN POGREBIN

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Fallon Sets Up Interactive Agency
body: Fallon McElligott in Minneapolis is opening Revolv, a stand-alone unit specializing in interactive advertising, by spinning off a department that creates World Wide Web sites for clients. Revolv opens with 30 employees in Minneapolis and 10 in newyork. Joe Duffy, 48, president and creative director at Duffy Design in Minneapolis and newyork, a division of Fallon, was named to the additional responsibilities of heading Revolv as president and creative director. Dorian Couglas, 37, founder of Network Frontiers in Minneapolis, the technology division of Fallon, was named to the additional position of chief technologist at Revolv.

title: EXECUTIVE CHANGES
body: CNET INC., San Francisco, an Internet information provider, named Douglas N. Woodrum its chief financial officer, succeeding Shelby Bonnie, who will retain the position of chief operating officer. TEXAS INSTRUMENTS INC., Dallas, said its vice chairman, William P. Weber, was planning to retire in April after 35 years at the company.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AXENT TECHNOLOGIES TO ACQUIRE RAPTOR FOR $250 MILLION
body: Axent Technologies Inc. agreed to acquire Raptor Systems Inc. for $250 million in stock. Axent, based in Rockville, Md., provides network security software and services. Raptor, based in Waltham, Mass., specializes in software known as a firewall, which connects a company's internal computer network with the public Internet without compromising security. Under the deal, Axent will swap four-fifths of a share for each Raptor share outstanding, issuing about 12.8 million shares. Raptor shares dropped $1.125, to $14.625, and Axent fell $1.75, to $19.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
2 Interactive Deals Are Announced
body: Two deals involving interactive advertising have been announced. Interactive Bureau, a Web site design company in newyork, and Lowe Bell Communications, an advertising and public relations agency in London, formed a joint venture to open an office of Interactive Bureau in London. Lowe Bell's parent, Chime Communications, will own 75 percent of the joint venture and Interactive Bureau will own 25 percent. Rodney Tyler, 54, a London journalist, was named to head the office as managing partner. And 360, a marketing company in Atlanta, will acquire and absorb Intellimedia Commerce Inc., an Atlanta company specializing in electronic commerce. Terms were not disclosed. Intellimedia, with more than 40 employees, was formed in 1996 by Cox Enterprises, American Software and Intellimedia Sports. 360 has 35 employees and billings estimated at more than $40 million from clients like the Coca-Cola Company. Ben Dyer, 49, president of Intellimedia, was named to the new positions of director for electronic commerce and chief financial officer at 360.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Miscellany
body: * Market Facts Inc., a marketing research information company, and Juno Online Service L.P. teamed up to create an interactive market research panel that will conduct surveys using the Juno email service.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE IN DEAL WITH TRAVEL SERVICE PROVIDER
body: America Online Inc. agreed yesterday to make Preview Travel Inc. its main travel-service provider. Preview will pay America Online $32 million over five years and will provide services that include ticket sales, car rentals and hotel reservations. Users can also customize information and do research. America Online and Preview will share advertising and transaction revenue, though America Online did not disclose how it would be divided. Preview Travel, based in San Francisco, said yesterday that it planned to sell 2.5 million common shares in an initial public offering, raising as much as $24.7 million. America Online, based in Dulles, Va., is the company's largest shareholder and will retain a 11.9 percent stake after the offering. America Online shares rose $3.375, to $83.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Accounts
body: * Qualcomm Inc., San Diego, to Ingalls Moranville Advertising, San Francisco, a unit of Davis Elen Advertising, to handle creative duties for Eudora email, which had been at Resource Marketing, San Francisco. Billings were $3 million. Media duties are handled by Susan Schermerhorn Media, San Francisco.  * Block Drug Co., Jersey City, to Publicis/Bloom, Dallas, a unit of Publicis S.A., to handle the Beano dietary supplement brand, which Block Drug recently acquired. Billings were estimated at more than $1 million. Block Worldwide, Radnor, Pa., handled the account for the previous owner of Beano, AkPharma Inc. Publicis/Bloom handles other Block Drug brands.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Sale of Unit Set By Knight-Ridder
body: Knight-Ridder Inc., a leading media company, is selling its on-line business information service, including its best-known brands, Dialog and Datastar, to M.A.I.D. P.L.C. of Britain for $420 million, the companies announced today. The new company will be renamed the Dialog Corporation. The purchase will create a global leader in on-line information, said Daniel Wagner, chief executive of M.A.I.D., which stands for Market Analysis and Information Database. Knight-Ridder has built the service's revenue from $99 million to $290 million in its nine years of ownership, including the 1993 addition of Datastar, a leading European provider of on-line information. Knight-Ridder said it would use the after-tax proceeds from the sale of the on-line business to reduce its debt and buy back stock. The Knight-Ridder unit provides on-line information and electronic, scientific and technical data. It also offers reference archives on areas including food and agriculture, energy and the environment, government regulations, medicine, news and general information.

title:
Government Plan Threatens Patients' Privacy;
Social Security on Line
body: To the Editor: Contrary to Stanley A. Spiegelman (letter, Sept. 10), the Social Security Administration's decision to use the Internet to provide earnings and benefits information is not headed for failure. This information is a valuable tool for retirement planning. When privacy concerns were raised, the agency took steps to strengthen security on the site, including holding public forums that solicited the views of experts on privacy, consumer advocacy, computer security and commercial Internet use. As a result, the Internet site will have security improvements sufficient to protect individual privacy.  SAWL WOOLFSON newyork, Sept. 11, 1997  The writer is a public affairs specialist, Social Security Administration.

title: New Investment Alliance
body: ETrade Group Inc. said today that it had agreed to form an alliance with the investment bank Robertson Stephens & Company to provide stock offerings and investment research through the Internet. ETrade is an on-line brokerage firm based in Palo Alto, Calif.

title: Presidential Adviser Sues America Online
body: Sidney Blumenthal, a Presidential adviser, today sued Matt Drudge, an Internet gossip columnist, and America Online Inc., which makes the column, the Drudge Report, available to millions of subscribers. Earlier this month, Mr. Drudge briefly posted on his Web site, and later retracted, anonymous allegations that Mr. Blumenthal "has a spousal abuse past that has been effectively covered up." Mr. Blumenthal's lawsuit, filed in Federal District Court for the District of Columbia, contends that Mr. Drudge knew the claim was false or made no attempt to check its accuracy. The suit seeks $10 million in compensatory damages and $20 million in punitive damages. It was filed on behalf of Mr. Blumenthal and his wife, Jacqueline Jordan Blumenthal, director of the President's Commission on White House Fellowships. Mr. Blumenthal's lawyer, William McDaniel, said in a statement that America Online also bore responsibility because it had contracted with Drudge to disseminate his report. America Online had no immediate comment. Mr. Drudge, who lives in Hollywood, could not be reached.

title: Knight-Ridder Near Sale of Unit
body: M.A.I.D. P.L.C., a British on-line provider of business information, said today that it was close to acquiring Knight-Ridder Information Inc. for what analysts said would be as much as $500 million. The combination of M.A.I.D.'s Profound news and research with the 650 specialty data bases of the much bigger Knight-Ridder would allow the company to halt the decline in its subscription revenue, analysts said. It also fits in with Knight-Ridder Inc.'s strategy of focusing on its more profitable newspaper business. Knight-Ridder Information's main on-line information products are Dialog and Datastar. The future of on-line data bases is also a question mark. Outlets for on-line information are popping up as fast as companies can set up Internet sites. Articles that cost $20 or more from an on-line vendor like Knight-Ridder are often free on the Web. Knight-Ridder Information's data base includes one of the most extensive bodies of on-line scientific and technical information.

title:
Metro Business;
Spending Increase Forecast
body: Total spending on entertainment and media products in the unitedstates will rise 44 percent by 2001, paced by a rapid increase in consumer on-line spending and advertising, according to an industry forecast. Veronis, Suhler & Associates, a newyork investment firm, said consumer and corporate spending on magazines, newspapers, videos and related advertising would increase to $419.6 billion in 2001, from $290.7 billion in 1996. The firm said this market will be the third-fastest growing industry in the nation over the next five years, behind telecommunications and educational services.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
INVESTMENT FIRM ADDING AMERICAN LAWYER
body: Wasserstein Perella, the investment banking firm, is acquiring the magazine The American Lawyer and its sister publications from Time Warner Inc. Time Warner announced in February that it was buying out the stake in American Lawyer Media L.P. held by its founder, Steven Brill, and also said that it intended to sell the magazines. Yesterday's sale does not include the Court TV cable network. Time Warner bought out Mr. Brill's stake in the cable network when it purchased American Lawyer. American Lawyer Media includes The American Lawyer, which Mr. Brill began in 1979, the Counsel Connect lawyers' on-line service and 10 other publications. The price was not announced yesterday.

title:
Updates/Media and Technology;
Targeted Advertising On Times Web Site
body: The newyork Times Electronic Media Company will announce today that it is introducing a new marketing technology to its World Wide Web site aimed at helping on-line advertisers reach specific audiences. The newyork Times on the Web (http://www.nytimes.com) will use an electronic data base system that will enable the Web site to display different ads to different on-line users, based on a user's demographic profile. The newyork Times on the Web gathers this information when people register to use the Web site. The demographic information includes age, gender, income and zip code, which the data base will tie to identifiable email addresses. Using these data, the company said, the Web site will be able to match advertisers with prospective customers. The company said it had 1.7 million registered users of its Web site.   ANDREW ROSS SORKIN

title: America Online in Deals With 2 Retailers
body: America Online Inc. said yesterday that it had agreed to give prominent placement on line to Amazon.com and 1-800-Flowers Inc. in exchange for a share of sales from the retailers worth at least $44 million. The agreements are meant to help the retailers make their on-line sites more readily available to consumers and expand a new source of revenue for America Online, the nation's largest on-line service. Under the agreement with 1-800-Flowers, the florist will remain the exclusive seller of floral and plant products on America Online. The florist expects to generate $250 million in sales from its new placement on America Online sites. The service said it would receive $25 million plus a share of revenue. America Online and Amazon.com agreed to a three-year deal under which Amazon.com will be the exclusive bookseller on America Online's home page and its Netfind search engine. America Online will receive $19 million over the three years, with additional payments if Amazon.com sales exceed certain levels. Shares of America Online rose $2.25, to $65.5625. Amazon.com jumped $3.625, to $27.625.

title:
Internet Promotes an Informed Drug Debate;
A Call for Censorship?
body: To the Editor: Re "A Seductive Drug Culture Flourishes on the Internet" (front page, June 20): Equating pornography with ideas that are unpopular with the Government and segments of society, and claiming that the Internet lacks a "quality control mechanism to separate facts from hyperbole," is an advocacy of censorship. Surely The newyork Times would reject any Government attempt to ban or limit the age of readership for printed news articles discussing the feasibility of legalizing marijuana. So what makes censoring the Internet any different?  J. D.  BRIGHTON Berkeley, Calif., June 23, 1997

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE AND CUC SHOPPING SERVICE FORM VENTURE - Correction Appended
body: America Online Inc. and the discount-shopping service CUC International Inc. are joining forces. Under a three-year agreement, America Online, the Internet access provider, will receive $50 million in fees plus potential other payments from a revenue-sharing arrangement. CUC is expected to generate more than a million annual memberships for America Online, which is based in Dulles, Va. America Online will promote CUC services on line and by direct mail to America Online subscribers. CUC, based in Stamford, Conn., is best known for restaurant coupon books often sold by churches and other nonprofit groups. Much of its $1 billion-plus annual revenue derives from fees it charges its millions of customers, typically $49 a year. Correction  A brief report by Dow Jones in some editions of the Company News column of Business Day yesterday about an alliance between America Online Inc. and CUC International Inc. understated CUC's annual revenue and misidentified the company whose membership is expected to surge because of the alliance. CUC's revenue exceeded $2 billion in its most recent fiscal year; it was not merely $1 billion-plus. In addition, it is CUC, not America Online, that expects to gain a million annual memberships. Correction-Date: June 12, 1997, Thursday

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
DONALDSON, LUFKIN MAKES CHANGES IN ON-LINE SERVICE
body: In an attempt to bolster its nine-year-old on-line unit, Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Inc. said yesterday that it would offer some of its on-line brokerage customers access to the firm's initial public offerings. The firm said its on-line broker, PC Financial Network (www.pcfn.com), would be renamed DLJ Direct, and that beginning June 20 the unit would reduce commission rates to a flat fee of $20 for each trade. Donaldson, Lufkin also said it would offer a portion of the firm's research on line to investors "who maintain an appropriate level of assets" in their on-line accounts.

title: Sony Increases Ad Agency Stake
body: The Sony Corporation said yesterday that it had gained control of a midsized Japanese advertising agency in a bid to tap into the rapidly growing market for ads on the Internet and satellite television. The company's president, Nobuyuki Idei, said Sony had increased its stake in Tokyu Agency International Inc. to 94 percent from 12.5 percent. He declined to say how much it paid for the shares, which it bought on May 1. Tokyu Agency International had sales of 32.5 billion yen ($273.7 million) last year, making it Japan's 20th-largest advertising firm. About a third of its business came from work with Sony. Sony named new executives to run the company and changed its name to Intervision Inc. The electronics maker and media company will use the agency to develop advertising for cable and digital television, game software, the Internet and more traditional media outlets, Mr. Idei said. The Tokyu Corporation, a Japanese railway system operator, owns the remaining 6 percent of Intervision. Sony bought the shares from Tokyu and D'Arcy, Masius, Benton & Bowles International Inc., the unitedstates ad agency that owned 24 percent of Tokyu Agency International.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Company to Study Internet Advertising
body: Competitive Media Reporting in newyork, a unit of VNU N.V. that tracks advertising spending, has formed a new company that will monitor advertising on the Internet. The new company, called Intermedia Advertising Solutions, will be headed by Joseph C. Philport, 48, as president. He has been an executive vice president at Competitive Media.

title: Reed Deal With Microsoft
body: Reed Elsevier P.L.C. has signed a five-year publishing agreement worth $30 million with the Microsoft Corporation. The deal allows Reed Elsevier to use Microsoft's commercial Internet system applications for future electronic offerings in the scientific, legal, business and travel information markets. Reed Elsevier, a joint British and Dutch publishing company, owns the Lexis-Nexis on-line information service.

title:
Metro Business;
Small-Business Awards
body: The newyork City Partnership and Chamber of Commerce, the civic and business organization, presented its annual small-business awards yesterday to the restaurateur Danny Meyer and two companies, Doubleclick, an Internet advertising network, and Cellularvision USA, a wireless communications company. The owner of Union Square Cafe and Gramercy Tavern, Mr. Meyer was singled out for his success in the restaurant world as well as his work to improve the Union Square neighborhood and for the campaign against hunger. Doubleclick was honored for its growth since its founding last March by Kevin O'Connor. The Manhattan firm, which now has nearly 100 employees, links advertisers and Web sites to match a company's ad with an audience. Cellularvision USA, with 100 employees in Manhattan and Brooklyn, was cited for its initial public offering last year on the Nasdaq exchange. It went public after receiving a Federal license to provide wireless telecommunications, including Internet access, television subscriptions and local telephone service. LISA W. FODERARO

title: Microsoft Sued By Ticketmaster
body: Ticketmaster Group Inc. filed suit in Federal court here today accusing the Microsoft Corporation of "electronic piracy" for providing links to Ticketmaster's Web site from its entertainment guide on the Internet. The suit seeks to stop Microsoft from letting users hook up to the Ticketmaster site from Microsoft's "Seattle Sidewalk" guide. Any Internet user can look up Ticketmaster's listings and, using a personal computer, buy tickets to entertainment events. But users who hook up to the site from Microsoft's guide can make their transactions without receiving information on policies and service information offered by Ticketmaster. The suit takes aim at the common Internet practice of providing free links to other companies' Web sites to enhance the attractiveness of a company's own site. The suit contends that Microsoft should have first signed an agreement with Ticketmaster. But Microsoft said that it had no plans to disconnect the link to Ticketmaster or to other outside services available from its on-line guide.

title: Merger Reports Lift Data-Service Shares
body: Shares of America Online Inc., the nation's largest on-line service provider, and of Compuserve, its biggest rival, rose sharply yesterday amid speculation that America Online was planning to acquire the smaller company. America Online shares rose $3.25, to $45.75. Compuserve stock, which opened the week at $9, rose $1.141 yesterday, to $11. Compuserve shares began their climb on Monday, after a small Wall Street newsletter reported talks of a takeover bid. The Washington Post reported earlier today that America Online was exploring a purchase, citing unnamed industry sources. The two companies declined to comment. Adam Schoenfeld, an on-line analyst at Jupiter Communications in newyork, said such a deal would be unlikely, noting that America Online is already struggling to manage its recent explosive growth.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Spending Rises For On-Line Ads
body: Spending for on-line advertising grew steadily throughout 1996, according to the first survey on the subject by the Internet Advertising Bureau in newyork. The bureau's new Advertising Revenue Reporting Program found that on-line ad spending totaled $267 million in 1996. That was similar to a recent survey by Jupiter Communications in newyork, which reported on-line ad spending last year at an estimated $301 million. According to the bureau's survey, on-line ad spending rose from quarter to quarter, reaching $109.5 million in the fourth quarter, up almost 45 percent from $75.6 million in the third quarter. The five largest categories for Internet ad spending, the survey reported, were: computing products, 38 percent of the total; consumer-related products, 20 percent; new media, 17 percent; telecommunications, 9 percent, and business services, 6 percent.

title: COMPANY BRIEFS
body: FIRST ENTERTAINMENT INC., Denver, a multimedia entertainment company, signed a letter of intent to acquire Online Casinos Inc. for $26 million, including debt. The company said it would offer gambling over the Internet within 60 days.  NATIONAL COMPUTER SYSTEMS INC., Minneapolis, agreed to buy Virtual University Enterprises, Bloomington, Minn., for 582,000 shares of common stock, or about $13.5 million. REDDI BRAKE SUPPLY CORP., Ventura, Calif., said it suspended operations at its 84 auto-part distribution shops after creditors filed to force its operating subsidiary into bankruptcy proceedings.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
On-Line Ads Grew In '96, Survey Says
body: On-line advertising in the unitedstates, as expected, grew substantially last year, according to an annual survey by Jupiter Communications, a newyork company specializing in on-line research. Ads on line totaled an estimated $301 million in 1996, Jupiter reported, up 447.3 percent from $55 million in 1995. The Netscape Communications Corporation led Web publishers in ad revenue last year with $27.7 million, Jupiter reported, followed by Yahoo Inc. with $20.6 million and the Infoseek Corporation with $18.1 million. Among advertisers, according to Jupiter, the Microsoft Corporation led in spending with $13 million, followed by the AT&T Corporation with $7.3 million.

title: Web Ads Require Children's Critical Response
body: To the Editor: Parents should not be surprised that alcohol and tobacco companies are using the World Wide Web to pitch products to young people ("On Web, New Threats Seen to the Young," front page, March 7). For simple demographic reasons, these industries want to replace older consumers, and the young are the easiest replacements to acquire as well as the most profitable. But we need not simply submit to this trend or to the cartoonish Web pages used to lure children. Government censorship is controversial and problematic, and industry self-censorship would be slow in coming and weakened by conflicts of interest. But there is another response: education. Parents and educators have begun to teach children to be savvy about movies, television and print advertising. Children should now be taught about the Internet and given the tools to discern the informative, or simply entertaining, from the hip pitches that disguise something potentially harmful.  MEG MILNE MOULTON WHITNEY RANSOME Concord, Mass., March 10, 1997  The writers are directors of the National Coalition of Girls' Schools.

title: Former TV Executive To America Online
body: America Online Inc. yesterday hired Brandon Tartikoff, the one-time head of the NBC television network's entertainment division, to bolster its development of on-line programs focusing on television, movies and other diversions. America Online also bought Lightspeed Media, a creator of on-line programs. The America Online division, called Greenhouse Networks Entertainment, will produce programs that blend movie reviews, entertainment recommendations, celebrity gossip, on-line chat and other fare. As part of its sharper focus, the company also licensed software from Firefly Network Inc. that customizes on-line information for viewers. Mr. Tartikoff will continue to head H. Beale Company, a television and production company with more than two dozen television and feature films in development. He was president of NBC Entertainment from 1980 to 1991, when the network made its rise to No. 1 in the prime-time ratings.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE PUTTING ADS IN CHAT GROUPS
body: America Online Inc. said yesterday that it planned to place advertising on company-sponsored discussion areas, or chat groups, to expand its revenue base beyond mainly subscriber fees. The company, based in Dulles, Va., said placing ads in the company-sponsored chat rooms would generate 360 million ad "impressions" each month. One analyst estimated the effort could generate $15 million to $25 million in new revenues this year. Impressions, or how many times an ad is viewed, are the advertising industry's standard way of measuring the impact of individual ad promotions. America Online stock rose $3, to $43 a share. That rise followed a gain of $2.50 on Monday.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
E*Trade Group To a WPP Unit
body: E*Trade Group Inc., an on-line investing company in Palo Alto, Calif., has named the San Francisco office of the J. Walter Thompson Company to handle the creative portion of its account, which had been handled in-house and fielded out on a project basis. Billings were estimated at $10 million. Thompson San Francisco, a unit of WPP Group, was awarded the creative assignment after a review that also included Gotham in newyork, part of the Interpublic Group of Companies, and three agencies in San Francisco: Black Rocket, Blazing Paradigm and Goldberg Moser O'Neill. Thompson San Francisco had earlier been named to handle on-line media planning and buying for E*Trade.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Times Co. in On-Line Pact
body: The newyork Times Company announced an agreement with America Online Inc. yesterday to expand the on-line provider's exclusive use of news and features from The newyork Times, including original material developed by The Times. The new features, which will be available to the eight million subscribers of America Online, will include an expanded version of Science Times, a new People electronic page, crossword puzzle chat rooms and a monthly "theme" crossword puzzle that will appear only on the electronic service. Officials of both companies said that the measures were intended to satisfy the growing demand for exclusive content and services as the on-line market expands. Apart from the exclusive elements, The Times's news report is also available from its own site on the World Wide Web, at http://www.nytimes.com.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
