Omnicom Takes Stake In Interactive Agency
body: Omnicom Group in newyork has acquired what was described as a significant minority interest in Organic Online, an agency in San Francisco that creates interactive advertising for marketers like the Colgate-Palmolive Company, Levi Strauss & Company and the McDonald's Corporation. Terms were not disclosed. The Omnicom stake in Organic Online will be managed through Communicade, a division devoted to interactive marketing and media that was formed in September. Communicade also manages Omnicom's interests in five other interactive agencies like Agency.com in newyork and Red Sky Interactive in San Francisco.

title: America Online Cutting Off Inactive Users
body: In an attempt to clear up network delays, America Online Inc. has begun monitoring individual subscribers and disconnecting those who do not appear to be using the service. America Online began sending on-line messages to subscribers every 45 minutes asking whether they want to remain logged on. If customers reply no, or do not answer within 10 minutes, the connection is cut. The move comes as America Online grapples with increased use after it introduced a flat monthly fee of $19.95 on Dec. 1. The pricing plan led to delays and busy signals, with many customers failing to get onto the service at all. To avoid such problems, some customers never log off once they log on. The company, based here, said it had begun sending subscribers the messages and disconnecting them in the last two weeks. Previously, subscribers would be asked to log off if they were not using the service. The access problems have prompted class action lawsuits and led to a settlement last week between America Online and 36 states. The on-line service agreed to refund as much as $39.90 per customer.

title: America Online Begins Refunds
body: Faced with frustrated customers who have trouble signing on to its service, America Online said yesterday that it was selectively offering refunds to customers who complain they cannot get the service they paid for. The move comes as America Online Inc. faces a rash of criticism from customers and consumer-protection officials who say the on-line computer service oversold a product that it could not deliver. Wendy Goldberg, a spokeswoman at America Online, said the company was offering refunds to customers case by case. The refunds may take the form of free on-line service, such as extra months, instead of cash, she said. Several states have threatened to sue America Online unless the company provides refunds. America Online has also been named in at least eight lawsuits brought by individual customers who say the pricing plan amounts to breach of contract. The problems stem from the company's decision in December to start charging subscribers $19.95 a month for unlimited on-line time. The rush of new users far outpaced the company's ability to add new equipment to handle it.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MORE TECHNICAL PROBLEMS FOR AMERICA ONLINE
body: America Online, the nation's largest on-line service, was hit with a new technical glitch yesterday as a power outage prevented customers from receiving email for two hours in the morning. The trouble was touched off by computer work that was intended to increase the system's capacity to handle a surge in on-line use. The problem heightened frustrations among users of America Online, which last week experienced two episodes of technical glitches. The trouble came as the company struggles to accommodate a flood of users who are taking advantage of a new pricing policy that allows unlimited use.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
NORTHERN TELECOM SELLS 25% OF INTERNET COMPANY
body: Northern Telecom Ltd. said yesterday that it had sold 25 percent of its newly formed Internet security company, Entrust Technologies Inc., to a group of institutional investors for $26 million. The investors include Olympus Partners, J. P. Morgan & Company, Societe Generale S.A., T. Rowe Price Associates and Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Inc. Northern Telecom, a phone equipment maker based in Mississauga, Ontario, said it was selling the stake to let Entrust have more freedom in choosing partners other than Northern Telecom and in selling its technology. Entrust provides software used to scramble and identify information on the Internet.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Trade Groups Propose Web Banner Guidelines
body: Two trade organizations that represent buyers, sellers and producers of Internet advertising issued the first voluntary guidelines yesterday for creating banner ads on the World Wide Web. The Coalition for Advertising Supported Information and Entertainment and the Internet Advertising Bureau said they hoped the recommendations would help simplify the creation and placement of the ads. There are now more than 250 sizes of banners, the small sign-like ads that appear on World Wide Web sites. To reduce that proliferation, the guidelines propose eight "voluntary model banner sizes." Newspapers and other traditional media have standardized their ad space units in much the same manner. The coalition, known as Casie, is a joint effort of the American Association of Advertising Agencies and the Association of National Advertisers. The ad bureau, formed this year, has more than 125 members.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE SWITCHES ON FEE FOR ITS FLAT-RATE PLAN - Correction Appended
body: America Online Inc. said yesterday that it had agreed to obtain customers' consent before switching them to its new flat-rate plan. The agreement resulted from negotiations with 19 states and will be adopted nationwide. The Internet service provider will also give retroactive refunds to all customers who ask to switch back to their old plan before April 10. America Online, which is based in Dulles, Va., received a complaint letter from 17 state attorneys general on Nov. 18 after it said it would automatically move subscribers on Dec. 1 to its new flat fee of $19.95 a month. The switch would occur unless customers chose another pricing option. Correction  A brief report by Bloomberg Business News in Business Day yesterday about an agreement between America Online Inc. and 19 states over its pricing plan referred imprecisely to customers' options under the agreement. America Online will move all customers to its flat-rate plan except those who choose another plan; the company does not need to obtain their consent before putting them in the flat-rate plan. Correction-Date: December 7, 1996, Saturday

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AXEL SPRINGER TO BUY STAKE IN AMERICA ONLINE UNIT
body: America Online Inc. said yesterday that the German newspaper publisher Axel Springer Verlag A.G. will acquire a 10 percent stake in AOL Germany for an undisclosed amount. AOL Germany is a unit of AOL Europe, a partnership between America Online and the German media company Bertelsmann A.G. In exchange for the stock, AOL Europe will gain access to some of the 40 newspapers and magazines that Springer publishes. Springer will also provide content and market support for the Internet service. America Online, based in Dulles, Va., said AOL Europe had more than 300,000 subscribers and would expand soon to Austria, Switzerland and Sweden. Shares of America Online rose $2.625, or 7 percent, to $40.125.

title: America Online Revises Price-Change Plan
body: America Online users nationwide will receive more time and information to consider a new pricing plan as a result of an agreement with the Attorney General of Washington. The agreement, announced on Friday, came after talks over America Online's plan to automatically switch subscribers to a $19.95 flat rate on Dec. 1 unless they advised the company they wanted to keep the current basic plan -- $9.95 a month for five hours and $2.95 an hour thereafter. The state Attorney General, Christine Gregoire, contended that the plan violated the state's consumer protection law. Under the agreement, the company will notify subscribers with an electronic message when they log on to the service. Customers who are automatically switched to the new plan on Dec. 1 can change back to the original through March 31 and get a refund for the difference. The new choices are: a standard $19.95 monthly plan offering unlimited use of America Online and the Internet; a $9.95 rate for unlimited access to America Online, for those who already have an Internet connection; and three hours of the service a month for $4.95, with additional time at $2.50 an hour.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE TO SHRINK, THEN EXPAND WORK FORCE
body: America Online Inc. plans to lay off 300 of its 5,900 employees as part of the plan to split itself into three divisions, the company said yesterday. America Online, based in Dulles, Va., said the cost of the layoffs would be included in a previously announced charge of $75 million for the current quarter. A spokeswoman for the company, the world's largest on-line service provider, said that after the cuts, "we are going to add another 1,000 to 1,500 between now and June." Many of the new hires will be in technology and in advertising sales, to help expand revenues beyond subscriber fees. Shares of A.O.L. rose $1 a share, to $25.75, on the newyork Stock Exchange.

title: Student Suspended Over email Threat
body: A prank death threat by email to President Clinton earned a high school student a visit from the Secret Service and a monthlong suspension. The message, sent on Oct. 9 over the Internet, read: "To Pres. Clinton: You are Dead," school officials said. They said the threat was sent by a 17-year-old senior at Trinity Catholic High School, one of scores of schools across Connecticut benefiting from a volunteer effort to link classrooms to the Internet. School officials said they assumed the message was sent to the White House. The Secret Service, whose agents spoke to the student, his parents and school officials, would not comment. No criminal charges were filed, Msgr. Frank C. Wissell, president of diocesan secondary schools, said.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Group to Study On-Line Users
body: NFO Research Inc. in Greenwich, Conn., said yesterday that it had formed a panel of more than 50,000 households to provide data about consumers who use interactive and on-line media and to conduct interactive market research. The panel, named NFO//net.source, is being described as offering a representative sample of households that use the Internet, the World Wide Web and services like America Online, Compuserve and Prodigy. NFO said the panel would be available in January.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Cybersites for News And Entertainment
body: Two companies have disclosed plans for Internet initiatives that are both scheduled to begin Monday. The Mecklermedia Corporation will introduce an Interactive Advertising Report on its Iworld magazine (http://netday.iworld.com/iar). The report will offer news, analysis and data aimed at agencies, advertisers and Web publishers. Tristan Louis, publisher of Iworld in Westport, Conn., said that Mecklermedia was talking to large computer advertisers about becoming sponsors of the report. And American Cybercast in Marina del Rey, Calif., in which companies including the Creative Artists Agency, Grey Advertising and the Intel Corporation hold stakes, will start a World Wide Web network (http://www.amcy.com) that combines two episodic series with their own Web sites, the Spot and Eon-4, with two new offerings, the Pyramid and Quick Fix Theater. Advertisers like Apple Computer Inc. that have sponsored the two series will continue; new sponsors will include Intel, the Toyota Motor Corporation and the Visa USA unit of Visa International.

title: Europe Online Returns as a Nonprofit
body: The former on-line information service Europe Online S.A., which shut down in August after going bankrupt, returned this week as a nonprofit organization promoting Europe on the Internet. "Europe Online is now a navigation service, a European gateway to the Internet," Candace Johnson, president of the company's board, said. The association, to be called Europe Online Asbl, is sponsored by Luxembourg P&T, the state telecommunications company, and was founded by former Europe Online S.A. employees. Europe Online Asbl said it was providing consumers with a user-friendly interface, easy navigation and information retrieval service for the Internet in various languages. It does not provide Internet access itself, but acts as a framework for information and content providers in Europe to put their content on the World Wide Web part of the Internet. Ms. Johnson said a number of Internet service providers had shown interest in incorporating Europe Online in their services. Membership dues and sponsors will finance the association's activities. The old Luxembourg-based company shut down in August after last-ditch talks with Deutsche Telekom and others failed to keep the operation running.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
On-Line Advertising Standards Proposed
body: The interactive-media coalition formed by the trade associations for agencies and advertisers has proposed standardizing advertisements for on-line media. The Coalition for Advertising Supported Information and Entertainment, known as Casie, said yesterday that its guidelines for standardization of the sizes and layouts of ad banners and so-called ad buttons would help reduce production costs, speed the creation of on-line ads and make ad-rate comparisons easier. Publishers that carry large amounts of advertising on the World Wide Web will be surveyed for opinions on the guidelines. Several advertising and interactive agencies have been seeking common standards for on-line ads. Casie was formed in 1994 by the American Association of Advertising Agencies and the Association of National Advertisers.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE SHARES DROP ON EARNINGS FORECAST
body: America Online Inc. shares fell about 10 percent yesterday after the company said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission that on-line and Internet rivals might cut into its earnings and revenue. Competition might force America Online to cut prices or increase marketing expenses, and it could lead to lower subscription growth and revenue, the company said. Shares of America Online fell $3.50, to $32, in trading of 5.4 million shares. The company's shares have lost more than half their value in the last four months because of investor concern about competition from rival services and direct-access providers.

title: America Online Wins Appeal on Mail
body: America Online Inc. won a Federal court appeal today giving it the right to resume blocking electronic junk mail to its subscribers from Cyber Promotions Inc., at least for now. A three-judge panel of the unitedstates Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit vacated a lower court's preliminary injunction against the block to America Online subscribers. In a one-page ruling, the judges wrote that they had not considered the merits of the arguments but that unitedstates District Judge Charles Weiner had erred by not holding a proper fact-finding hearing before issuing the injunction. America Online, based in Dulles, Va., began blocking Internet sites this month that had been sending mass commercial email messages to America Online subscribers. It said junk mail was the leading source of customer complaints. Cyber sends messages on three of the five sites that America Online cut off. Judge Weiner can now hold a hearing to determine whether to reinstate the ban, pending a resolution of Cyber's lawsuit, scheduled for trial on Nov. 12. The suit by Cyber, filed in March, accuses America Online of trying to drive Cyber out of business. Cyber is based in Philadelphia.

title: Junk email Costs Receivers Real Money
body: To the Editor: Your Sept. 5 Business Day article on America Online's blocking of unsolicited commercial messages aimed at users misses the major point that differentiates junk email from conventional forms of advertising: conventional advertising is paid for by the advertiser, while junk email is paid for by the recipient. On an on-line service that charges by the minute, the recipient will pay for the time the computer takes to identify and discard the junk mail. On-line service providers must purchase additional computer and storage resources to maintain their existing level of service while processing 700,000 unsolicited messages a day; this cost is passed on to the customers. Thus, your comparison of junk email with fliers on windshields is flawed. You are more correct in comparing junk email to junk faxes; a recipient of junk faxes pays for the paper used by the unwanted messages.  YORAM EISENSTADTER newyork, Sept. 5, 1996 Graphic   Drawing.

title: AOL May Appeal Ruling
body: America Online Inc. will probably appeal a Federal court order that it stop blocking promotional electronic mail from a Philadelphia firm, a lawyer for the on-line service firm said today. "I think we're probably going to appeal, and probably move to stay" the order, Michael Grow, a lawyer for America Online, said in an interview. On Thursday, Judge Charles Weiner ordered America Online not to block email from Cyber Promotions Inc., which sends mass electronic mailings of promotional material, pending a November trial on a lawsuit Cyber Promotions filed against America Online. America Online, the largest unitedstates on-line service provider, told subscribers on Thursday that it had denied access to mailers from five Internet sites, including three associated with Cyber Promotions.

title: Corrections
body: A report in the Cyberscout column on Aug. 18 about the Internet Travel Network misstated a reservation procedure. The reservations are made by the client through the network, and the client's travel agent issues tickets and processes payments; the travel agent does not make the reservations.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
America Online Sued by N.B.A.
body: The National Basketball Association filed a lawsuit yesterday against America Online Inc. and Stats Inc. for using game scores and data without permission. The N.B.A. wants to block the computer on-line service from using real-time information on its games. Stats Inc. supplies America Online with the scores. The N.B.A. is also seeking unspecified damages. The suit is almost identical to one the N.B.A. won against Motorola Inc. last month. Then, a Federal judge said Motorola could not transmit scores on pagers that simulate action during N.B.A. games because the league owned the scores. Stats Inc. was also named in the Motorola suit. Bob Meyerhoff, a lawyer for Stats Inc. in Skokie, Ill., said the company had no comment.

title: AT&T Internet Offering
body: The AT&T Corporation said today that it would offer access to America Online Inc., the world's most popular consumer on-line service, on its Worldnet service. AT&T said the service would cost 20 percent less than use of the telecommunications giant's standard dial-up access rate. AT&T Worldnet customers will receive 15 hours of free use under America Online's one-month trial offer and can download the registration software by clicking on links from the AT&T Worldnet At Home page, the company said. America Online provides email, on-line communities, chat content and original programming for interactive communities. AT&T Worldnet Service provides value-added access to the Internet, including access to on-line service providers such as America Online.

title: Genie Online Is Acquired
body: The IDT Corporation has bought Genie Online Service, a small Internet company that provides electronic discussions and games, from the Yovelle Renaissance Corporation. Terms were not disclosed. The sale comes seven months after Genie's founder, the General Electric Company, sold the service to Yovelle. Genier was one of the first companies to offer Internet services when it was created in 1985. The service had about 20,000 customers in the unitedstates.

title:
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS;
Operations Cease At Europe Online
body: The bankrupt online service Europe Online S.A. logged off for good today after last-ditch talks with Deutsche Telekom A.G. and others to keep the Luxembourg-based operation running failed. "Europe Online has ceased to operate," Albert Wildgen, one of Europe Online's liquidators, said. "No agreement was reached by a deadline this morning, so we had to close it down." He declined to give further details. With about 25,000 subscribers altogether, multilingual Europe Online had national services in Germany, Britain and Luxembourg, as well as an international service in English, which included news, weather, travel, sports and entertainment. The company suffered a major financial blow in July when its biggest single shareholder, the German publisher Burda Holding, said it would not provide further financing. Other shareholders included the AT&T Corporation. Desperate attempts followed to find new investors or shareholders, including negotiations with the rival U.S. online company Compuserve Inc. and Deutsche Telekom. No deal was reached, and the company was declared bankrupt Aug. 2.

title:
August 4-10;
Red-Faced @America Online
body: America Online, the nation's largest on-line commercial computer network, went abruptly off-line last week, leaving its 6.2 million subscribers stranded in cyberspace for nearly 19 hours. The outage on Wednesday illustrated how much small businesses have come to depend on America Online for electronic mail and other services, without which many were closed for the day. It also pointed up the vulnerability of traditional on-line services to the ever-growing Internet, which never goes down. Engineers eventually traced the shutdown, which began during an early-morning maintenance procedure, to a combination of software bugs and human error.   LAWRENCE M. FISHER

title: Cyberspace Blackout
body: To the Editor: The 19-hour shutdown of America Online (news article, Aug. 8) was inconvenient, costly and annoying to regular users, but it was hardly surprising -- just longer than usual. Those of us who employ America Online regularly are all too familiar with the four most widely used words in its lexicon: "Connection lost: no carrier." Service interruptions are so common as to be an actual part of the service. When they occur, they are customarily accompanied by a screen telling you to check your modem connection and other settings, suggesting that the interruption is your fault. No wonder America Online veterans refer to the supposedly user-friendly service as America On Hold.  GEORGE FASEL newyork, Aug. 8, 1996

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE BUYS AT&T COMPUTER GAME UNIT
body: America Online Inc., the computer on-line service, said yesterday that it had bought Imagination Network Inc., a money-losing computer game unit of the AT&T Corporation. The purchase price was not disclosed. AT&T had paid more than $40 million in November 1994 to acquire the 80 percent of the company that it did not already own. AT&T officials declined to estimate the size of the losses the company incurred during its sole ownership of Imagination. Imagination said it would operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of America Online.

title: Europe Online Bankrupt
body: Europe Online, an Internet information service based in Luxembourg, was declared bankrupt on Friday, "and liquidators have been appointed," the Luxembourg Court of Commerce said today. Europe Online, whose biggest shareholder, the German publisher Burda, said it would not finance it anymore, had been under court protection from creditors since last month while talking with potential new shareholders, including Compuserve, ITT and Deutsche Telekom A.G. A small player in a growing market, multilingual Europe Online had 25,000 subscribers.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE PLANS TO MOVE TO THE BIG BOARD
body: America Online Inc. said yesterday that it would file for a listing on the newyork Stock Exchange and that it expects to begin trading under the symbol AOL in the "near future." The stock now trades on Nasdaq as AMER. "We expect that moving to the newyork Stock Exchange will bring benefits to the company and its shareholders," Steve Case, the company's chief executive, said. After the announcement, first reported yesterday in The Wall Street Journal, America Online shares jumped $2.875 to $33.375.

title: Infusion for Europe Online
body: Deutsche Telekom A.G. is in talks to invest in Europe Online S.A., the troubled on-line information service, both companies said today. Compuserve and the ITT Corporation have already been identified in press reports as potential investors in Europe Online. "These are negotiations about concrete offers -- from among others Deutsche Telekom -- and a final decision is expected this week," said Alexander Fink, a spokesman for Europe Online. Earlier this month, the Luxembourg-based company won court protection from its creditors.

title: Verisign Security System Is Selected by Visa
body: Visa International Inc. said yesterday that it had chosen Verisign Inc. to verify the identity of credit card users when they make purchases using the Internet. The bank credit card association is hoping that Verisign's so-called digital certificates will provide added security for purchases on the Internet, where transactions can be vulnerable to computer hackers. Verisign will operate the service for Visa, which in turn will make it available to Visa member banks. "By offering digital certificates through Verisign, Visa is working to enable its members to move cost effectively into the electronic commerce marketplace," a Visa official, Steve Herz, said.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE EXPECTS TO DOUBLE ITS EARNINGS
body: Trying to avoid being splashed by bad news from its rival Compuserve Inc., America Online said yesterday that it expected to at least double its fourth-quarter earnings -- meeting or exceeding Wall Street analysts' expectations. Compuserve, the No. 2 on-line service after America Online, said on Tuesday that it expected to post an operating loss in its quarter ending July 31. America Online's chairman, Steve Case, said yesterday that his company expected to meet or exceed analysts' predictions of 16 cents a share for its fourth quarter, which ended on June 30; it reports financial results Aug. 8.

title: Corrections
body: The Advertising column in Business Day on July 8 about Newsweek magazine's World Wide Web sites misstated the address of one site, Newsweek International. It is http: //www.newsweek-int.com.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
America Online Forms Alliance for News
body: America Online Inc. said today that it had teamed with the Tribune Company to expand the local news and services it offers to 88 local markets on the Internet. The venture, dubbed Digital City, already operates in Washington, Boston and San Francisco, providing America Online members with information on local news, weather, sports, traffic conditions and local events. Tribune will help America Online begin local information services in Chicago, southern Florida and Hampton Roads, Va., where Tribune currently publishes newspapers. Financial details of the alliance were not disclosed, but The Wall Street Journal reported the venture was expected to require a $100 million investment. Chicago-based Tribune is expected to take a 20 percent stake in Digital Cities, putting up roughly $20 million, The Journal said. The Digital Cities initiative was started last fall by America Online, based in Dulles, Va.

title:
NEW JERSEY DAILY BRIEFING;
Property for Thomas Edison
body: New Jersey's virtual college is expanding into some very real real estate. Officials at Thomas Edison State College will break ground tomorrow on a $12.7 million project to turn a row of five historic town houses into headquarters for the school's electronic classrooms and training and conference centers. Thomas Edison, which calls itself a "distance learning school," has no regular classrooms. Rather, its 3,000 students, located in all 50 states and 65 foreign countries, take courses via computer, video and correspondence. Michael Scheiring, the college's vice president and treasurer, said the corporate-style conference and training rooms would be used by students in the school's new master's program in management when the project is completed in 1997. The state-owned town houses, on West State Street, were once home to the New Jersey Council on the Arts.   ANDY NEWMAN

title: Publisher Burda to Sell Europe Online Stake
body: The German publisher Burda G.m.b.H. said today that it planned to sell its 36 percent stake in Europe Online S.A., an Internet service provider. Burda said it had been pressing Europe Online to change its management structure to streamline decision making. "We feel that it is no longer economically viable to keep putting capital and creativity into a project that is so complicated to navigate," a spokesman for Burda, Philipp Welte, said. He said Burda planned to concentrate on developing its own Internet service for the German market. Officials of Europe Online, who insisted on not being identified, said the company, which is based in Luxembourg, was negotiating with potential investors.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Ad Group Begins New Media Award
body: The Coalition for Advertising Supported Information and Entertainment, a joint venture of the Association of National Advertisers and the American Association of Advertising Agencies focusing on the new media, plans to begin an annual awards competition for effective advertising and marketing on the Internet and the World Wide Web. The Casie Awards will be presented for the best interactive advertising campaign and the best advertiser Web site. The initial awards will be announced during the 1996 annual meeting of the advertiser association, Oct. 4-7 at Amelia Island, Fla.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
America Online Has a New Strategy
body: America Online Inc., seeking additional revenue to supplement subscription fees, said yesterday that it would significantly revamp its advertising strategies. "We asked why Madison Avenue wasn't buying us and our conclusion was we weren't acting like a media company," said Myer Berlow, vice president for interactive advertising. "So we developed procedures that speak to advertisers and agencies." Under the program, America Online will guarantee audiences and set ad rates based on the cost-per-thousand model used for media like magazines, measuring actual page views rather than estimating exposure. America Online has six million subscribers; analysts have forecast that growth in the second quarter will be less than half that of the first quarter, when 800,000 subscribers were signed. About 10 percent of the $1 billion in revenue anticipated this year will come from advertising, on-line transaction fees and merchandising, said Ted Leonsis, president of the AOL Services Company, who declined to offer estimates for 1997. Current advertisers include American Express, Nynex and Reebok.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Softbank Awarded Interactive Work
body: Two companies have named Softbank Interactive Marketing in newyork to handle interactive advertising accounts. NBC Interactive Media, which oversees the on-line activities of the NBC unit of the General Electric Company, named Softbank to sell advertising and sponsorships on its Olympic World Wide Web site (http://www.olympic.nbc.com). And the Netscape Communications Corporation in Mountain View, Calif., which provides software for the Internet, selected the media sales division of Softbank Interactive to handle sales for technology, business-to-business and financial services accounts on Netscape's Web site. Softbank Interactive is a joint venture of the Softbank Corporation, Interactive Marketing Inc. and Network 1.0.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE TO SELL ADVERTISING FOR NETSCAPE SITE
body: America Online Inc. said yesterday that it and the Netscape Communications Corporation were forming an unusual arrangement in which America Online sales representatives would also sell advertising space on Netscape's World Wide Web site. Netscape has one of the most popular sites on the Web, allowing visitors to download its Navigator software, which helps users browse the Web. Analysts said they expected the deal to bring in more revenues for America Online.

title:
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS;
America Online Gains on Report
body: The shares of America Online Inc. climbed yesterday, assisted by a report that it planned to team up with a Japanese company to offer Internet access service in Japan by the end of the year. The Kyodo news agency in Japan reported over the weekend that America Online would form a joint venture with Mitsui & Company to offer Japanese-language Internet services. An America Online spokeswoman declined to comment. Shares of America Online rose $5.25, to $67.875, in Nasdaq trading of more than three million shares. The company expects to have more than a million subscriptions in Japan in the next two years, Kyodo reported. The Japanese on-line companies, the Nifty Corporation, a joint venture of Fujitsu Ltd. and the Nissho Iwai Corporation, and PC-Van, a unit of the NEC Corporation, each have about 1.5 million subscribers, it said. Kyodo quoted industry sources as saying that America Online planned to expand into India and Australia.

title: Lexis-Nexis to Carry Bloomberg Services
body: Lexis-Nexis, one of the world's largest providers of on-line information, and Bloomberg L.P. are expected to announce today an alliance that will provide Bloomberg's business news and daily market summaries to more than 750,000 Lexis-Nexis subscribers, beginning in the second half of this year. Bloomberg's news and analysis services are currently sent electronically to more than 55,000 specialized computer terminals used by brokerages, newspapers and other business news consumers. Under terms of the deal to be announced today, the same Bloomberg information, delayed 12 hours, will be made available to Lexis-Nexis subscribers for a fee that has not yet been determined. The addition of Bloomberg news services is the latest in a string of alliances for Lexis-Nexis, whose customers are primarily in legal, business or government offices. In the past year, Lexis-Nexis, a Dayton, Ohio-based division of Reed Elsevier P.L.C., has also agreed to carry information provided electronically by the Dun & Bradstreet Corporation and CNN, a unit of the Turner Broadcasting System. The financial terms of today's agreement have not been disclosed.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
COMPAQ IN CLOSER TIE WITH INTERNET SECURITY CONCERN
body: The Compaq Computer Corporation will incorporate network security software by Raptor Systems Inc. into its computers, the companies said yesterday. In Nasdaq trading yesterday, shares of Raptor rose $3.375, to $32.625. Financial terms of the arrangement, which builds on an existing relationship, were not disclosed. But Raptor stands to grow rapidly if Compaq deploys its software broadly. Raptor lost $2.6 million on $3.9 million in sales last year. Compaq intends to use Raptor's EagleNT software in machines that companies want to work with both internal corporate networks and the Internet.

title: $12 Million Award in Software Dispute
body: Computer Associates International Inc. said yesterday that a newyork State judge had ordered it to pay $12 million in a royalty dispute case tied to a 1991 acquisition. A spokesman for Computer Associates said the company would appeal the recent decision, which was based on an arbitration award entered last year. The case grew out of Computer Associates' $100 million acquisition of privately held Online Software International Inc. of Fort Lee, N.J., in 1991. One of Online Software's products was Datavantage, a software that simplifies testing and system assurance on mainframe computers. The plaintiffs in the lawsuit were the developers of the software, which Computer Associates provided to other companies. They said yesterday that a newyork arbitration panel had found that Computer Associates had "fraudulently concealed" certain transactions to avoid paying them royalties, violating the Federal Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act. The developers said the ruling required Computer Associates to return Datavantage to them and turn over records related to the product.

title: Softbank Enters Marketing Deal
body: The Softbank Corporation, the world's largest computer magazine publisher, agreed today to buy an equity stake in Interactive Marketing Inc., an on-line marketing and communications company. An executive at Interactive Marketing said Softbank Holdings Inc., the unitedstates unit of the Japanese software maker, would own half of the company. Spokesmen for both companies declined to comment on the terms. Interactive Marketing, based in Hermosa Beach, Calif., produces trade shows and publications about advertising and marketing on the Internet. It also sells media space on the World Wide Web, the graphics-rich portion of the global computer network. The on-line marketing company was founded in 1990 and generated $4.4 million in sales last year. Softbank, based in Tokyo, became the largest publisher of computer magazines in February when it completed the purchase of the Ziff-Davis Publishing Company from Forstmann Little & Company for $2.1 billion.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
Newsweek Adds Election Campaign
body: Newsweek magazine said yesterday that it had expanded its relationship with Mezzina/Brown Inc. in newyork by awarding the agency an assignment to create a print, direct mail and interactive advertising and promotional campaign focusing on Newsweek's coverage of the 1996 Presidential election. Spending on the campaign, which carries the theme "Now you know," was not disclosed. Mezzina/Brown has worked with Newsweek, which is owned by the Washington Post Company, since last year as the agency for Newsweek Interactive, the magazine's on-line service. The Newsweek agency of record, Jerry & Ketchum in newyork, which is a venture of Jerry Della Femina and Ketchum Communications, will continue to create general advertising carrying the theme "It's time for Newsweek." Diana Pearson, a spokeswoman for Newsweek in newyork, said that Mezzina/Brown was selected for the assignment after a three-month review that also included four undisclosed agencies.

title: Thomson Deal Is Under Antitrust Review
body: The Justice Department's antitrust division has opened an investigation into the Thomson Corporation's $3.43 billion acquisition of the West Publishing Company, whose on-line legal research business is similar to that of one of Thomson's big divisions. Gina Talamona, spokeswoman for the antitrust division, confirmed that the investigation had begun. Thomson hopes to complete the deal by early next month. The purchase would double Thomson's $800 million annual sales in on-line legal research materials. Thomson officials maintain that the two companies operate at different ends of the business, with West strongest in law data files, while Thomson's legal publishing division deals in secondary legal references and background documents. Thomson officials said they were not worried about the development.

title: Company Briefs
body: HEWLETT-PACKARD CO., Palo Alto, Calif., agreed to buy the Internet security business of the privately held Secureware Inc., Atlanta, for undisclosed terms.  OLSTEN CORP., Melville, L.I., said it had acquired Top Notch Temporary Services Inc. and Multiforce Temporary Services Inc., employment service companies based in Puerto Rico, for $11 million.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
ORACLE AND VERIFONE TO PURSUE ON-LINE PAYMENT SYSTEM
body: The Oracle Corporation, the giant data base software developer, and Verifone Inc., the largest developer of credit-card verification systems, will announce an alliance today to create a secure payment system for consumers and businesses on the Internet. The system will combine Oracle's Webserver software with Verifone's secure payment software to give merchants, banks and other financial providers an on-line payment system. The companies will also incorporate the Verifone Pay Window software into Oracle's Power Browser, its free browser for surfing the Internet's World Wide Web. Verifone's Pay Window software will provide transaction options and make the Power Browser easier to use.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
MICROSOFT PURCHASE INVESTIGATED BY U.S.
body: The Microsoft Corporation's acquisition of a fledgling World Wide Web software company, Vermeer Technologies Inc., is being investigated by Federal antitrust regulators, the Justice Department said yesterday. The investigators are looking at whether the purchase will hurt competition on the Internet's World Wide Web. It is unusual because it involves such a small company in the emerging and competitive market for Web software, antitrust lawyers said. Since last year, Federal officials have been examining the company's entry into the market for on-line information services. The Justice Department investigation of the Vermeer acquisition was first reported yesterday by The Wall Street Journal.

title:
Jan. 28 - Feb. 3;
Attention, Cyber-Shoppers!
body: Would-be cyber-shoppers who have been squeamish about transmitting their credit card numbers onto the Internet, can feel a bit more secure now that Mastercard International and Visa International have announced a standard of protection called Secure Electronic Transactions, or SET. Last year Microsoft and Visa sparred with Mastercard and upstart Netscape Communications Corporation, each with its own standard, each arguing that the other was trying to lock up shoppers. But cooler heads prevailed. It will be possible later this year to transmit a scrambled card number, secure from thieves and other interlopers, and purchase goods and services from software to groceries.   JOHN MARKOFF

title: America Online Expands Service
body: America Online Inc., the leading unitedstates on-line service, has started AOL Canada, extending its international reach. The new service from America Online, which is based in Vienna, Va., plans to feature Canadian content and also provide email and access to the Internet, the company said. Key partners in the new service include Citytv, a Toronto-based television producer; MuchMusic, Canada's first national music television channel, and Shift magazine. Intuit Inc., which makes the popular Quicken financial-management software, will provide access to new kinds of financial information, America Online said. Canadian subscribers will have access to the content offered on America Online's German, British, and unitedstates services. All America Online subscribers will have access to the full Canadian service, the company said. Separately, AOL named William Razzouk as its president and chief operating officer. Mr. Razzouk was formerly chief operating officer at the Federal Express Corporation and fills a newly created position at America Online.

title: WHO NEEDS AMERICA ONLINE?
body: Does Ted Leonsis truly believe that "when you go to a cocktail party and America Online diskettes are being used as coasters, you know you've become mainstream"? I get about four mailings a year, with one or two diskettes, from America Online, likewise from Compuserve and Prodigy. Sometimes the diskettes are inserted into magazines. I don't even know which recycling bin to use to discard this item of junk mail. It seems to me that the party givers are being more innovative than just going "mainstream." Leonsis should take a lesson.  HERBERT WEISS Middleville, N.J.

title: Times On-Line Pact
body: The newyork Times and America Online Inc. said yesterday that they had agreed to extend their relationship for one year. Under the new agreement, the interactive and multimedia features on @times, the newyork Times service that is offered on America Online, will be expanded. In addition, Martin Nisenholtz, president of The newyork Times Electronic Media Company, said, the companies plan to explore a range of new services, either on the Internet's World Wide Web or on America Online, that would include advertising. The @times service, which has been available to America Online subscribers since June 1994, was recently revamped, adding a reproduction of The Times's front page and a classified advertising section, among other features.

title:
INTERNATIONAL BRIEFS;
On-Line Joint Venture Draws European Inquiry
body: The European Commission opened an inquiry yesterday into whether the plans of a joint venture by America Online Inc., the German media company Bertelsmann A.G. and Deutsche Telekom to create an on-line service would be anti-competitive. In a statement, the commission said it was concerned about possible anti-competitive situations that could slow the development of other on-line services.   (AP)

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
VIRGIN ATLANTIC FINED FOR VIOLATIONS IN ADS ON INTERNET
body: Virgin Atlantic Airways was hit yesterday with the first civil penalty imposed by the Department of Transportation on an airline for violations in advertisements on the Internet. Virgin Atlantic, the British carrier, has agreed to pay a $14,000 fine for failing to disclose the full prices of flights advertised on the Internet's World Wide Web and for listing a fare that was not available.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
TIME MAGAZINE WILL SWITCH TO COMPUSERVE
body: Compuserve Inc. said today that Time magazine had signed an exclusive agreement to leave America Online Inc. and join Compuserve, the No. 2 on-line service behind America Online. Time said it would create a news service on Compuserve early next year. The service will be continually updated during the day with breaking news and will include photos and graphics. Terms of the agreement were not available. The agreement is a coup for Compuserve, a unit of H & R Block Inc. that has 3.6 million customers. The switch marks the second time in six months that America Online has lost a news source to a rival on-line service. NBC left America Online earlier this year for the Microsoft Corporation's new on-line service.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Europe Online to Start
body: Europe Online S.A. said today that it would begin its service on Dec. 15 despite being hurt by the defection of major publishing partners. The Luxembourg-based company had originally planned an early 1996 starting date. Its only major publishing partner appears to be Burda Verlag G.m.b.H. of Germany, the publisher of Focus and Bunte magazines. Europe Online will begin offering its service in Germany and Britain and extend to other European countries next year, a spokeswoman said.

title: America Online to Split Its Stock, Again
body: Shares of America Online Inc. rose 8.9 percent yesterday after the company said it planned to split its stock 2-for-1. The split is the third in 12 months for American Online. Over the last year, the company's shares have more than quadrupled in value after being adjusted for the stock splits. Since the last 2-for-1 split in April, its share price has almost doubled. Another 2-for-1 split took place last November. "It is easier for America Online to appeal to individual investors, like its subscribers, if the stock is at $40, instead of $80," said Paul Sweeney, an analyst with Wheat First Butcher Singer. Its stock closed yesterday at $86.25, up $6.25, in Nasdaq trading. In November 1994 the stock traded as low as $15.25. Shareholders of record on Nov. 14 will receive two shares for each one held. The shares will be distributed on Nov. 28. The company said that after the split it will have about 80 million shares outstanding. The company, based in Vienna, Va., also said yesterday that its chief executive, Steve Case, was named to the added post of chairman of the board. He replaces Jim Kimsey, who will continue as a director and chairman emeritus.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE UNVEILS ITS INTERNET NAVIGATOR
body: America Online Inc. unveiled its Internet service, Global Network Navigator, yesterday. In August, America Online delayed the relaunch of the service because of the release of the Microsoft Corporation's Windows 95. In a statement America Online said the service is aimed at the segment of on-line consumers who seek full-feature, Internet-only access and the growing number of publishers interested in enhancing their presence on the Web. America Online said pricing for Global Network Navigator provides consumers with free unlimited use for the first month. Then, a monthly fee of $14.95 covers 20 hours of use. Each additional hour costs $1.95. America Online's stock rose $5.125 yesterday, to $79.375, in Nasdaq trading.

title: America Online Looks at Yahoo
body: America Online Inc., the nation's largest on-line service provider, is in talks to acquire Yahoo, the maker of one of the most popular Internet directories, The San Francisco Chronicle reported today. An America Online executive confirmed the negotiations, but a spokeswoman said no deal was imminent, the paper said. An acquisition of Yahoo, a start-up company based in Mountain View, Calif., would augment America Online's established directories, which allow users to search the graphical portion of the World Wide Web by using key words, subjects or phrases. Yahoo, which was created by two Stanford University students, Jerry Yang and David Filo, is in the process of starting to sell advertising space on Yahoo Web pages as a way of generating revenue.

title: Glitch at America Online
body: A software glitch in a new program forced the computer service America Online to shut down for about three and a half hours on Friday night as the company fixed the problem, officials said today. The system software manages the process of signing personal computers on and off the system.

title: America Online Offering
body: America Online Inc. said today that the company and some of its shareholders were planning a public offering of 3.5 million of its common shares. The company said it had filed a plan with the Securities and Exchange Commission in which it would offer to sell 1.95 million shares and certain shareholders would offer 1.55 million shares. The computer on-line services company said it would use its portion of the proceeds to generate new subscribers, for marketing programs and to expand its network.

title: House Takes Its Turn on Internet Censorship
body: To the Editor: Draconian censorship of the Internet is imminent, and nobody knows about it. A counterpart to Senator Jim Exon's infamous Communications Decency Act lurked in what is called a "managers' amendment" to the House version of the telecommunications bill. Accordingly, new Internet speech crimes, related, as usual, to expression about sex, could bring up to five years in prison. Managers' amendments are presumed to be for housekeeping matters, and when the House voted, apparently some members were unaware of this one's contents. You fail to report that these restrictions passed as part of this bill. House Speaker Newt Gingrich got much recognition for saying, several weeks before the vote, that he thought such legislation was "a violation of free speech and a violation of the right of adults to communicate with each other." But does anyone suppose this got by without approval? Who, after all, is the real manager of the House? The press needs to alert us about this, especially since the telecommunications bill will soon be considered by a House-Senate conference committee.  LEANNE KATZ Executive Director, National Coalition Against Censorship newyork, Sept. 7, 1995

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
INTERNET PROFILES SELECTED TO AUDIT WEB USE
body: Hoping to become the Nielsen rating service of the Internet, the Internet Profiles Corporation of San Francisco has been selected by Playboy Enterprises, the Netscape Communications Corporation, Ziff-Davis Publishing, a unit of Forstmann Little & Company, and several other media companies to provide independent auditing of World Wide Web users. The companies will use data compiled by Internet Profiles' I/Audit program to determine electronic advertising costs, sell advertising space and evaluate the effectiveness of ads on the Web. Several companies have announced plans to provide such services, but Internet Profiles, a privately held company known as I/Pro, is the first to gain a following among big Internet publishers.

title:
CHATTER: Censor the Internet;
Against Censorship
body: What, if anything, should be done to limit sexually explicit material on the Internet? Young or old, you have to look for sex on the Internet. People who want to censor the Internet want to censor any discussion or description of sexual life. That's wrong.  VINCE LEO Minneapolis

title:
CHATTER: Censor the Internet;
Don't Seek, Don't Find
body: What, if anything, should be done to limit sexually explicit material on the Internet? I haven't seen a bit of porn, because I haven't looked for any. At my local drugstore, I can't locate a copy of Time magazine without scanning the displays of lewd ones. At least on the Internet, we have a choice.  JOE ORAWCZYK Yermo, Calif.

title:
CHATTER: Censor the Internet;
How Much Control?
body: What, if anything, should be done to limit sexually explicit material on the Internet? How far do we go in policing the Internet before it becomes a violation of freedom of speech? What is the punishment if one is found guilty of a conduct violation? Fines? On-line banishment?  STEFEN SHADY Palmdale, Calif.

title:
CHATTER: Censor the Internet;
Taking Responsibility
body: What, if anything, should be done to limit sexually explicit material on the Internet? It should be the user's responsibility to determine what should and should not be seen on the computer. And there is software available to block pornographic stuff. Leave the Government out of our communications superhighway! They have too much control already.  LANCE PARKER Baton Rouge, La.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
WASHINGTON POST AND ZIFF-DAVIS PUBLICATIONS ON LINE
body: The Washington Post and Ziff-Davis Publishing introduced electronic versions of their publications yesterday on the Interchange on-line service owned by the AT&T Corporation. The newspaper, owned by the Washington Post Company working with the Digital Ink Company, will feature the contents of its publication, updated news-service copy, and articles about Congressional legislation and Supreme Court rulings. Ziff-Davis, which is owned by Forstmann Little & Company, will provide the contents of its publications, which include PC Magazine, PC Week and MacWeek.

title: America Online's Growth
body: America Online Inc., the on-line services company, said today that it now had more than three million subscribers.  Its subscribers have grown from 300,000 two years ago, the company said. In May, the company had 2.5 million subscribers. Shares of the company, based here, rose $2.25, to $46.50, in Nasdaq trading today.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS: ADVERTISING -- ADDENDA;
America Online Seeks an Agency
body: America Online Inc. said yesterday that it was seeking an agency to help develop a corporate branding campaign, now handled in-house. The billings were not disclosed, but Adweek estimated they could total as much as $30 million. Pam McGraw, a spokeswoman for America Online in Vienna, Va., confirmed a report of the search this week in Adweek, which also reported that the company was close to signing a contract with the newyork office of Chiat/Day. Ms. McGraw said there was no "formal relationship" with Chiat/Day "at this time."

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE TO BUY TWO SMALLER COMPANIES
body: America Online Inc. plans to buy two smaller computer products companies that will expand its publishing and Internet presence, the commercial on-line service said yesterday. The company said it would acquire the multimedia and Internet publishing and production companies Medior Inc. and Wide Area Information Servers Inc. America Online would acquire Medior for about 825,000 shares in stock, or about $31 million. The company would acquire Wide Area Information Servers for about 400,000 shares, or about $15 million. Shares of America Online gained $1 yesterday, to $36.75, in Nasdaq trading.

title: Satan Designer Is Hired by Sun
body: Dan Farmer, a software designer who lost his job at Silicon Graphics Inc. last month because of his work on a controversial computer security program, has been rehired by Sun Microsystems Inc. The Satan data security program, which was co-designed by Mr. Farmer on his own time, was intended to help companies find weaknesses in computer systems linked to the Internet but was criticized as a weapon that could be used by hackers to break into computer networks. Mr. Farmer was dismissed by Silicon Graphics a few days before he began distributing Satan free on the Internet. "When he popped back up and was available, we snapped him right up," said Carolyn Turbyfill, director of engineering for Sun's Internet commerce divisions.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Knight-Ridder Tourism Move
body: Knight-Ridder Inc. has bought 50 percent of an on-line tourism-information service owned by a media rival, the Tribune Company. The service, Destination Florida, was started by the Tribune-owned Orlando Sentinel in June to offer information about Orlando-area attractions, hotels and restaurants. The service, offered through America Online, also allows users to buy event tickets statewide through Ticketmaster Florida. The Sentinel's publisher, John Puerner, said the partnership with Miami-based Knight-Ridder should mean more South Florida offerings on the service. Destination Florida has experienced rapid growth since it began. It received 342,000 computer inquiries in March, said Julie Anderson, the service's general manager.

title: COMPANY BRIEFS
body: AMERICA ONLINE INC., Vienna, Va., an on-line computer service, plans to open a customer service center in Jacksonville, Fla., that will hire 1,000 people in the next two years. MACMILLAN BLOEDEL LTD., Vancouver, British Columbia, the forest products concern, said it would build a $154 million medium-density fiberboard plant near Pembroke, Ontario, in a joint venture with Fidev Corp.

title: Times Ads Available Over America Online
body: Beginning today, the three largest Sunday classified advertising sections of The newyork Times will be available through the week to subscribers of the America Online computer service. The new service is accessible from the main screen of @times, The Times's on-line service, and includes the help wanted, real estate and automotive advertisements from tomorrow's newspaper. Several newspapers, including The Chicago Tribune and The San Jose Mercury News in California, already offer classified advertising on line. But Steve Rago, director of The newyork Times Company's new media unit, said the new @times service "should be faster and easier to use, because it exploits new software tools." He said subscribers would be able to narrow their searches of classified advertising to particular automotive makes and models, for example, or to real estate listings in particular towns. The Sunday classified advertisements will be posted on America Online for a test period of about six months at no additional charge to advertisers or on-line subscribers.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
A SECOND 2-FOR-1 STOCK SPLIT FOR AMERICA ONLINE
body: America Online Inc. will split its shares 2 for 1 on April 13, the second such split in six months. America Online, a provider of on-line computer services based in Vienna, Va., said yesterday there would be about 35 million shares outstanding after the split. In November, the company had another 2-for-1 split. Since early that month, its shares have more than doubled, from $34.625. The shares were up $2.50 yesterday, at $76.75, in Nasdaq trading of more than 1.2 million shares. America Online provides electronic mail, news, software and chat lines to more than two million customers.

title: America Online Adds Clients
body: America Online Inc. said yesterday that it had surpassed two million subscribers, and it asserted that it had overtaken both Compuserve and Prodigy to become the largest consumer information service in the unitedstates. America Online, based in Vienna, Va., said it had added 500,000 members since December. But the growth has come at the cost of deteriorating service, many subscribers have complained. Busy signals, slow connections and electronic mail delays of several hours, or in some cases days, are increasingly common. In some cases, electronic mail "is zapped into never-never land," said Mary Modahl, an analyst with Forrester Research Inc. of Cambridge, Mass. "The degradation of their service is remarkable. They haven't been able to keep up with demand." Steve Case, America Online's president and chief executive, acknowledged the problems in a letter to subscribers earlier this month, noting that the service was struggling to handle 1.5 million electronic mail messages a day. America Online's rivals shopped short of disputing the assertion by the company that it was now the largest domestic on-line service.

title: America Online Deal
body: America Online Inc. said last week that it had completed its $35 million acquisition of Advanced Network and Services Inc., an Elmsford, N.Y., company that built much of the Internet global computer network. The purchase was made with $20 million in cash and $15 million in stock, which amounts to 258,065 America Online shares.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
COMPUSERVE PLANS TO OFFER WIDER INTERNET ACCESS
body: Compuserve Inc. said yesterday that it was within 60 days of offering the World Wide Web and other Internet services to some of its 2.6 million on-line information service customers. The company, a division of H & R Block that is based in Columbus, Ohio, will make the Internet services available to computer users with "dial P.P.P." Internet connections. Such connections are typically more complex than those made to standard commercial information services and are usually made through companies called Internet service providers. Only a relatively small number of Compuserve's customers are thought to have dial-P.P.P. connections.

title: America Online Acquisitions
body: America Online Inc., the fast-growing computer on-line service, said today that it had acquired Booklink Technologies Inc. and Navisoft Inc. in tax-free stock deals valued at $47.7 million. Booklink, based in Needham, Mass., makes worldwide web browsers, which are tools used to search bulletin boards on the Internet, the global web of computer networks. Navisoft, based in Hillsboro, Calif., makes tools for publishing on the Internet. America Online, based here, said the acquisitions were expected to strengthen its strategic initiative of popularizing the Internet for publishers as well as consumers.

title: U.P.I. Talks With AT&T
body: United Press International, the privately held news wire service, said it was in talks with the AT&T Corporation to form a venture, possibly to provide on-line information services. A joint venture would further enhance AT&T's push into the $6 billion on-line services market. AT&T officials refused to comment. AT&T, the largest long-distance phone company, bought the on-line business of the Ziff Communications Company last week. Ziff's Interchange Network is being tested and is expected to be started in 1995. MCI Communications, the No. 2 long-distance provider, and the Ameritech Corporation, the Chicago-based Bell operating company, also have talked to U.P.I. about a joint venture, said Ron MacIntyre, U.P.I.'s vice president for marketing. The wire service filed for bankruptcy reorganization in 1992. The Middle East Broadcasting Company then bought U.P.I. that year for $3.9 million. Middle East is owned primarily by the Saudi banker Saleh Kamel and Walid Ibrahim, brother-in-law of King Fahd of Saudi Arabia.

title: America Online
body: Shares of America Online Inc., a fast-growing on-line service, rose sharply yesterday after it said that it expected to more than double its number of customers. The company expects to have 3 million subscribers a year from now, up from about 1.4 million. Graphic   Graph: "America Online" shows daily closing stock prices for America Online from Nov. 21st to Dec. 6th. (Source: Datastream)

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
A NAME CHANGE IS PLANNED FOR MEAD DATA CENTRAL
body: The new owner of Mead Data Central plans to change the company's name to Lexis-Nexis, making reference to the names of its on-line database products. Reed Elsevier P.L.C. is expected to make the change when it completes the acquisition of the electronic legal information and news retrieval company. Reed, an British-Dutch publishing company, said on Oct. 4 it would pay $1.5 billion to the Mead Corporation of Dayton, Ohio, for the data unit. The companies hope to complete the deal by the end of the year. Lexis offers on-line legal information, and Nexis offers electronic retrieval of text from a wide range of newspapers and magazines. It had sales of $551 million in 1993.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE STOCK UP AGAIN ON ACQUISITION PLAN
body: Shares of America Online Inc., the computer on-line services provider based in Vienna, Va., rose again yesterday after it said on Monday that it planned to buy Advanced Network and Services, a major architect of the Internet. The acquisition is part of America Online's strategy to expand its access to the Internet, the global web of computer networks. The stock rose $2.875 yesterday, to $43.75, on Nasdaq. On Monday, the shares gained $4.125.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE APPROVES 2-FOR-1 STOCK SPLIT
body: America Online Inc. said yesterday that its board had approved a 2-for-1 stock split, payable on Nov. 24. The split is part of the company's plan to keep its shares affordable to potential investors, said Stephen Case, America Online president and chief executive. The split, payable to shareholders of record as of Nov. 10, will double the company's shares outstanding to about 16 million, the company said. America Online provides electronic mail, chat lines, software and news to customers through their modem-equipped personal computers. The shares closed down 37.5 cents, at $68.375, in Nasdaq trading after rising as much as $3.75 earlier in the day.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AN EARLY INVESTOR IN AMERICA ONLINE SELLS HIS STAKE
body: A prominent investor in America Online Inc., Paul Allen, sold his remaining stake in the company yesterday. "A key criterion of Mr. Allen is to work with companies that can contribute technologically to his other companies," said Susan Pierson, Mr. Allen's spokeswoman at Vulcan Northwest Inc., his investment vehicle. "The synergy hoped for wasn't realized with America Online." Mr. Allen's initial investment of about $30 million grew to about $130 million earlier this year. America Online, based in Vienna, Va., is the country's third-largest on-line service, providing electronic mail, news, software and access to chat lines to customers through modem-equipped personal computers. Mr. Allen, a co-founder of the Microsoft Corporation, was an early investor in America Online when the company went public in the spring of 1992 and at one point tried to buy it.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
TOP AMERICA ONLINE INVESTOR SELLS HALF OF STAKE
body: America Online Inc.'s most prominent investor, Paul Allen, has sold 733,000 shares, or more than half his stake in the company, his spokeswoman said. "It was a good time to realize some profits," said Susan Pierson, Mr. Allen's spokeswoman. She would not say whether Mr. Allen planned to sell any more shares. Before yesterday, Mr. Allen, a co-founder of the Microsoft Corporation with his high school friend William Gates, owned about 18 percent of the common shares of America Online, which provides news, electronic mail services and entertainment to its customers through modem-equipped personal computers. The large share sale apparently spooked investors. Shares of America Online fell $5 yesterday, to $55.625, on trading of 2.2 million shares. Mr. Allen now owns 698,000 shares, or about 9 percent of the shares outstanding.

title:
THE MEDIA BUSINESS;
Times Begins On-Line News
body: The newyork Times Company and America Online started a service yesterday to give computer users access to an electronic data base of articles and information from The newyork Times. People who subscribe to the service, which is called "@times," will have access through their computers to the main news articles of the day from The newyork Times News Service. But the two companies said the main feature of the service would be an entertainment guide that included a range of reviews and articles on cultural as well as arts and leisure activities in the newyork region. It will include information about the theater, movies, books, restaurants, art exhibitions, music performances and sports events as well as an archive of reviews from The Times. The service is interactive, meaning subscribers to the service can post messages to electronic bulletin boards to discuss a variety of topics. In the future, the companies said, users will be able to hold discussions through the service with some writers at The Times. Information about subscribing to the service, which is available seven days a week, can be obtained from America Online at (800) 827-6364.

title: Corrections
body: An article in Business Day on Saturday about on-line information services misstated the ownership of Dialog Information Services. It is owned solely by Knight-Ridder Inc. The News Corporation, headed by Rupert Murdoch, owns the Delphi Internet Services Corporation.

title: Internet Commercials Are O.K., but Be Polite
body: To the Editor: The problem with Laurence Canter's advertisement over the Internet (Business Day, April 19) was not that he used the Internet for commercial purposes. Commercial usage is legal. The real problem is that he posted his message to thousands of news groups unrelated to the topic. I teach an introduction to Internet for faculty and staff at Swarthmore College; one thing we discuss is Netiquette: using the Internet politely. That means choosing a news group designed for the type of information you intend to post. Mr. Canter bombarded Internet users with the same message in every conceivable news group. That's the electronic equivalent of ambulance-chasing, and it is rude and destructive.  ANDREW J. PERRIN Philadelphia, April 19, 1994

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
SHARES OF AMERICA ONLINE RISE AFTER VALUE ESTIMATE
body: Shares of America Online Inc. closed at an all-time high yesterday after a Chicago Corporation analyst, Rick Martin, said the company's shares could be worth as much as $200 in a takeover. Stock of the on-line computer data base company closed up $8.75, or almost 11 percent, at $91.50, on Nasdaq volume of one million shares. In his report, Mr. Martin said the "minimum takeover value is probably $160, with $200-plus a real possibility." The analyst said that a near-term takeover was unlikely but that he believed America Online, based in Vienna, Va., "will eventually be bought by a major cable or telephone company."

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
APPLE HAS A WARRANT FOR 6.6% OF AMERICA ONLINE
body: Apple Computer Inc. said yesterday that it held a warrant to buy a 6.6 percent stake in America Online Inc., a fast-growing on-line computer service whose stock price has been climbing rapidly. Shares of American Online moved up another $3 yesterday, closing at $73.50 in Nasdaq trading. Apple slipped 75 cents, to $35.75. In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Apple said it had acquired the warrant in connection with a master software and license agreement with America Online signed on Dec. 3, 1992. Apple said it was holding the warrant, for 500,000 shares, for investment purposes.

title:
COMPANY NEWS;
AMERICA ONLINE STOCK ADVANCES BY 14%
body: America Online Inc. shares rose $7.50, or 14 percent, yesterday after the company told Wall Street analysts that computer users were subscribing to the online service faster than was anticipated. The Vienna, Va., company said that at current growth rates, it will have a million subscribers by October instead of December, when analysts had expected the milestone. Currently, America Online has about 600,000 subscribers. The stock closed at $60.75 in Nasdaq trading. America Online provides news, electronic mail services, chat lines and software to subscribers through modem-equipped personal computers.

title: Microsoft Undercut in Effort To Depict Rival as Thriving
body: Trying to defang the Government's antitrust charges against it, the Microsoft Corporation introduced a host of evidence this week to show that the Netscape browser was still healthy and thriving, despite Microsoft's all-out assault on the browser market. But in a single stroke this afternoon, a Government lawyer undercut Microsoft's strategy by producing a Microsoft email written in January suggesting that the company had cynically and selectively produced data to support this point of view. In the email, Greg Shaw, a Microsoft public relations executive, asked others at the company: "What data can we find right away, showing that the Netscape browser is still healthy? The Government is introducing a bunch of data showing Netscape headed down big time and Microsoft way up." The Netscape Communications Corporation's browser held a commanding lead until Microsoft entered the market with a browser, Internet Explorer, that was tied to the Windows operating system and set out on a campaign to dissuade other companies to work with Netscape. The Government's antitrust case is built on the contention that Microsoft used its dominance in operating systems to bolster its share of the browser market illegally. "It would help if you could send me some reports showing their market share healthy and holding," Mr. Shaw added. Later that morning, Robert Bennett, group product manager for Windows, wrote back, saying, "All the analyses have pretty much come to the same conclusion, which is that Netscape is declining and Internet Explorer is gaining." A half-hour later, Yusef Mehdi, director of Windows marketing, weighed in, saying that he had found one survey showing "us very close on Internet Explorer share" and another that "has Netscape even or even higher." "This is for the trial," Mr. Mehdi added, "so let's provide the more negative analysts." As David Boies, the lead Government lawyer, read that aloud, Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson, who is trying the case without a jury, chuckled and shook his head, while Microsoft's lawyers looked grim. And when Mr. Boies asked the witness, Franklin Fisher, an economist from Massachusetts Institute of Technology, what he thought this said about his analysis of Microsoft's take on the browser war, Mr. Fisher said only: "This document speaks for itself rather louder than most." In questioning the witness again a short time later, a Microsoft lawyer, Michael Lacovara, heatedly asserted that all the Microsoft executives involved in the email exchange were "marketing and public relations personnel" and that the exchange was "a discussion of trial public relations," not of legal issues. In fact, at one point, Mr. Shaw wrote that the request for market data "is for press purposes." But it was not the first time Microsoft had been shown to gin up surveys or statistics that would indicate support for the company's view. In January, Mr. Boies offered as evidence an email message in which William H. Gates, the chairman of Microsoft, wrote, "It would help me immensely to have a survey showing that 90 percent of developers believe that putting the browser into the operating system makes sense." Later, he added, "Ideally we would have a survey before I appear at the Senate on March 3d." In subsequent email messages, Microsoft employees laid out how they would phrase the survey questions to be sure they elicited the responses Mr. Gates wanted. Earlier today, Mr. Boies also seemed to take some of the sting out of Microsoft's attack Thursday evening on a previous Government witness, James Barksdale, who was chairman of Netscape. In court last October, Mr. Barksdale asserted that because of what he described as Microsoft's predatory conduct, Netscape could no longer get computer makers to provide the Netscape browser with their products. "That's over half the distribution channel, and we're basically out of it," he said. But an internal document prepared for America Online at the same time, as part of that company's research for its purchase of Netscape, showed that just over one-fifth of the nation's computer manufacturers were shipping Netscape at the time. As a result, Mr. Lacovara asserted that Mr. Barksdale's credibility had been thrown into question, and Judge Jackson expressed interest in that. Today, Mr. Boies pointed to several passages in Mr. Barksdale's direct written testimony in which he listed all the companies that were shipping Netscape on at least some of their computers and explained precisely what the arrangements allowed. All this detailed information, Mr. Boies and Mr. Fisher both said, showed that Mr. Barksdale was not trying to overstate the depth of Netscape's problem. Judge Jackson did not remark on this development. http://www.nytimes.com

title: In Spanish and Portuguese, Web Growth Spurt
body: IN January, Anna Spinello, a clothing designer in Buenos Aires, set up a Web site to help boost sales of her spring line. By clicking on a little flag, a viewer can see the site in English, Spanish or Portuguese. "Considering we haven't publicized it, we've had an amazing response," said her son Francesco Spinello, 42, who manages the small, family-run business (www.annaspinello.com) that sells to boutiques in Argentina, Chile, Uruguay and Brazil. "We've made a lot of contacts that should pay off with the next collection." The Spinellos are part of a wave of Latin Americans who have recently discovered the Web. Lagging perhaps two years behind the unitedstates, Japan and Western Europe in its development, the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking Internet market is one of the fastest-growing in the world and has emerged as the latest battleground for viewers among such Internet titans as America Online and Yahoo. "This is the year the scales are tipping," said Heather Killen, the vice president of Yahoo International, who oversaw the start-up of a Spanish version of the Yahoo portal (espanol.yahoo.com) in June 1998. "The shape of the Internet is no longer a comet with the U.S. as the head and this thin trail behind." Latin American governments, aware of the need to promote local Internet access and business so that more precious dollars do not flow overseas, are also beginning to look at ways to encourage more people to get on line. The governments of Argentina and Chile, for example, have mandated that privately held phone companies charge half price for local Internet access phone calls. Recent privatization of the state-run phone company in Brazil, which is the only Portuguese-speaking country in Latin America, is expected to lead to reduced phone charges and better infrastructure and service in that country, the most populous in the region, accounting for roughly half the Internet users.
